The journey ends beneath Orgrimmar in the Cleft of Shadow, where warlocks, rogues, and demon-binders work out of sight. Shenthul, a Shattered Hand trainer, awaits there. The gruff troll judges the newly arrived undead agent with harsh skepticism. Reputation alone will not satisfy him; he wants to see whether the envoy has real cunning or has wasted the voyage across the Great Sea.

quest:2379.text: Zando'zan. In Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow, promising rogues begin training with the Shattered Hand. Trainer Shenthul sends his chosen initiate to meet Zando'zan and enter the Horde's covert ranks. Orgrimmar's rulers know brute strength cannot win every war. Beneath the city, the Cleft of Shadow houses the Shattered Hand, a covert guild that handles espionage, sabotage, and theft for the Horde. When rogue trainer Shenthul sees promise in an initiate, he sends them to report to Zando'zan for dedicated operative training. Zando'zan does not grant respect to every inexperienced rogue who enters the cavern. Meeting him marks a formal initiation into the finer clandestine arts, beginning with stealth, subterfuge, and thievery. His training bridges the distance between rough street cutpurses and organized intelligence operatives, preparing rogues for fieldwork beyond the safety of the capital's red canyon walls.

quest:2380.text: To Orgrimmar!. Kaplak sends a young rogue from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar. There, you are to find Shenthul in the Cleft of Shadow and enter the Shattered Hand's network. Kaplak sends you north from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar. Your budding skills have caught the notice of more prominent handlers, though they remain unpolished. The red crags of Durotar are behind you as you make for the capital.

quest:2381.text: Plundering the Plunderers. Wrenix the Wretched sends new Shattered Hand rogues against the Southsea Freebooters near Ratchet. Aboard the Tide Razor, they face pirates, locked strongboxes, and a dangerous guardian before claiming the Southsea Treasure. Wrenix the Wretched, a goblin contact in Ratchet, tests aspiring Shattered Hand operatives. He sends rogues south along the Barrens coast to a cove where the Tide Razor lies at anchor, crewed by Southsea Freebooters. They must board without being seen, enter the pirates’ den where cutpurses train, pick the strongboxes in the hold, and bring back the plunder.

quest:2382.text: Wrenix of Ratchet. In Orgrimmar, Wrenix of Ratchet draws Horde rogues toward a goblin port far to the south. Zando'zan sends them to aid Wrenix the Wretched, a disreputable goblin in Ratchet. In Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow, the rogue guild works out of winding crevices, largely unseen. Zando'zan, a troll who speaks in wild ramblings, greets operatives with ominous portents. His visions include Warchief Thrall struck down by poison and blade. He gives no explanation for the prophecy, and quickly sends agents south to the port town of Ratchet in the Barrens. Ratchet lies on the Barrens coast, east of the Crossroads. Scoundrels, mercenaries, and tinkerers gather in the neutral port, where Wrenix the Wretched makes his home. Wrenix has little patience for Zando'zan's eccentric ways. He says the troll's earlier recruits met grim ends in the bay, among its hungry predators.

quest:239.text: Westbrook Garrison Needs Help!. Marshal Dughan sends available adventurers west to Westbrook Garrison, the outpost at Elwynn Forest's border with Westfall. Stormwind's army is stretched thin across the kingdom, while Deputy Rainer and his guards face growing pressure from Riverpaw gnolls and wandering thieves without regular reinforcements. Westbrook Garrison guards the western edge of Elwynn Forest, where settled woodland meets Westfall's troubled plains. Gnoll warbands and bandits grow bolder along the waterways and western roads, and the small garrison has asked for more men. Marshal Dughan and Goldshire's administration have no Stormwind soldiers to spare. Local commanders must hire traveling mercenaries and wandering adventurers. Deputy Rainer and his men face the Riverpaw gnolls, whose raiding parties harass travelers and nearby homesteads. The pack operates in the borderlands between Elwynn and Westfall. With Stormwind distracted by political and military troubles, the gnolls press deeper into inhabited territory. Westbrook Garrison guards against their unchecked advance into the heart of the forest.

quest:2399.text: The Sprouted Fronds. At Denalan's garden by Lake Al'Ameth, the planted frond has taken root and sprouted. Travelers can see the new growth among the garden beds. You find Denalan's garden near Lake Al'Ameth, where the botanist studies Teldrassil's peculiar plants. After a shimmering frond is planted, new fronds rise from the soil in his planter, ready to be gathered and examined. Teldrassil is young and vast, and its plant life grows quickly. Night elf herbalists find that growth fascinating and troubling. The shimmering fronds and their offshoots show how quickly life takes hold on the World Tree's boughs, though its vitality can be hard to predict.

quest:2438.text: The Emerald Dreamcatcher. In Dolanaar, Tallonkai Swiftroot asks you to recover a cherished heirloom from his abandoned home in Starbreeze Village. Gaerolas Talvethren, the druid warden, gave him the Emerald Dreamcatcher, which he left behind when corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs overran the settlement. Recovering it keeps its gentle nature magic from falling into foul hands. Gaerolas Talvethren gave Tallonkai a rare druidic talisman. The warden watches over the sleeping druids within Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Crafted to channel the serene currents of the Emerald Dream, the amulet draws on that pure spiritual energy to bring peace and fortune to its bearer. Such gifts go only to a trusted few whose lives are bound to the forest's care. Starbreeze Village was peaceful until the Gnarlpine furbolgs succumbed to violent madness. They drove the villagers from their ancestral homes. During the fearful flight, Tallonkai left his most treasured possession hidden inside his dresser in the village's southeastern quarter. He could not reclaim it on his own.

quest:2459.text: Ferocitas the Dream Eater. Tallonkai Swiftroot in Dolanaar sends you after a stolen emerald in northern Teldrassil. The jewel was pried from his damaged heirloom dreamcatcher by Gnarlpine furbolgs north of Starbreeze Village, and now hangs from their leader, Ferocitas the Dream Eater. Tallonkai Swiftroot felt relief when the dreamcatcher recovered from the corrupted wilds came back to him, then dismay at its ruined state. The sacred artifact had been vandalized, its emerald centerpiece pried from the woven frame. Night elves spoke of Gnarlpine mystics north of Starbreeze Village, fallen under the influence of a furbolg leader named Ferocitas the Dream Eater. He wore a brilliant green stone around his neck. In Ferocitas's clutches, the sacred gem was useless and perverse, so Tallonkai sent defenders to take it back. The Gnarlpine furbolgs in Teldrassil's northern reaches were once peaceful neighbors. Corruption seeping into the World Tree drove them into frenzy and madness. Their mystics once practiced harmonious nature rites, but began drawing on distorted magical energies. Travelers can track down Ferocitas by cutting through the mystics guarding his woodland enclave. The jewel can then be returned to Tallonkai, so his dreamcatcher may be made whole and balance restored to the woods.

quest:2498.text: Return to Denalan. At Lake Al'Ameth, Return to Denalan carries Rellian's alarming news to the botanist studying corruption in Teldrassil. After examining the mossy tumors on timberlings, you head south to help Denalan with his discovery. Rellian Greenspyre studies the mossy tumors afflicting Teldrassil's timberlings when urgent word arrives from his colleague Denalan. At his camp beside Lake Al'Ameth, Denalan has finally isolated the cause of these unnatural growths on the forest's nature spirits. Rellian recognizes the gravity of this discovery and sends you south at once to lend a hand.

quest:2499.text: Oakenscowl. Along Lake Al'Ameth, blight spreads from a corrupted timberling called Oakenscowl. Denalan asks you to end the threat. The maddened creature dwells in a cave on the lake's southern bank. Timberlings tend the boughs of Teldrassil, and Oakenscowl once led them. Now corruption runs through the world tree, reaching humble wildlife and ancient protectors alike. A massive growth swells across Oakenscowl's bark, driving the timberling mad. Where it once guarded the forest, blight now takes hold. Oakenscowl hides in a cavern on Lake Al'Ameth's southern shore. Its presence poisons the nearby water and woodland beasts. Denalan cannot face the creature alone, so he seeks its destruction to cut off the corruption and study the strange growth afflicting the lake's spirits.

quest:2518.text: Tears of the Moon. At the Temple of the Moon, Priestess A'moora mourns Lady Sathrah's madness. Once cherished by Elune, the great spider has become dangerous, and the Sisterhood seeks to end her suffering and recover her sacred spinnerets. In Darnassus's Temple of the Moon, Priestess A'moora grieves for Lady Sathrah. Sathrah was once blessed by Elune. Beneath the night sky, she wove delicate silver webs that caught the evening mist on Teldrassil's boughs. The Sisterhood of Elune gathered and kept the shimmering dew from those webs, which held healing powers for their sacred ministrations.

quest:2519.text: The Temple of the Moon. In Darnassus, Sister Aquinne calls for aid to a suffering ancient creature in Teldrassil. The Sisterhood of Elune needs help, and this is the opening call to a solemn ritual of mercy. Sister Aquinne asks for help in the Temple Gardens. As a devoted servant of Elune, she speaks for her order: a venerable forest creature is suffering, and the Sisters cannot attend to it alone. Sister Aquinne sends you southeast to the Temple of the Moon. Priestess A'moora coordinates the rituals and practical duties needed to address Teldrassil's troubled wildlife, preparing allies to carry out a sorrowful act of mercy.

quest:2520.text: Sathrah's Sacrifice. At the Temple of the Moon, Sathrah's Sacrifice gives a fallen creature's spirit a final rite. You carry Lady Sathrah's spinnerets to Elune's sacred waters, where the Priesthood seeks to cleanse her soul of corruption. Priestess A'moora asks you to perform a final rite after Lady Sathrah is slain. The great spider fell to the dark madness spreading across Teldrassil, which twisted her peaceful nature into mindless aggression. The Priesthood of Elune seeks to redeem her fallen essence, not treat her death as a simple culling. You place her silvery spinnerets in the fountain at the heart of the Temple of the Moon. Its consecrated waters wash away the corruption and grant her release.

quest:2541.text: The Sleeping Druid. Oben Rageclaw lies asleep in Ban'ethil Barrow Den, but his spirit is caught in the Emerald Dream. Gnarlpine shamans have drawn it from his body and set his flesh moving through the den. Night elf druids sleep in barrow dens across Kalimdor while their spirits wander the Emerald Dream. Their bodies rest in stone alcoves, safe through centuries of slumber. Teldrassil's corruption has driven the Gnarlpine furbolgs to desperate savagery. In Ban'ethil Barrow Den, Gnarlpine shamans found a way to breach Oben Rageclaw's sacred rest and draw his living spirit from his sleeping body.

quest:2561.text: Druid of the Claw. Oben Rageclaw’s spirit waits in the barrows beneath Teldrassil, unable to rest. The Gnarlpine furbolgs have bound his body with a dark enchantment, and you can break that bond by destroying his soulless shell. Oben Rageclaw was resting in the barrows beneath Teldrassil when the corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs laid a voodoo enchantment over his sleeping body. The magic tore his spirit from his mortal flesh and trapped it in the Emerald Dream. Now his spirit lingers nearby, unable to rest or reclaim his body.

quest:26.text: A Lesson to Learn. Mathrengyl Bearwalker sends young druids from Darnassus to Moonglade to learn the ways of water. There, they meet an elder of the Cenarion Circle and begin training in their aquatic aspect. Mathrengyl Bearwalker guides young night elf druids as they practice among Darnassus’s boughs. When an initiate shows a firm bond with nature and readiness for greater responsibility, Mathrengyl sends them toward mastery of the waters. Cenarius’s gifts demand focus, and learning to cross the depths without drowning calls for guidance from the Cenarion Circle’s elders. The initiate leaves Darnassus for Moonglade, an ancient sanctuary beneath Mount Hyjal. In Nighthaven, Dendrite Starblaze waits as an elder mentor of the Cenarion Circle. Starblaze judges whether young shapeshifters are ready for the trials that lead to aquatic form. Mastering water takes both physical resilience and mental resolve.

quest:2751.text: Barbaric Battlements. In Orgrimmar, Orokk Omosh seeks someone to carry on his family's forge craft. With no heirs, he asks an aspiring smith to prove a sure hand with bronze before sharing his knowledge. Orokk Omosh works the anvils of Orgrimmar under the weight of his family's past. For twenty generations, the Omosh line has shaped ore into weapons and armor for the Horde. Orokk has no kin and cannot sire children, and he sees himself as a failure to that line. With the family craft at risk of ending, he sets bloodline pride aside and seeks an apprentice to carry its smithing traditions forward. Orokk will not share his secrets with an untested smith. He asks for two patterned bronze bracers, two bronze greatswords, and two sharp beast claws as proof of basic skill at the anvil. To him, blacksmithing is no idle luxury: its highest honor is armor and steel stained with enemy blood. Meeting his demands may persuade the old smith that the Omosh legacy can live on through an apprentice, and earn a chance to learn more of the craft.

quest:2753.text: Trampled Under Foot. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Orokk Omosh puts smiths through an advanced blacksmithing trial. Forging green iron armor tests their endurance and teaches them to make heavy iron boots, with the Omosh bloodline's secret techniques at stake. Orokk Omosh trains armorsmiths in Orgrimmar through hard physical trials. He sees metalworking as more than heating ore and shaping it; the work honors his ancestral clan and tests a smith's endurance. This is the third trial in his chain, and repeated crafting of tempered green iron armor is meant to build muscle and discipline. Smiths who bring Orokk the requested green iron gear earn rare praise from the gruff armorsmith. He compares an artisan who endures the work to his grandfather, Chief Gorokk of Omosh. In exchange for the armor, Orokk teaches the ancestral design for sturdy iron boots, made so Horde warriors can crush their enemies beneath their heels.

quest:2755.text: Joys of Omosh. After an adventurer's great help, Orokk Omosh shares a family tradition in Orgrimmar. The veteran blacksmith brushes off his tears as soot, then performs the Omosh dance of joy to pass down an unusual piece of family heritage. Near Orgrimmar's scorching forge, Orokk Omosh is known for heavy hammer blows, not tears. The burly blacksmith has received great help from you, and the kindness overwhelms him. He stubbornly blames a stray bit of soot in his eye rather than admit he is weeping. Before you part, Orokk says he must share one last secret of the Omosh family. He performs the vigorous, exhausting Omosh dance of joy for his apprentice, then teaches the apprentice to strike with an iron fist.

quest:2950.text: Nogg's Ring Redo. In Orgrimmar, Nogg works to improve a ring recovered from Gnomeregan. He asks for rare materials and information about Dark Iron dwarves, eager to prove goblin craft superior to gnomish design. You bring a cleaned gold ring from Gnomeregan to Nogg's workshop in the Valley of Honor. The goblin engineer takes one look at its modest gnomish craft and offers a bargain. Bring raw materials and a modest fee, and he will add an intricate lattice of silver and moss agate to the band, meant to amplify the magic within it.

quest:2998.text: Tome of Divinity. A summons bearing the Tome of Divinity calls promising paladins from Elwynn to Stormwind. Answering Brother Wilhelm's call begins the sacred trials needed to master resurrection through the Holy Light. Novice paladins in Elwynn Forest spend their early days helping locals and testing their strength against wolves, Defias bandits, and kobolds. When an initiate shows martial discipline and devotion to the Holy Light, mentors such as Brother Wilhelm send a personal summons. Leaders of the paladins take note of promising students and direct them to leave the local chapels behind and report straight to the kingdom's spiritual heart. In Cathedral Square, Stormwind's Cathedral of Light is the supreme sanctuary of the kingdom's priesthood and the Knights of the Silver Hand. Duthorian Rall resides there and oversees those sworn to the Order. Beneath its soaring vaulted ceilings, high-ranking paladins set formal trials from the Tome of Divinity before each initiate. The challenges test compassion, fortitude, and a willingness to sacrifice.

quest:3065.text: Simple Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, a marked parchment sends you to Frang after you prove yourself against local beasts. The warrior trainer waits outside the Den. After you prove you can face the Mottled Boars, Gornek hands you a parchment marked specifically for you. Durotar is harsh, and the Horde quickly gives its fighters guidance. The parchment directs you to Frang, the veteran warrior trainer outside the Den. Frang shelters in the shade outside the Den and watches recruits arrive from the red scrubland. With a seasoned eye, he judges each new arrival before teaching the fundamentals, whether with a heavy axe or a spear. He prepares each recruit to defend the young Horde's fragile settlements.

quest:3082.text: Etched Tablet. Gornek sends a carved tablet to hunters in the Valley of Trials. It bears Jen'shan's mark and calls them to begin training in the wilderness. Gornek brings novice hunters a carved tablet after they prove themselves against the boars near the Den. The stone bears Jen'shan's mark. She is a skilled troll huntswoman stationed nearby, and the message shows that seasoned hunters have noticed the young recruit's grit. The lesson now moves beyond surviving the local dangers and toward disciplined training in the wild. Jen'shan teaches that orcs and trolls have a long history within the Horde. Orcs brought renowned traditions of warriors and shamans, while the Darkspear trolls carried ancient skills in stalking, tracking, and survival. Those skills helped the orcs endure life on Azeroth. As Jen'shan trains new hunters, the two peoples continue to share what they know, bound by respect for the hunt.

quest:3083.text: Encrypted Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, Gornek gives a coded summons to aspiring rogues. It sends them to Rwag in the Den, where rogue instruction meets the Shattered Hand. Gornek gives an Encrypted Tablet to each initiate who proves their mettle against the local wildlife. Its message is written in cipher, a fitting test and precaution for those trained in stealth, poison, and subterfuge. The summons directs the recruit into the Den to meet Rwag, who trains the Horde’s rogues, thieves, and cutpurses. Inside the Den, initiates find Rwag, an agent aligned with the Shattered Hand. He tells new rogues the guild will not dictate their every breath, but the Hand holds him accountable if an apprentice fails to perform. The fledgling Horde is surrounded by foes and relies heavily on silent scouts and agile cutpurses to gather intelligence and eliminate threats from the shadows.

quest:3084.text: Rune-Inscribed Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, new shamans receive a summons from Shikrik. It calls promising initiates to formal training in the spirits and the elements: earth, fire, water, and air. Gornek gives fledgling shamans a carved stone tablet after they prove their early discipline in the dusty training grounds of the Valley of Trials. Its runes carry an invitation from Shikrik, the local shaman trainer. The summons tells each initiate they are ready to look beyond physical combat and heed the deeper currents of the natural world. Shamanism holds a sacred place in the revitalized Horde. Shikrik teaches that shamans draw power from the four elements and strength from ancestral spirits. They follow Warchief Thrall's example as spiritual guides and sources of wisdom for their communities. Across Durotar, they protect the settlements taking root.

quest:3085.text: Hallowed Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, a message from Ken'jai reaches young priests after their first test. The tablet calls them to learn how Darkspear priests commune with the spirits. After you prove yourself against the boars under Gornek's watch, he gives you an inscribed stone called the Hallowed Tablet. Its message bears Ken'jai's mark. The Darkspear mystic waits outside the Den, where he watches over newcomers drawn to faith and spiritual magic. Darkspear priests among the Horde seek communion with spirits and loa, unlike human and dwarven priests who follow the Holy Light across the sea. Ken'jai welcomes you to Durotar and teaches that your power grows through spiritual discipline. He will instruct you in greater rites as your bond with the spirits matures.

quest:3086.text: Glyphic Tablet. In the Valley of Trials, a Glyphic Tablet sends young Horde mages to Mai'ah. Gornek passes it to them after they prove their strength, and the troll trainer waits outside the Den. You have proved your strength against the Valley of Trials' wildlife, and Gornek gives you an inscribed tablet. Mai'ah, the valley's mage trainer, sent it. She asks you to find her by the Den's entrance when you are ready to begin your arcane studies. Mai'ah speaks plainly about the power mages wield and the danger that comes with it. She warns that their greatest threat is magic's unseen pull toward corruption, not rival warriors or enemy races. Humility and patience matter, she says, because unchecked sorcery can make a mage believe they have mastered more than they have.

quest:3087.text: Etched Parchment. In the Valley of Trials, Etched Parchment calls a young hunter to Jen'shan. Gornek delivers it after the initiate's first blooding, opening the way to wilderness training in Durotar. After proving themselves against mottled boars, hunters in the Valley of Trials receive an etched parchment from Gornek. Jen'shan, a skilled Darkspear hunter, sent the note after watching new arrivals from the edges of the encampment. It welcomes the initiate to formal training and recognizes the instincts needed to master Durotar's untamed beasts and harsh land. Reporting to Jen'shan marks the move from recruit to dedicated stalker. She warns that hunting is no easier than the arcane arts or ancestral shamanism. Mastering Durotar's predators, maintaining ranged weapons, and surviving on unforgiving land all demand discipline. Jen'shan sends her apprentices to aid the valley's other inhabitants and test their abilities before returning to learn more advanced survival techniques.

quest:3088.text: Encrypted Parchment. In the Valley of Trials, Encrypted Parchment sends proven novice orc rogues into the Den. Its cipher points them to Rwag, an agent of the Shattered Hand. Gornek passes the coded parchment to novice orcs who have proved themselves against the local wildlife. Other trainers recruit pupils openly in the clearing, but rogue instructor Rwag sends his summons by cipher. The message directs you beyond the sunlit camp and deep into the cavern called the Den. Inside the Den, you find Rwag keeping watch among the rock. Warlocks lurk deeper in the cave, and he tells you he watches recruits for the Shattered Hand. While orcish society prizes open honor and glory in battle, the Shattered Hand works as the Horde's hidden network of spies, cutthroats, and gatherers of intelligence.

quest:3089.text: Rune-Inscribed Parchment. At the Valley of Trials, a rune-marked summons calls new shamans to Shikrik. Gornek delivers the parchment, which begins their formal training in communion with spirits and elements. After proving their survival skills against local wildlife, new orc shamans receive a rune-inscribed parchment from Gornek, overseer of the Valley of Trials. Its mystical writing comes from Shikrik, the valley's shaman trainer, who asks to meet the newly arrived initiate. Meeting Shikrik begins a shaman's sacred duty to the Horde. She teaches that shamans serve as conduits for ancestral spirits and wielders of elemental wrath. Under her guidance, new shamans learn to channel spiritual energies, mend wounds, and call upon Kalimdor's natural forces.

quest:3104.text: Glyphic Letter. A sealed summons reaches novice human mages in Northshire Valley, sent by Marshal McBride. Khelden Bremen calls promising spellcasters to Northshire Abbey to begin their arcane tutelage. Marshal McBride gives the rune-marked letter to an aspiring apprentice who has proved capable by helping him against local vermin. Khelden Bremen, Northshire's resident mage trainer, wrote it. He watches new recruits arriving at the abbey for signs of magical discipline and talent. Northshire Abbey has long been a sanctuary of the Holy Light, but Stormwind's dangers call for practitioners of every discipline. The letter brings you upstairs to Khelden Bremen. He offers no easy praise. Instead, he warns that mastering arcane power means defying natural limits, earning both profound respect and deep fear from ordinary folk.

quest:3105.text: Tainted Letter. At Northshire, Tainted Letter calls novice human warlocks away from the Abbey guards for instruction in the fel arts. Drusilla La Salle entrusts it to Marshal McBride, who delivers it to her recruits. Novice warlocks receive a letter from Marshal McBride after proving themselves against the kobold menace. While priests and paladins study openly in Northshire Abbey, warlocks must tread carefully. Drusilla La Salle's insignia marks the letter, which directs each fledgling spellcaster to her secluded post outside the abbey's main walls before taking on other duties. Drusilla warns that warlocks walk a precarious path under the watchful eyes of Stormwind's guards, whom she calls 'pathetic mundanes.' Drawing power from the Twisting Nether and communing with demons always risk corruption. She counsels patience, prudence, and firm self-control when handling those dark energies, but says caution must not extinguish a warlock's ambition.

quest:3116.text: Simple Sigil. In Shadowglen, Alyissia calls young night elf warriors to defend their people. Conservator Ilthalaine carries her summons as the Kaldorei face changes across Teldrassil and beyond. After you prove your basic survival skills against Shadowglen's restless wildlife, Conservator Ilthalaine gives you an inscribed sigil. The token formally marks your move into combat training. It carries a request from Alyissia, the warrior trainer at Aldrassil, asking you to dedicate your strength to defending your people. Alyissia sets your training against a time of rapid change and danger. In only a few years, the night elves have raised the World Tree Teldrassil, seen a taint spread through forest beasts near and far, and reconnected with ancient lands once thought lost, including Feralas. The Kaldorei need capable defenders against these perils. Alyissia prepares young Kaldorei for more than combat. She urges you not to judge outsiders who arrive on Teldrassil by their race. Some travelers may not act from pure generosity, but allies are vital to the Kaldorei's defense. As you take up the work of protecting your people, she asks you to offer them reasonable trust.

quest:3117.text: Etched Sigil. In Shadowglen, the Etched Sigil calls young night elf hunters to Aldrassil. Through Conservator Ilthalaine, Ayanna Everstride summons them to meet their trainer and begin learning archery and beastcraft. After young kaldorei hunters help defend Shadowglen, Conservator Ilthalaine gives them an inscribed token. A messenger brought it from their mentor, Ayanna Everstride. The sigil directs each novice up into Aldrassil’s high boughs, where the trainers watch over the canopy. Meeting Ayanna begins a hunter’s training on Teldrassil. She teaches novices marksmanship and how to understand Kalimdor’s wild creatures. A hunter must respect their beast companions and meet the world’s unseen dangers with awareness and humility.

quest:3118.text: Encrypted Sigil. In Shadowglen, a coded summons calls new night elf rogues to begin their training. Conservator Ilthalaine carries it for Frahun Shadewhisper, who also warns of the fragile peace across Kalimdor. While young night elves study nature's balance under Conservator Ilthalaine, those drawn to stealth receive a quieter summons. A runner brings the Encrypted Sigil from Frahun Shadewhisper, Shadowglen's rogue mentor. Its ciphers are meant for initiates of the trade. The bearer is to decipher the message and find Frahun near the roots of Aldrassil to begin instruction. Frahun's message also warns of Kalimdor's uncertain peace. The Third War has ended, but the truce between the Alliance and the emerging Horde remains fragile. Rogue scouts and informers in Shadowglen are urged to sharpen their eyes and ears early. They watch for threats and covert provocations that could renew war across the borders.

quest:3119.text: Hallowed Sigil. In Shadowglen, young night elf priests are called to begin their training in Aldrassil. Conservator Ilthalaine passes along Shanda's message as novices learn to wield Elune's grace. Night elf priests serve Elune as handmaidens and servants of the moon goddess. When a young kaldorei in Shadowglen shows devotion and an affinity for the divine light, Conservator Ilthalaine gives them a hallowed sigil. Shanda, the priest trainer, sent the token by messenger as an invitation to come to Aldrassil and begin spiritual training. Shanda tells the young acolyte that unusual change has reached Teldrassil's sheltered sanctuary. Travelers fill the World Tree's boughs, including members of the wider Alliance who have leave to meet with the kaldorei. The wider world calls, but Shanda urges novices to first attend to the troubles facing Shadowglen before turning to conflicts beyond it.

quest:3120.text: Verdant Sigil. A summons reaches newly awakened night elf druids in Shadowglen. Conservator Ilthalaine passes the Verdant Sigil to fledgling shapeshifters, directing them to Mardant Strongoak within Aldrassil. The token marks the start of their formal training in nature and the Emerald Dream. When a young night elf shows promise in keeping Shadowglen's balance, the order calls for a formal introduction. A runner brings the Verdant Sigil to Conservator Ilthalaine, who entrusts it to the initiate. The token shows that the circle in Aldrassil has taken notice and invites the young druid to begin formal training. Presenting the sigil to Mardant Strongoak inside Aldrassil brings the initiate into the fold. Deeper communion with the Emerald Dream and mastery of animal forms lie ahead. For now, Mardant becomes their first guide, teaching them to read nature's spirits and channel the raw power of the woods.

quest:3261.text: Jorn Skyseer. In the southern Barrens, seasoned Horde hunters seek guidance from Jorn Skyseer. After you hunt local raptors for Sergra Darkthorn, she sends you south to Camp Taurajo, where an elder tracker offers deeper lessons. You have hunted the cunning sunscale and scytheclaw raptors stalking the northern savannah, earning Sergra Darkthorn's respect at the Crossroads. She knows martial skill must be joined with understanding of the land's great beasts. With her mentorship complete, she sends you south. Follow the Gold Road south through increasingly rugged plains to Camp Taurajo, a vital tauren settlement near the southern wilds. Jorn Skyseer waits there, an elder tracker ready to teach hunters how to pursue elusive, legendary quarry across the Barrens.

quest:3281.text: Stolen Silver. Gazrog at the Crossroads sends you after payroll silver stolen by raptors. Rumors of their cunning lead you south of Ratchet, into the Raptor Grounds. The garrison needs its wages back. Gazrog needs the Crossroads guards paid, and the raptors have taken their wages. You are sent to recover the stolen coin, not simply punish the beasts. When raptors ambushed the payroll shipment, Gazrog first sought vengeance. But killing the pack would not restore the missing money. The Horde must learn how the raptors carried off heavy crates of coin, and where they took them. Scouts found a raptor nest between two craggy peaks, south of Ratchet and northwest of Northwatch Hold. The creatures dragged the intact lockbox into their territory, where they guard it alongside eggs and fresh kills. Tales of raptor cunning and hoarding now seem true to Gazrog. Ordinary beasts rarely stash metallic valuables.

quest:33.text: Wolves Across the Border. Eagan Peltskinner asks you to hunt wolves prowling Northshire Valley and bring him their meat. He waits outside Northshire Abbey, where the valley’s needs continue despite the guards’ focus on Defias bandits. Eagan Peltskinner waits by Northshire Abbey’s walls with a grudge against the local timber wolves. Marshal McBride and the Stormwind guards have limited strength to defend the abbey from Defias bandits, while tradesfolk still have daily needs. Eagan asks you to thin the wolves’ numbers and bring back their tough meat for his cooking. Wolves roam closer to Northshire Abbey as patrols weaken. The Kingdom of Stormwind has too few troops and is strained by missing leadership. Young wolves and timber wolves now prowl the abbey’s paths and orchards. Hunting them supplies Eagan’s pantry and makes nearby trails safer for novitiates, laborers, and newly arrived defenders.

quest:3301.text: Mura Runetotem. You carry a snapjaw shell from the Barrens across the sea to Mura Runetotem in Silverpine Forest. Its strange vitality may help the tauren healer aid the Forsaken. Tonga Runetotem notices something peculiar about altered snapjaws while investigating the magically changed wildlife around the Barrens oases. Their shells pulse with resilient energy despite their corruption. He asks you to carry one across the Great Sea to his clanmate, Mura Runetotem, who is stationed in the Eastern Kingdoms. Mura Runetotem is at the Sepulcher, a Forsaken outpost in Silverpine Forest. She made the arduous journey there to help the Horde's newest allies cleanse and renew their ailing, blighted woodland. Mura hopes the shell's inner glow and enduring spark of life will reveal ways to restore vitality to the northern continent.

quest:332.text: Wine Shop Advert. In Stormwind, Renato Gallina draws passersby to his family's wine shop. He offers a voucher for a free bottle of vintage wine from their canal-side storefront, a small sign of trade in the reconstructed capital. Everyday life in Stormwind revolves around brisk commerce. Renato Gallina walks the Trade District's cobbled streets, promoting Gallina Winery, the small shop he runs with his sister, Suzetta. He hands flyers to thirsty travelers and locals, each offering a free tasting. The Gallina family offers a bottle of their famous pinot noir. Follow the ticket to the winery entrance near the canals, where Suzetta Gallina hands over the bottle. The family hopes a taste of their signature wine will bring newcomers back.

quest:333.text: Harlan Needs a Resupply. Harlan Bagley, a Stormwind merchant, cannot keep sturdy clothes and armor in stock. As demand surges, he sends an urgent cloth order to Rema Schneider at the Canal Tailor and Fit Shop, unaware of the conflicts brewing beyond the city walls. Across Stormwind City, Harlan Bagley's shelves are emptying fast. Citizens and wandering adventurers are buying reinforced tunics, traveling clothes, and battle-ready armor. Harlan wonders if people are preparing for a harsh season or winter, but the rush has left his shop short of finished cloth. Harlan sends a runner across the city's waterways to Rema Schneider, a seamstress at the Canal Tailor and Fit Shop. She is glad of his trade, yet the sudden demand for protective clothing troubles her. Rumors of tension spread through the kingdom, and Rema wonders whether the House of Nobles is hiding talk of open war from ordinary people.

quest:334.text: Package for Thurman. In Stormwind City, Rema Schneider needs her son Thurman’s tailoring supplies at Larson Clothiers in the Mage Quarter. He left home without his shears and needles, and Rema asks you to carry them to his workshop. Rema Schneider worries that Thurman will fall behind in his tailoring work without his shears and needles. He left home in a rush, and his mother asks you to carry the tools across Stormwind’s canals to his workshop.

quest:35.text: Further Concerns. Marshal Dughan sends an Alliance courier east from Goldshire to check reports of danger. You cross Elwynn Forest to speak with Guard Thomas, who watches the river crossing toward Redridge. Rumors tell of hostile aquatic creatures creeping along Elwynn's riverbanks. Marshal Dughan commands the Goldshire garrison, where banditry and vermin already trouble the center of the forest. He will not dismiss the reports, but he cannot spare guards from town. Instead, he sends you east to consult Guard Thomas, the sentry at the bridge over the river toward Redridge. Guard Thomas has held the bridge outpost for more than a week and has seen what Goldshire's leaders only feared. Hostile, semi-intelligent murlocs have made camps along the waterways of eastern Elwynn. Stormwind's army is absent, while local garrisons protect town walls and supply lines. That leaves rural bridge posts like Thomas's isolated before the growing danger.

quest:3519.text: A Friend in Need. Iverron lies bitten and in danger in Shadowglen. The young night elf calls for Dirania Silvershine, whose help may save him from Githyiss the Vile's venom. Iverron lies weakened after a bite from Githyiss the Vile. He ignored warnings and went too near the webwood caverns, where the vicious spider struck. Dizziness and failing strength leave him unable to reach safety alone. Iverron sends passersby toward Aldrassil's central tree to find Dirania Silvershine. She looks out for him and knows the dangers of Shadowglen. His life may depend on her preparing an antidote before the venom proves fatal.

quest:3522.text: Iverron's Antidote. In Shadowglen, Iverron waits for medicine before its strength fades. Poisoned by Webwood spiders, the night elf scout depends on Dirania Silvershine's brew, which must reach him within five minutes. Dirania Silvershine brews the cure from fresh venom sacs, lily roots, and hyacinth fungi. The unstable mixture keeps its strength for only five minutes after it is distilled. Whoever carries the vial must sprint straight from the glade toward the northern heights without hesitation. Webwood spiders around Shadowglen's barrows and caves have poisoned Iverron. He admits he has a habit of stumbling into danger and often depends on Dirania's herbal skill to save him. Even after drinking the antidote, his recovery is fragile. The hostile spiders still guard his way home, and he remains wary of them.

quest:3524.text: Washed Ashore. Along Darkshore, Washed Ashore begins an inquiry into the many sea creatures dying on its shore. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde starts it in Auberdine for the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, where priestesses fear the strandings may be an ill omen. Darkshore has seen great sea creatures beach themselves from time to time, a tragic but occasional sight. Now the strandings come in growing numbers along the coast. The Priestesses of Elune in the Temple of the Moon see more than a natural oddity in these deaths. They fear the pattern may bring ill omens to northern Kalimdor. The Temple of the Moon sends scholar Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde to the port town of Auberdine to learn why the great beasts are coming ashore. She gathers biological samples to send by hippogryph to Darnassus for close examination. But Greymist murlocs swarm the carcasses in the surf, scavenging the remains and keeping researchers from the bones without armed protection.

quest:353.text: Stormpike's Delivery. Grimand Elmore sends travelers north with an axe for Mountaineer Gringer Stormpike. The road leads from Stormwind's Dwarven District to an Ironforge outpost in Loch Modan. Grimand Elmore has been asked to make a weapon for Mountaineer Gringer Stormpike. The Stormpike clan is respected in Ironforge for its discerning taste and martial pride. Elmore turns to trustworthy travelers to carry the axe north, across the distance between Stormwind and the dwarven borderlands. At Loch Modan's northern guard tower, Mountaineer Stormpike watches over lands troubled by wandering troggs and burrowing kobolds. The southern human kingdoms face rumors of unrest and banditry, while the dwarven frontier has dangers of its own. Stormpike needs a new blade to help keep the mountain passes secure.

quest:36.text: Westfall Stew. In Westfall, another family is leaving its farm as banditry drives homesteaders from their land. Before departing, Verna Furlbrow entrusts her cherished local recipe to Salma Saldean. Defias thieves and wild mechanical harvest reapers have driven Verna and Farmer Furlbrow from their family acreage. They pack their wagon and prepare to seek refuge behind Stormwind's walls. Before leaving, Verna gives her neighbor Salma Saldean the recipe for Westfall Stew, hoping the farm's home-cooked tradition will live on. Salma Saldean and her husband, Farmer Saldean, still hold their homestead just down the road. Verna's recipe marks the loss of another neighbor to the unrest, yet keeps a local farm tradition alive. Salma sets out to gather the ingredients needed to feed those still struggling on the frontier.

quest:37.text: Find the Lost Guards. Guard Thomas is waiting at Elwynn's eastern bridge for word of two missing guards. Rolf and Malakai were sent north along the river to watch for murlocs, but neither has returned. Guard Thomas watches the eastern crossing of Elwynn Forest, where the King's road approaches Redridge. Murlocs have made the nearby waters more dangerous. Days ago, Thomas sent two Stormwind guards, Rolf and Malakai, north along the riverbanks to scout the threat and clear out nests. Neither has returned, and Thomas fears violence stopped their patrol.

quest:38.text: Westfall Stew. Salma Saldean cooks Westfall Stew on her farm, making a meal from what the frontier offers. Its ingredients reflect how Westfall homesteaders endure bandits, famine, and dangerous beasts. Westfall's settlers contend with bandits, famine, and rampaging beasts, far from Stormwind's lavish larders. Families like the Saldeans make do with what the land provides. Salma Saldean turns ingredients many city folk might call pests or scraps into a sustaining meal for working farmhands. Salma's recipe brings together local okra, stringy meat from circling vultures, and snouts from wild goretusks roaming the plains. It also calls for fresh murloc eyes gathered from coastal raiders. The thought of river beasts and carrion birds may turn delicate stomachs in Elwynn, but Westfall cooks swear the blend makes a rich, fortifying meal.

quest:3861.text: CLUCK!. In Westfall, a chicken may answer when you call and feed it. Follow its scratched message to the Saldean family, and a warm egg may be yours to hatch. Ordinary chickens wander the farmsteads of Azeroth, and most travelers pass them by. Mimic a chicken's gestures and clucking, and it may stop pecking to regard you with interest. In that brief moment, the bird scratches letters in the dirt. The message points to the farmer who can provide the food it wants. The bird's request calls for Special Chicken Feed. In Westfall, the Saldean family keeps this grain for their flock. Offer the feed and cheer the chicken on as it eats. In return, it lays a warm egg that can be nurtured into a feathered companion.

quest:39.text: Deliver Thomas' Report. In eastern Elwynn, Guard Thomas sends word of two dead guards and rising danger. He asks you to carry the report to Marshal Dughan in Goldshire, where the garrison has few hands to spare. Guard Thomas watches the bridges into eastern Elwynn, where river traffic meets the wilderness. Guards Malakai and Rolf have been killed by aggressive murloc tribes. With his remaining guards too few to contain them, Thomas sends you down the road to Goldshire with an urgent report. Marshal Dughan receives Thomas' report in Goldshire, already struggling to keep patrols on the roads. Kobolds infest the area, Defias bandits threaten travelers, and Stormwind City has sent no reinforcements. The deaths of two experienced guards add to his burden. Murlocs may soon threaten Goldshire itself, while the defenses across the region grow ever thinner.

quest:3903.text: Milly Osworth. At Northshire Abbey, Deputy Willem sends you to help Milly Osworth. Her wagon and livelihood are in jeopardy, and she needs help across the abbey grounds. The work takes you from defending the abbey to aiding Elwynn Forest's civilians. After you prove your mettle against the Defias thieves encroaching on Northshire Valley, Deputy Willem recognizes you as capable and willing to help. He sends you to assist his friend Milly Osworth. This favor is personal, outside the abbey's official guard duties, and Milly is a civilian caught in the valley's growing unrest. Milly waits beside her wagon on the far side of Northshire Abbey, near the stables. Deputy Willem must stay at his post to defend the abbey. Milly's troubles lie out in the valley, where the stretched guard garrison has too few hands to help her.

quest:3904.text: Milly's Harvest. Defias brigands have driven Milly Osworth from the Northshire vineyards. Her harvest lies scattered in buckets and crates among the occupied rows, where it may be stolen or crushed. Milly Osworth fled the southeastern fields of Northshire Valley when Defias brigands swarmed the vines. She left her gathered grapes behind in buckets and crates among the occupied rows. Northshire's garrison is stretched thin, and Milly fears that boots and fighting will crush any fruit the bandits leave behind. Defias bandits now occupy working vineyards, a sign of how little safety Northshire can offer. Stormwind's attention is elsewhere, and the valley has too few guards. Farmers like Milly must depend on recruits and wanderers to protect their property and secure the food and wine that supply the abbey.

quest:3905.text: Grape Manifest. Milly Osworth records her rescued grape harvest for Northshire Abbey. She writes a manifest of the yield recovered from Defias thieves, then sends it to Brother Neals so the brotherhood can replenish its wine stores. Northshire Valley's soil and orchards have long supported local food and the abbey's wine. When thieves and bandits seized the eastern fields, they cut off the abbey's supply of grapes and food. With the harvest recovered from the occupied fields, Milly Osworth records the yield in a manifest. Brother Neals oversees food and drink at Northshire Abbey. He is known for sampling Northshire's vintages in the quiet of the bell tower. Brigands still threaten the gates, but fresh grapes give the brotherhood a moment to toast the Light and take heart.

quest:3921.text: Wenikee Boltbucket. Near the Mor'shan Rampart, Wenikee Boltbucket may be able to mend a broken samophlange. Sputtervalve tinkered with the device after it was retrieved from the Sludge Fen, and now needs an expert hand before his colleagues in Undermine demand results. Sputtervalve's claims to his fellow engineers in Undermine now hang on a broken machine. An adventurer retrieved the mysterious samophlange from the Venture Company's control console at the Sludge Fen, and Sputtervalve could not resist showing it off. His tinkering damaged the delicate contraption. He needs someone with sharper skill to diagnose the damage and repair it. Wenikee Boltbucket camps beside the road just south of the Mor'shan Rampart. The rampart divides the northern Barrens from Ashenvale. Her inquisitive mind is drawn to intricate machinery, and the broken samophlange quickly captures her attention. Its internal gears hold her curiosity, and she sets to work figuring out how to rebuild it.

quest:3922.text: Nugget Slugs. At the Sludge Fen, Wenikee Boltbucket needs parts for a recovered samophlange. The eccentric tinkerer sends you to the nearby Venture Company drilling crews for spare hardware. Wenikee Boltbucket has a recovered samophlange and wants to learn how the intricate machine works. Its goblin mechanisms need exact parts, so she sends you to the Venture Company crews at the Sludge Fen. Their heavy tool buckets hold the seventeen-point-five gauge nugget slugs she needs.

quest:3923.text: Rilli Greasygob. In Orgrimmar, Rilli Greasygob is the specialist Wenikee Boltbucket seeks. She sends you there with a damaged samophlange, hoping his knowledge of its Venture Company origins can explain the device. Wenikee Boltbucket examined the samophlange recovered from the Venture Company drilling site in the Barrens. Her extra gauges showed the apparatus nearing collapse. More levers and dials might destroy it, so she stopped and sent the problem to someone with knowledge of its design. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor, Wenikee sends you to Nogg's Machine Shop. Rilli Greasygob works there as an engineer and once learned his trade within the Venture Company. He recognizes the machine at once and marvels that anyone survived exploring the company's contested operations in the Barrens.

quest:3924.text: Samophlange Manual. In Orgrimmar, Rilli Greasygob needs help with a broken samophlange. The goblin engineer sends you back into the Barrens for the operating instructions, held by his former Venture Company rival. Rilli Greasygob once worked beside Boss Copperplug in the Venture Company. Copperplug oversaw the samophlange’s inner workings and guarded their secrets closely. He shared no manual with Rilli. Instead, he gave out separate pages only to underlings he trusted, leaving his fellow engineer without the knowledge to understand the device.

quest:399.text: Humble Beginnings. Baros Alexston seeks help from his home in Stormwind's Cathedral Square. His family's Westfall farm has burned, and thieves hold its ruins; he hopes to recover an heirloom from his youth. Baros Alexston grew up working the fields of Westfall. Now he is an accomplished architect in Stormwind City, advising on stonework and city buildings. His path from farm boy to city planner is rare in the kingdom, yet he remains attached to the modest beginnings that shaped him. Lawlessness swept across Westfall, and the Alexston Farmstead fell to it. Bandits and vagrants burned the house, forcing Baros's father from his livelihood. Family heirlooms were left behind amid the fire and occupation. Baros asks you to search the ruined, bandit-held farmstead west of Sentinel Hill for his first compass, hidden before the home fell.

quest:40.text: A Fishy Peril. In Goldshire, A Fishy Peril begins with reports of murlocs moving inland through the waterways. Remy "Two Times" asks travelers to alert Marshal Dughan, whose guards are already stretched thin. Remy "Two Times" grows uneasy over a new threat while seeking business in Goldshire. Murlocs are creeping up the streams and into inland shallows, disrupting fishing and menacing innocent travelers. Remy fears the local guard is overlooking a danger that is still growing, so he asks passersby to carry word to the heart of the township. Marshal Dughan hears the report in Goldshire but remains skeptical. He is charged with protecting the realm while royal forces are stretched thin elsewhere, and Riverpaw gnolls and Defias highwaymen already demand his attention. With no confirmed military intelligence, he will not divert his scarce men to pursue rumors of fish-men in the eastern streams.

quest:4161.text: Recipe of the Kaldorei. Zarrin teaches a lesson in balance through the Recipe of the Kaldorei. In Dolanaar, young cooks learn to gather only what they need from Teldrassil's woods. Behind the inn in Dolanaar, Zarrin tends a bubbling cauldron and teaches young adventurers the traditions of his people. The night elves once called themselves the kaldorei, or children of the stars. Zarrin begins their understanding of that heritage with the bond between a hunter, their food, and Teldrassil's boughs, rather than the battlefield. Zarrin teaches restraint through a simple demand: gather small spider legs from the woodland arachnids outside Shadowglen, but take exactly seven. The kaldorei seek harmony with nature by taking only what they need and showing kindness to the wild. Even in troubled times, that balance matters. A spider kabob becomes a lesson in living with care.

quest:4495.text: A Good Friend. At Aldrassil, Dirania Silvershine grows worried when Iverron misses his daily visit. She asks travelers to search the hills near Shadowthread Cave, north of Shadowglen. Dirania Silvershine waits beneath Aldrassil for Iverron, who visits her every day. Hours pass without him, and she asks travelers heading into Shadowglen to look for her friend. Iverron often wanders the hills in northern Shadowglen, near the webwood spiders of Shadowthread Cave. The spiders make the surrounding slopes dangerous for travelers. Search west of the cave entrance, where Iverron is hiding and needs help.

quest:45.text: Discover Rolf's Fate. In eastern Elwynn, two Stormwind guards are missing near Stone Cairn Lake. Malakai's half-eaten remains and webbed tracks lead toward a murloc village, where the search for Rolf continues. Guard Thomas sent patrols around eastern Elwynn Forest as threats grew, but Malakai and Rolf vanished near Stone Cairn Lake. Malakai's half-eaten remains lie by the shore. Webbed footprints pressed into the mud lead east along the water's edge, straight to a ramshackle murloc camp.

quest:4513.text: A Little Slime Goes a Long Way. Following his initial study of tainted specimens, the gnome researcher Laris Geardawdle seeks untainted ooze samples to understand how these strange creatures adapt to their environment. Having realized that oozes absorb the corrupted nature of places like Felwood, he sends adventurers to discover and gather pure, unpolluted specimens from across Kalimdor. Laris Geardawdle's preliminary experiments in Ironforge hit an immediate stumbling block: the oozes he previously examined were thoroughly polluted by the dark energies of Felwood. While this demonstrated that oozes absorb and reflect the traits of their surroundings, it left him without a control group. To understand the baseline nature of ooze life, he needs specimens untouched by demonic taint or urban filth.

quest:456.text: The Balance of Nature. Conservator Ilthalaine calls newly awakened night elves to tend Shadowglen’s wildlife. Young nightsabers and thistle boars have grown too numerous, and keeping Teldrassil’s natural harmony calls for stewardship and difficult choices. In Shadowglen, beneath the Great Tree’s sprawling boughs, heavy spring rains have disrupted Teldrassil’s young, fragile forest cycle. Some wildlife populations have grown beyond what the land can sustain. They threaten to strip the glen of resources and bring famine to the ecosystem. Preserving the forest calls for active care. Conservator Ilthalaine watches over Shadowglen’s woods, keeping any one part from overtaking the others. To prevent mass starvation among the animals, he sends young night elves into the grove to thin thistle boars and predatory nightsabers. The work is unglamorous, but vital: kaldorei stewardship means seeking harmony with nature through active balance and difficult decisions.

quest:457.text: The Balance of Nature. Conservator Ilthalaine sends defenders into Shadowglen to thin its growing wildlife. Mature thistle boars and mangy nightsabers threaten the glade's balance. Shadowglen's adult animals now threaten the World Tree's ecosystem. Conservator Ilthalaine sends young defenders deeper into the forest to hunt mature thistle boars and older, mangy nightsabers. Their appetites can exhaust the land's limited plants and game. North of Aldrassil, younger cubs give way to mottled nightsabers and aggressive boars that root through the soil. For kaldorei, controlled hunting is a grim duty, but it protects the whole forest from collapse.

quest:458.text: The Woodland Protector. In Shadowglen, Melithar Staghelm hears troubling whispers from the forest spirits. He asks you to find Tarindrella, an elusive dryad whose unexpected return hints at trouble beneath Teldrassil’s canopy. Melithar Staghelm receives troubling omens from the woodland spirits while training novices beneath Aldrassil’s boughs. Tarindrella, a dryad regarded as a protector of the wild, has returned to Shadowglen after many years away from Kalimdor’s woodlands. Dryads rarely appear without cause, and Melithar fears the natural order is out of balance.

quest:459.text: The Woodland Protector. In Shadowglen, Tarindrella seeks the cause of the forest’s sudden unrest and the furbolgs’ disappearance. Grells have turned aggressive, and Fel Moss points to dark magic in Teldrassil’s boughs. Shadowglen’s quiet woods have grown hostile. The furbolgs have left their ancestral dens and gathered as the Gnarlpine tribe. Feral grells and grellkin now overrun the woodland paths, and Tarindrella has noticed the dark change spreading through Teldrassil. Tarindrella suspects corruption is stirring the forest’s creatures. You slay the grells and bring her samples of Fel Moss, evidence of dark enchantments clinging to Teldrassil’s boughs. With the corruption confirmed, she sends young defenders to Dolanaar to speak with Druid Athridas Bearmantle.

quest:46.text: Bounty on Murlocs. Murlocs are spreading through eastern Elwynn, and the Stormwind Army has put a bounty on them. With the garrison stretched thin, Guard Thomas turns to travelers to clear the shoreline camps around Stone Cairn Lake and the southern waterways before the murlocs overrun nearby farms and roads. Murlocs have made shoreline camps around Stone Cairn Lake and along the fork of the southern streams. Lurkers and foragers now attack travelers and press toward human settlements. What began as a minor nuisance has grown into a threat across eastern Elwynn, while the western roads remain comparatively secure. Guard Thomas is stationed at the eastern bridge beside the Redridge Mountains, where dangers beyond the bridge and disorder at home compete for his attention. King Varian Wrynn is missing, and Stormwind's military command is mired in bureaucracy. Town garrisons rarely get the reinforcements they request. Marshal Dughan and local officers have turned to public bounties, offering coin for murloc fins to slow the attacks along the waterways.

quest:4681.text: Washed Ashore. Along Darkshore's misty coast, dead sea creatures have drawn Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde into a troubling inquiry. She serves the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus and seeks to learn why marine life is stranding or dying along the shore. Dead sea creatures line Darkshore's beaches and shallows, puzzling the night elves of Auberdine. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde has already examined one stranded creature along the beach. Now she asks you to dive west of the docks, near a sunken vessel, and inspect the bones of a massive sea turtle. The evidence will help her report to the Temple of the Moon.

quest:47.text: Gold Dust Exchange. At Goldshire's crossroads, Gold Dust Exchange brings Remy "Two Times" coin for gold dust from kobolds in Elwynn's mines. Travelers gather the dust and trade it to the nervous broker for pay. Goldshire sits where Elwynn Forest's roads meet, and travelers, merchants, and guards pass through town. Remy "Two Times" is a shady broker with a habit of repeating his words and a sharp eye for profit. Instead of paying mining crews to dig for raw minerals, he turns to travelers passing through the Lion's Pride Inn. He offers coin for gold dust taken from the kobolds in the region. Kobolds have overrun Fargodeep Mine south of Goldshire and Jasperlode Mine to the northeast. These rat-like tunnelers chip through the dark for candles and shiny baubles, gathering flecks of unrefined ore in their pouches. Pushing them back serves the kingdom, and gathering their dust turns the work into a trade for coin.

quest:4722.text: Beached Sea Turtle. Along Darkshore’s surf-battered shore, a massive sea turtle lies beached as murlocs pick over its carcass. Viable biological samples remain among the scavenged remains, and Auberdine naturalists send them to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus for study. Darkshore’s long coast often catches the dead and confused from the Great Sea. Ancient sea turtles drift ashore after death or beach themselves in confusion. Their carcasses quickly draw scavengers, and hostile Greymist murlocs have made crude camps around this turtle’s skeletal frame. They carve away flesh and shell, yet viable bone, shell, or tissue samples may remain intact in the wreckage. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde is stationed in Auberdine as a field researcher, documenting unusual marine life and ecological disturbances along the coast. Night elves regard stranded beasts with reverence and scientific curiosity. Suitable remains are cataloged and prepared for shipment to scholars in Darnassus, who seek to understand why so many giants of the open sea are washing ashore.

quest:4723.text: Beached Sea Creature. At Mist's Edge, a giant sea thresher lies stranded while murlocs feed on its carcass. In Auberdine, Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde gathers samples for night elf researchers in Darnassus, who seek to learn why deep-sea giants are washing ashore. Enormous thresher remains have appeared along Mist's Edge, where shipwrecks and tide-washed debris are familiar sights. This beast dwarfs the wildlife of Darkshore's shallows, suggesting it came from far beyond the calm waters of the Veiled Sea. Murlocs swarm over the corpse to feed, but they lack the strength and coordination to bring down a creature of this size. Something else killed the predator before the sea carried it ashore. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde coordinates efforts in Auberdine to salvage bones and biological samples from Darkshore's stranded sea giants. Night elf researchers in Darnassus hope the remains will show whether illness, disturbances in the deep sea, or arcane corruption drives the giants onto the killing sands.

quest:4725.text: Beached Sea Turtle. Along Darkshore's shore, Beached Sea Turtle lies with a broken carriage on its shell. Greymist murlocs have gathered around the great carcass. You find a broken carriage strapped across a giant sea turtle's shell on Darkshore's misty shore. Many sea creatures have washed up along this coast, but this turtle was made to carry a load. Its handlers drove it onto the beach, and the carriage now lies abandoned in the tide. Greymist murlocs soon swarm the turtle's remains. They have made a den among the rotting meat and scavenged timber. A marked container lies among their refuse and the broken carriage frame, left by the turtle's former masters.

quest:4727.text: Beached Sea Turtle. Along Darkshore’s northern shore, Beached Sea Turtle remains untouched by nearby Greymist murlocs. A sample is carried to Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde in Auberdine for the Temple of the Moon. Naturalists and priestesses seek to learn why great sea creatures wash ashore and scavengers leave them alone. Greymist murlocs crowd Darkshore’s northern coast and scavenge whatever food washes up from the Veiled Sea. Yet the great turtle’s skeleton lies mostly untouched. Those studying the shore wonder whether the murlocs missed it or avoided it for some unknown reason. In Auberdine, Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde gathers samples from beached sea turtles for the Temple of the Moon. The night elf priestesses study the disturbances in Darkshore’s waters. Skeletal fragments may help them learn whether sickness, magic, or dangerous sea predators are killing the ancient creatures.

quest:4728.text: Beached Sea Creature. Along Darkshore, a giant sea mammal lies washed ashore beside an abandoned dig site. Its carcass and scattered tools draw murlocs and passing travelers. A giant sea mammal lies on Darkshore's sand, partly gutted and worn by the sea. A rusted wheelbarrow and discarded tools mark the place where an organized study began. The researchers left before they could finish. Dwarven field researchers from the Explorer's League were studying the carcass in Darkshore. Their work stopped when local murlocs swarmed the site to scavenge. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde in Auberdine acts for the Temple of the Moon and accepts salvaged bone samples to help study the unnatural wash-ups along the coast.

quest:4730.text: Beached Sea Creature. Along Darkshore, a great sea mammal lies half-devoured on the sand. Murlocs gather around it, and Priestess Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde in Auberdine seeks bone samples to learn why gentle sea beasts are dying on the shore. Far north along Darkshore's lonely beaches, a great sea mammal lies rotting and half-eaten. Murlocs pick over its bones, more vicious than usual. These beasts were gentle in life, and their deaths trouble the coast as much as the blighted forests inland. Priestess Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde says these gentle mammals live in the waters around Teldrassil's base. Unlike aggressive threshers, they have never been known to drive themselves onto the rocks. The Temple of the Moon is gathering bone samples to learn what corruption or threat drives them from the deep.

quest:4731.text: Beached Sea Turtle. Along Darkshore's coast, a Beached Sea Turtle lies dead beneath the carriage it once hauled. A box marked with strange runes rests in the wreckage. A dead sea turtle lies among the ancient bones scattered along Darkshore's coast. Splintered carriage boards still cling to its broad shell. The turtle was driven onto the rocks while hauling cargo, rather than stranded by sickness or disorientation. A container carved with unfamiliar, serpent-like marks lies in the wreckage, amid scavengers feeding on the remains.

quest:4733.text: Beached Sea Creature. Along Darkshore's rocky Twilight Shore, a colossal thresher lies stranded, far larger than any known local specimen. Its death and stranding add to the deep-sea troubles worrying the night elves. You find driftwood and sea debris along the Twilight Shore in southern Darkshore, but one inlet holds the remains of an enormous thresher. Tides and scavengers have begun picking it apart, yet its skeleton dwarfs ordinary predators in these coastal shallows. The giant is an outsider to these waters. Sickness or disorientation may have driven it onto the rocks, or some deeper disturbance may lie out in the Veiled Sea.

quest:4740.text: WANTED: Murkdeep!. Auberdine posts an Alliance bounty for Murkdeep, blamed for a Sentinel's death and ships lost off Darkshore. The village council wants the dangerous murloc chieftain dead. Find him south along the misty coast. The Greymist murlocs along Darkshore are usually a nuisance, but Murkdeep has turned against Auberdine. The wanted poster outside the inn names him as the killer of at least one night elf Sentinel. It also suspects him of sabotaging or wrecking two cargo vessels offshore. With ships lost and raids along the coast, the Auberdine Village Council has set a public bounty on the murloc leader. Murkdeep lurks off the southern coast, near murloc huts clustered around a bonfire. Trespassers draw an organized defense: Greymist coastrunners and shore-crawlers surge from the surf to protect their settlement. Murkdeep then emerges alongside his vanguard to strike the intruders. Proof of Murkdeep's death meets a grim need for the Sentinels. Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea handles the bounty payout for the council. With Greymist leadership broken, travelers and ships on the foggy Darkshore coast gain a reprieve from sabotage.

quest:475.text: A Troubling Breeze. Athridas Bearmantle waits for word from Starbreeze Village, but the reports have stopped. Great Warden Gaerolas Talvethren watches over the sleeping Druids of the Talon in the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, and his silence points to danger in Teldrassil. Athridas Bearmantle depends on regular word from Gaerolas Talvethren, the Great Warden watching over the Druids of the Talon in the Ban'ethil Barrow Den. The druids sleep there to keep their sacred pact with Ysera in the Emerald Dream. Their sanctuary matters to the spiritual balance of the young World Tree. Now reports from the east have ceased, and unease spreads through the forest.

quest:476.text: Gnarlpine Corruption. Near Starbreeze Village, Gnarlpine Corruption threatens Teldrassil. Wounded Great Warden Gaerolas Talvethren sends word to the night elf leadership in Dolanaar: Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun the village and fallen to demonic corruption. Their violence may reach the sleeping druids of Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Near the ruins of Starbreeze Village, Gaerolas Talvethren lies grievously wounded after an ambush by his former allies. The Gnarlpine furbolgs were long regarded as peaceful neighbors and stewards of the wild, but now they have turned feral. Too injured to carry the warning himself, Gaerolas entrusts you with bringing word to Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar before the madness spreads farther through Teldrassil.

quest:4761.text: Thundris Windweaver. In Auberdine, reports of Blackwood aggression reach the village elder. Terenthis sends you to Thundris Windweaver with news of the furbolgs’ growing hostility. Thundris seeks the cause of the corruption spreading through Darkshore. After scouting corrupted furbolg camps in Darkshore, you carry Terenthis’s report to Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine. Terenthis remains in the wilds to investigate the spreading corruption. As village elder, Thundris oversees the settlement’s daily welfare and considers the spiritual and environmental dangers facing the kaldorei. Your report gives Auberdine’s leadership evidence that the furbolgs are growing more than territorial: an unnatural malice is taking hold of them. Thundris has heard of rising hostility from the forest dwellers near Auberdine. The furbolgs’ aggression is not the only concern. Corruption is spreading through Darkshore’s soil, plants, and waters. Thundris believes the land cannot be healed until the source of the blight is found. He turns to the waterways and enlists capable allies to trace the taint upstream.

quest:4762.text: The Cliffspring River. In Darkshore, foul water now runs down the Cliffspring River toward Auberdine. Thundris Windweaver asks Alliance investigators to take a sample from the pool beneath a road bridge waterfall. He suspects the corruption began beyond the riverbanks. The Cliffspring River runs from the eastern highlands to the coastal shoals of Mist's Edge, just north of Auberdine. Its waters have begun to carry an unnatural rot toward the night elf settlement. Thundris Windweaver fears the foul water will poison the shores and the town's supplies, so he sends scouts upriver to take samples from the waterfall pool beneath the road bridge.

quest:4811.text: The Red Crystal. Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea asks travelers in Auberdine to investigate a red crystal in Darkshore's eastern mountains. Hostile moonkin are multiplying nearby and seem drawn to it, and the Sentinels need to know if the formation is real. Moonkin were long seen as gentle, mystical creatures bound to the wilds of Kalimdor. Now aggressive packs are multiplying along the slopes east of Auberdine. Some night elves still revere them, but Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea puts the town's safety first as the danger grows. Reports place the beasts at a single spot among the eastern peaks. Scouts and wanderers speak of an unnatural red crystal jutting from a rocky hillside high above Darkshore. Rumors travel easily along the fogbound coast, so Glynda wants someone to see the place firsthand. The crystal is real, and the Sentinels still need to learn why the moonkin gather there and whether it threatens the land.

quest:4812.text: As Water Cascades. Sacred water is brought to bear on the red crystal in Darkshore. Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea hopes moonwell water from Auberdine will reveal what lies beneath its opaque surface. Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea seeks a safe way to study the red crystal high on Darkshore's eastern cliffs. Moonwell water holds divine, restorative magic, blessed by the night elves' devotion to Elune. Glynda believes water from Auberdine's moonwell may react with the strange stone and pierce its opaque shell without destroying it.

quest:483.text: The Relics of Wakening. At Ban'ethil Barrow Den, an urgent effort is underway to save the sleeping Druids of the Talon. Corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun the sacred mounds, threatening the druids whose spirits wander the Emerald Dream. Four ritual relics are needed to bring the sleepers safely back to the waking world. West of Dolanaar, a swarm of corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs has overrun the winding corridors of Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Barrow dens are secluded sanctuaries where night elf druids hibernate while their spirits walk the Emerald Dream. A foul taint spreading across Teldrassil has driven these former allies mad. They have desecrated the sanctum, leaving the sleepers unaware that danger threatens their physical bodies. Athridas Bearmantle needs four sacred relics for the delicate ceremony that can safely awaken the Druids of the Talon. A druid's spirit needs an anchor when returning from the Dream; without one, a sudden awakening can shatter the mind or strand the spirit. The relics lie in chests across the den: the Raven Claw Talisman, the Black Feather Quill, the Sapphire of Sky, and the Rune of Nesting. They are the sleepers' only hope before the Gnarlpine butcher or abduct them.

quest:486.text: Ursal the Mauler. In Teldrassil, Athridas Bearmantle seeks to wake the Druids of the Talon from their unnatural sleep. Their kin remain trapped in the Barrow Den, and the corrupted Gnarlpine chief behind the disturbance must be slain. The Druids of the Talon withdrew to the Barrow Den of Ban'ethil to sleep and commune with the Emerald Dream. Their peaceful trance became a prison with no way back to waking. Athridas Bearmantle traced the trouble to the gnarlpine furbolgs, and to their vicious leader, Ursal the Mauler, who meddled with the druids' sacred ritual. The sleepers remain caught between waking and the Dream. Athridas needs more than the Relics of Wakening to reach the druids through the spiritual fog. The source of the interference must be ended. Ursal the Mauler makes his lair in Gnarlpine Hold, the tribe's home in far southwestern Teldrassil. Striking down the furbolg warlord breaks his hold on the sleepers' minds.

quest:487.text: The Road to Darnassus. Along Teldrassil’s western road, corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs threaten the route from Dolanaar to Darnassus. Moon Priestess Amara coordinates scouts and travelers to keep this trade and messenger road clear of ambushes. You travel west from Dolanaar toward Darnassus on Teldrassil’s main overland road. Trade goods, political messages, and travelers use it each day to stay connected with the capital and the boughs of the great tree. Teldrassil is young and wild, so safe roads matter to its kaldorei communities. The Gnarlpine furbolgs of Teldrassil have fallen to a foul corruption. Driven mad by a sickness plaguing the boughs of the World Tree, they attack from hidden dens beneath the ridges. Gnarlpine ambushers stalk the tree line beside the road, preying on couriers and travelers and making the forest passage deadly. Moon Priestess Amara watches over the road outside Dolanaar. She joins the spiritual authority of Elune’s priesthood with the Sentinels’ vigilance, directing capable travelers to strike at ambushers near their dens below the road. The safety of the route to Darnassus’s gates depends on keeping them at bay.

quest:488.text: Zenn's Bidding. Zenn Foulhoof draws newcomers into his schemes north of the road from Shadowglen to Dolanaar. The solitary satyr asks them to gather animal parts, preying on their trust and naivety. Travelers on the path from Shadowglen to Dolanaar may find Zenn Foulhoof beneath the Great Tree. The satyr offers material rewards and secrets for simple work, asking for nightsaber fangs, strigid owl feathers, and webwood spider silk from the surrounding woods. He whispers conspiratorially, urging travelers to keep their bargain between themselves.

quest:489.text: Seek Redemption!. In Dolanaar, you face the Council of the Forest's demand for atonement. Adventurers were duped into doing Zenn Foulhoof's dirty work, and now the council sends you to trick the satyr into eating corrupted fel cones. Just outside Dolanaar, solitary satyr Zenn Foulhoof uses deceit to make passersby do his bidding. Adventurers who unwittingly slaughtered nightsabers, strigid owls, and webwood spiders to satisfy his twisted appetites draw the Council of the Forest's sharp disapproval. The council will not accept harm to nature, especially from its own allies. Syral Bladeleaf, Sentinel Kyra Starsong, or Sentinel Shayla Nightbreeze warns you that you must make amends to remain welcome in Teldrassil. Dolanaar's guardians tell you to turn Foulhoof's wicked gluttony against him instead of facing him with steel. Gather the billowing, corrupted fel cones from the forest floor, then offer the unsuspecting satyr a taste of his own foul medicine.

quest:5041.text: Supplies for the Crossroads. Thork needs supplies back at the Crossroads after Razormane quilboar raids. The stolen crates hold provisions the outpost needs amid conflict across the Barrens. Thork needs provisions restored to the Crossroads after a supply caravan is ambushed. The outpost links Horde travel, trade, and defense across the Barrens, and cargo arrives from Durotar and Mulgore. Without it, shortages of provisions, tools, and arms threaten daily life in the harsh wilderness. Razormane quilboar have taken the crates. These swine-beasts contest Horde control across central Kalimdor. They hauled the cargo to their thorn-bush camps and keep it there. Thork sends trusted warriors into Razormane territory to recover the supplies for the Horde.

quest:5061.text: Aquatic Form. You return to Darnassus with the restored Pendant of the Sea Lion. The rite teaches Alliance druids to attune their spirits to deep waters. For Cenarion Circle initiates, shapeshifting joins the druid’s spirit to the wild aspects of Azeroth. After enduring trials in the dark coastal depths and in Moonglade, young night elf druids receive the assembled Pendant of the Sea Lion from Dendrite Starblaze. They carry the sacred token back to Teldrassil as proof of their respect for the laws of air, water, and breath. Mathrengyl Bearwalker awaits your return in the Cenarion Enclave. The trials along the coasts of Darkshore and Westfall demand endurance and attunement. Presenting the completed pendant shows Bearwalker that your mind and body are ready to shed their mortal skin and take the swift, breathing form of the sea lion.

quest:52.text: Protect the Frontier. Guard Thomas watches Elwynn's eastern bridge as predators threaten the frontier.
