Stormwind's forces are thin here, and wolves and bears have grown bold near the Eastvale Logging Camp. He asks capable adventurers to cull the beasts threatening travelers and workers. Guard Thomas watches the bridge over the river at Elwynn Forest's eastern edge. Goldshire and the Northshire Valley have a visible Stormwind garrison, but this frontier receives far less protection. With Stormwind's forces stretched across the realm, Thomas is one of few sentries between the settled heartlands and the wilderness. Travelers help keep vital supply roads open. Eastvale Logging Camp supplies timber to Stormwind City, but woodsmen felling trees at the forest's edge meet dangerous wildlife. Prowlers, gray forest wolves, and young forest bears now roam near roads and lumber yards. Culling them eases the danger to local workers for a time. Thomas suspects a disturbance deeper in the woods is driving the beasts toward settlements.

quest:5261.text: Eagan Peltskinner. Outside Northshire Abbey, Eagan Peltskinner has work for recruits as timber wolves threaten the valley. The local furrier needs hunters to thin the packs and bring back pelts. Deputy Willem often sends recruits from the abbey to find Eagan Peltskinner, who works nearby on its grounds. Northshire Valley's orchards and fields lie beside wild woods where timber wolves prowl. Eagan wants newcomers to hunt the aggressive packs and gather pelts for his craft. Timber wolves threaten workers, acolytes, and supplies moving in and out of Northshire. Sending young champions to Eagan helps keep nearby paths safe while sparing Stormwind's few remaining guards. They are already occupied by rising tensions across Elwynn Forest.

quest:543.text: The Perenolde Tiara. Count Remington Ridgewell seeks a lost heirloom in the Ruins of Alterac. The Stormwind aristocrat sends mercenaries north to recover the Perenolde Tiara, once owned by Alterac's royal family and now said to be held by an ogre mage. Alterac's royal family wore an emerald-set tiara crafted by master dwarven jewelers in Ironforge. During the Second War, King Aiden Perenolde betrayed the Grand Alliance and joined the Orcish Horde. His betrayal led to Alterac's conquest and collapse. In the fall of Alterac City, many treasures of the royal family vanished among the snowy rubble of the Alterac Mountains. Grel'borg the Miser, an ogre mage of the Crushridge ogres, came to hold the tiara among the ruins of Alterac. He searches the broken stones for baubles and abandoned wealth. Count Remington Ridgewell, a collector of historical oddities in Stormwind City, learns the tiara survived. He hires mercenaries to enter ogre-held territory, defeat Grel'borg, and bring the jewel back to his gallery.

quest:5502.text: A Warden of the Horde. In Orgrimmar, Children's Week ends with Grunth's return to Orphan Matron Battlewail. After seeing the world with his guardian, the young orphan hopes to become a hero himself. After the adventures of Children's Week, Grunth thanks you for showing him more than he ever dreamed he would see. He remembers his parents' advice to rise above hardship and hopes to become a hero like you. His final request is to return home and tell the matron about your time together. You return Grunth to Orphan Matron Battlewail at the orphanage in the Valley of Honor. In the new Horde, caring for the young is a profound duty, since war has left countless children without parents. Battlewail praises your compassion as the true measure of a Horde hero. Grunth parts with a beloved pet so you will remember the bond formed during your travels.

quest:5545.text: A Bundle of Trouble. At Eastvale Logging Camp, A Bundle of Trouble begins with timber left in the woods and a deadline near. Supervisor Raelen needs the cut wood brought back before the shipment falls behind. Supervisor Raelen has a shipment of timber due soon. Eastvale Logging Camp cuts wood for Stormwind, and her crew has fallen behind schedule. With the deadline close, Raelen needs the timber sent on its way. Wolves and bears north of the camp have driven the woodcutters away from bundles of cut timber. The workers left the wood where it lay. Raelen cannot wait for guards to clear the area, so she asks you to bring the bundles back to camp.

quest:5621.text: Garments of the Moon. Laurna Morninglight sends a young priest to aid a wounded Sentinel south of Dolanaar. The duty tests an initiate's devotion and brings formal recognition in the Sisterhood of Elune. The Sisterhood of Elune guides kaldorei in worship and helps defend Teldrassil's borders. Sentinel Shaya is wounded while patrolling the wilderness south of Dolanaar, and priest trainer Laurna Morninglight cannot leave her post to help. She asks a newly trained initiate to tend Shaya's wounds and strengthen her with protective magic. After restoring Sentinel Shaya's vigor, a priest returns to Dolanaar to receive formal robes of office from Laurna Morninglight. The robes mark an acolyte's passage from classroom instruction to practical service that can save lives. For the kaldorei, aiding the Sentinels is both service to Elune and a duty to Teldrassil's safety.

quest:5622.text: In Favor of Elune. Young night elf priests leave Shadowglen for guidance and training in Dolanaar. Priestess Shanda sends them along the forest path to Laurna Morninglight. Priestess Shanda trains initiates serving Elune within Aldrassil's secluded shelter. Their learning begins with simple prayers and defensive invocations under her watchful eye. Shadowglen's cloistered life cannot prepare a priestess or priest for the turmoil gripping the wider world. Once an initiate shows steady faith and discipline, Shanda sends them down the shadowed forest path toward Dolanaar to continue their education. Reaching Dolanaar marks an essential milestone in a night elf's divine vocation. There, respected priestess Laurna Morninglight prepares disciples for the trials facing Teldrassil. The acolyte can receive advanced instruction in moonlit spellcraft and claim their first formal vestments, marking their official standing within the Sisterhood of Elune.

quest:5623.text: In Favor of the Light. Priestess Anetta sends you south from Northshire Abbey to continue your training in Goldshire. Priestess Josetta is waiting at the Lion's Pride Inn to guide your next steps in the Holy Light. Northshire Abbey gives you shelter and your first lessons in the Holy Light. After you learn prayer and divine healing, Priestess Anetta sends you south along the road to Goldshire. There, you leave the abbey's sheltered study for service among the people of Elwynn. Priestess Josetta tends to Goldshire's spiritual needs from the Lion's Pride Inn and guides rising acolytes. She builds on the lessons you learned at the abbey, teaching you to offer comfort, protect the faithful, and heal the injured. Under her guidance, you begin learning the duties of the Church's servants across the kingdom.

quest:5624.text: Garments of the Light. At Goldshire, Garments of the Light mark a novice priest’s first trial under Priestess Josetta. She sends you east to Crystal Lake to tend the wounded Guard Roberts. The work tests your healing and earns you vestments recognized by the Church of the Holy Light. Priestess Josetta teaches acolytes who come to Goldshire from Northshire Abbey. Before the Church of the Holy Light formally recognizes a novice, she tests their skill with divine power. When Guard Roberts is reported wounded by the lake east of Goldshire, Josetta sends you to care for him. His need gives you a chance to prove your healing in practice. You need to do more than close Guard Roberts’s wounds. Mend him with restorative prayers, then strengthen him with a blessing of fortitude. Stormwind’s forces are stretched thin, and local garrisons face kobolds and bandits. Josetta teaches that priests help defenders endure danger. Healing Roberts will aid the township and show that you can support its guards. After treating Guard Roberts, return to the Lion’s Pride Inn. There you receive your first formal robes, a sign of approval and fellowship from the priesthood in Stormwind. The robes are not required for further training, but they show that the Church recognizes you as a servant of the Holy Light.

quest:5627.text: Stars of Elune. In Darnassus, night elf acolytes are called to the Temple of the Moon after proving their devotion to their people. There, the Sisterhood of Elune teaches them sacred arts of their faith. Night elf priests draw their holy power from Elune, their goddess, while humans and dwarves turn to the Light. When an acolyte serves the realm with steadfast devotion, the Sisterhood in Darnassus takes notice. The acolyte is summoned to the Temple of the Moon and judged ready for deeper communion. There, the priest learns sacred spells passed down through thousands of years of worship. Priestess Alathea calls the initiate to receive instruction in holy mysteries of the night elf faith, including Starshards. These spells channel the radiant wrath and grace of the White Lady. The teaching marks an acolyte's passage beyond basic training, ready to venture beyond Teldrassil's protective canopy in Elune's name.

quest:5628.text: Returning Home. In Goldshire, a novice night elf priest receives a call to return home. The novice has wandered as far as Elwynn Forest, where Priestess Josetta relays an urgent message from Darnassus: return to the Temple of the Moon and continue spiritual training under Priestess Alathea. Night elves are an unusual sight in Elwynn Forest, and a young acolyte among its human settlements draws attention. When you arrive in Goldshire, Priestess Josetta greets you warmly with news. A Sister of Elune has traveled across continents seeking you, bearing an urgent command from the Temple of the Moon. It is time to return to Kalimdor and advance your calling. At the heart of Darnassus stands the Temple of the Moon, center of night elf faith and leadership. Priestess Alathea and High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind oversee the Sisterhood’s instruction, watching their disciples even when curiosity carries them overseas. When you return, the priestesses welcome you with motherly concern and immediately set you to deeper studies of the Moon Goddess’s celestial mysteries.

quest:5629.text: Returning Home. In Darnassus, Returning Home brings young night elf priests before the leaders of their faith. After proving themselves in Teldrassil’s wilds, they are summoned to the Temple of the Moon to meet Priestess Alathea and High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. Priests tending the wounded and cleansing corruption around Dolanaar draw the Sisterhood of Elune’s notice. Trainer Laurna Morninglight intercepts promising initiates with word that Priestess Alathea has asked to meet them. Aid to local settlements matters, but each devotee must also deepen their communion with the Moon Mother and answer the faith’s higher calling. The road leads from Teldrassil’s boughs to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. The sanctuary rises above the city in Elune’s gentle glow. It is the kaldorei’s chief house of worship and spiritual capital. An invitation into its halls means an initiate is recognized by the priesthood’s leaders, no longer treated only as a young student. Priestess Alathea greets returning initiates warmly. She says she and High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind take pride when initiates venture into the uncertain world and return unharmed. This homecoming begins deeper sacred trials under Alathea’s direct guidance.

quest:5630.text: Returning Home. A summons reaches wandering night elf priests in Dun Morogh, calling them back to Darnassus. Maxan Anvol, the dwarven priest trainer, directs them to report to Priestess Alathea at the Temple of the Moon. In Kharanos, Maxan Anvol takes note of the night elf's fortitude amid Dun Morogh's bitter cold, far from Teldrassil's serene forests. The dwarven priest trainer brings urgent word: a priestess of Elune passed through looking for the elf, carrying orders from Darnassus that demand an immediate return. The road leads across the sea to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, among Teldrassil's sacred boughs. Priestess Alathea welcomes the traveler back to the Sisterhood of Elune, relieved to see another devotee return unscathed from foreign lands. She swiftly prepares the priest for the next rites of devotion, beginning with the Stars of Elune.

quest:5631.text: Returning Home. In human lands, a night elf priest receives a summons to return to Teldrassil. Brother Joshua delivers the message from Priestess Alathea, who calls the young priest to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus for advanced guidance in Elune’s mysteries. Night elf priests sometimes travel to human lands such as Stormwind to share spiritual fellowship with the Church of the Holy Light. Their deepest ties remain with the Sisterhood of Elune. Brother Joshua tells an acolyte that a night elf emissary has come searching for them. Their early travels are over, and their home temple calls them back for deeper training with High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind’s inner circle. Across the sea, Darnassus welcomes the returning priest at the Temple of the Moon. Priestess Alathea greets the acolyte warmly and celebrates their safe passage through a troubled world. Their return brings joy to Alathea and Tyrande, while more demanding spiritual trials await.

quest:5632.text: Returning Home. Priestess Alathea calls promising night elf priests back to Darnassus. The summons brings them to the Temple of the Moon to be recognized by the Sisterhood of Elune and receive advanced guidance. A messenger from the Sisterhood reaches you while you visit Nara Meideros in Stormwind's Park. You have served your people abroad, and the order's leaders now require you in Darnassus. They have watched your spiritual growth and call you back for an evaluation and a rite of recognition. The journey marks your passage from a new initiate to an active servant of the Mother Moon. The summons sends you to Priestess Alathea at the Temple of the Moon, Darnassus's highest sanctuary. High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind oversees the Sisterhood, which watches over its members wherever they serve. Your safe return to the temple honors your community and Elune. It also shows that the goddess's grace has guided and preserved you through your early trials in the wild.

quest:5633.text: Returning Home. Night elf priests in Ironforge are called back to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. A Sisterhood emissary seeks out acolytes abroad and sends them to Priestess Alathea for urgent training and sacred duties. In Ironforge, night elf priests remain tied to the Sisterhood of Elune, though they are far from Teldrassil. Braenna Flintcrag, a dwarven priest trainer in the Mystic Ward, carries a message from a visiting night elf priestess. The messenger sought young disciples traveling abroad and said their mentors needed them back in the capital at once. At the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, returning acolytes report to Priestess Alathea. Beneath the watchful gaze of High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind, Alathea welcomes her student and is relieved they crossed the seas safely. Their return begins further devotion and sacred duties, including the Stars of Elune.

quest:5634.text: Desperate Prayer. In Stormwind, human priests seek a prayer for their own hour of need. At the Cathedral of Light, High Priestess Laurena teaches acolytes to call on the Holy Light when their lives are at risk. Priests in the Cathedral of Light learn to use their faith to shield companions, heal wounds, and strike at evil. Yet even the devout can be isolated, cornered, or brought close to death. In such moments, an acolyte may cry out to the Holy Light for help, with their own survival at stake. High Priestess Laurena guides clergy in Stormwind's Cathedral Square and judges when an acolyte is ready for deeper teachings. Human initiates who show devotion to the Light across the kingdom receive this lesson as both protection and a charge to continue serving the realm.

quest:5635.text: Desperate Prayer. Promising priests from Elwynn Forest are summoned to Stormwind for further training in the Church of the Holy Light. After proving their devotion and discipline, they come before High Priestess Laurena at the Cathedral of Light. Priestess Josetta guides novice priests in Goldshire, while other local mentors serve the outlying settlements of Elwynn Forest. When a disciple proves capable in spirit and deeds, word reaches the senior priesthood in Stormwind. A summons to the Cathedral of Light marks the move to deeper responsibilities in the faith and formal training at the spiritual heart of the Kingdom of Stormwind. At the Cathedral, acolytes present themselves to High Priestess Laurena, one of the Church's senior leaders in Stormwind. She oversees their spiritual grounding and practical training as newly elevated priests. Her instruction prepares them for the harsh trials facing the Alliance and teaches the Light's miracles, including Desperate Prayer, the plea for salvation known among human practitioners.

quest:5636.text: Desperate Prayer. In Dolanaar, Laurna Morninglight sends human priests home to Stormwind for further training. A fellow priest has crossed continents to summon them to the Cathedral of Light. In Dolanaar, Priestess Laurna Morninglight brings you word from home. A fellow priest has crossed continents to find you, and Laurna urges you to return without delay. She offers Elune’s blessing and good wishes for your faith as you leave Teldrassil. Your path leads across the Great Sea to Stormwind City’s Cathedral of Light. High Priestess Laurena guides the Alliance faithful in their spiritual growth. She summons promising acolytes to deepen their devotion and learn Desperate Prayer, an emergency prayer that can save a life in a darkest hour.

quest:5637.text: Desperate Prayer. In Stormwind, dwarven priests are called to deepen their service to the Light. High Priestess Laurena summons promising acolytes from Dun Morogh to the Cathedral of Light. There they take on wider duties among the Alliance. Dwarven priests trained in Dun Morogh can outgrow the lessons of local mentors like Maxan Anvol in Kharanos. When an acolyte shows promise, High Priestess Laurena sends a formal summons from the Cathedral of Light. Her attention means the young priest is ready for deeper study and greater duties in the faith. Ironforge keeps its own holy traditions in the Mystic Ward, while Stormwind's Church of the Holy Light welcomes humans and dwarves alike. The journey south by Deeprun Tram brings dwarven acolytes into the wider church community and strengthens the spiritual bond between the allied kingdoms.

quest:5638.text: Desperate Prayer. In Stormwind, a summons carries a young priest from the Park to the Cathedral of Light. Nara Meideros sends you to High Priestess Laurena for further instruction. In Stormwind’s Park, Nara Meideros keeps faith with Elune. The city’s spiritual guides share ties across their different traditions. When the Cathedral seeks a promising student, Nara sends you across the canals with quiet encouragement. The message brings good tidings, not cause for alarm. At the Cathedral of Light in Cathedral Square, you report to High Priestess Laurena. One of Stormwind’s senior clerical leaders, she guides young acolytes beyond their first prayers. Laurena teaches the sacred invocation called Desperate Prayer, a personal plea for divine aid. It can mend grievous wounds in an instant when a servant of the Light stands near death.

quest:5640.text: Desperate Prayer. In Darnassus, young human and dwarven priests find guidance in another faith. Priestess Alathea teaches the ways of Elune, while followers of the Holy Light are directed to Stormwind. There, High Priestess Laurena welcomes the returning acolyte to the Cathedral of Light. Alliance priests follow different sacred paths. In Darnassus, the priesthood tends to Elune, channeling the moon goddess's radiance and wrath. Priestess Alathea honors Elune and respects the Holy Light, but cannot teach another race the deeper prayers bound to a different devotion. Human and dwarven acolytes who seek those prayers must look elsewhere. Initiates of the Holy Light return home to learn its rites, including the prayer for divine aid in a moment of peril. High Priestess Laurena guides returning priests in Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, beneath its marble arches.

quest:5648.text: Garments of Spirituality. In Razor Hill, Tai'jin sends new priests to prove their healing in the field. They seek Grunt Kor'ja, wounded while standing against Kul Tiras survivors, and tend her injuries. Those who succeed earn ceremonial vestments and recognition among the Horde's spiritual practitioners. South of Razor Hill, the Horde still fights remnants of Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's forces. Tai'jin, the troll priest trainer, tests new priests in the work of real combat triage. She sends them to find Grunt Kor'ja, a warrior badly wounded while repelling human infiltrators. You tend her injuries and strengthen her before she succumbs. Healing Kor'ja proves a young priest is ready to serve the Horde's spiritual tradition. Tai'jin awards the Garments of Spirituality for saving a frontline defender. To orcs and Darkspear trolls alike, the robes mark their wearer as more than an apprentice of incantations: they can be trusted to keep Horde warriors alive in battle.

quest:5649.text: In Favor of Spirituality. Young Darkspear priests leave the Valley of Trials under Ken'jai's direction. They report to Tai'jin in Razor Hill and take their first steps into Durotar's wider challenges. Their path balances ancestral troll heritage with life in the Horde. Darkspear acolytes leave the Valley of Trials after learning their basic rites under Ken'jai. The paths out of the secluded training grounds lead to Razor Hill, a crossroads settlement in Durotar. For a young priest, the journey marks a step beyond basic survival drills and toward the spiritual and cultural responsibilities of the tribe. Ken'jai speaks plainly about the Darkspear's place in Thrall's Horde. The trolls value the orcs' loyalty and lessons of honor, yet some ancestral traditions sit uneasily among their allies. Darkspear spiritual leaders teach their pupils to preserve their heritage quietly while serving the Horde. At Razor Hill, Tai'jin welcomes the acolytes and guides them toward self-sufficiency and strength within the community.

quest:5654.text: Hex of Weakness. In Durotar, Hex of Weakness carries a young Darkspear priest from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar. Tai'jin sends an initiate north to Ur'kyo, who welcomes new students into the tribe's spiritual circle and teaches the loa's darker arts. Young Darkspear priests continue their lessons in Razor Hill's barracks under Tai'jin's watch. Once an acolyte shows command of spiritual communion and shadow magic, the first lessons end. Tai'jin sends the promising priest north, across Durotar's red dirt canyons, toward the Horde capital. There, elder practitioners guide the tribe's wider magical traditions. The Darkspear keep a distinct cultural sanctuary in Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits, apart from the orcs' clanging forges and warrior grounds. Ur'kyo, an elder priest, waits there for new initiates. Joining his circle means embracing the ancestral traditions of the jungle trolls: honoring the loa while learning potent curses and hexes that sap an enemy's strength in battle.

quest:5713.text: One Shot. One Kill.. On the road to Auberdine, Sentinel Aynasha needs help to survive an ambush and deliver her message. Marosh the Devious and his furbolg trackers have poisoned her, leaving her unable to travel while she mixes an antidote. Sentinel Aynasha was carrying important communications toward Auberdine when hostile furbolgs intercepted her on a northern Kalimdor trail. Marosh the Devious led the pack. Their venom left the scout unsteady and unable to continue on foot. Aynasha knows how to make natural remedies, but mixing and taking an antidote takes time. Marosh's trackers are closing in, so she needs travelers to guard her while she works. Though her strength is failing, she keeps her bow steady and fires into the brush to hold the attackers back.

quest:5722.text: Searching for the Lost Satchel. Rahauro sends you from Thunder Bluff’s Elder Rise into Ragefire Chasm. Magatha Grimtotem seeks her lost emissary Maur and the unusual discovery he made among the troggs. Magatha Grimtotem hears on Thunder Bluff’s Elder Rise that her emissary, Maur Grimtotem, entered the cavern beneath Orgrimmar to study the troggs and try to parley with them. He never returned, and rumors say he found something unusual shortly before his death. While Warchief Thrall and his advisers focus on the Shadow Council presence in Ragefire Chasm, the Grimtotem clan follows its own interests.

quest:5723.text: Testing an Enemy's Strength. Magatha Grimtotem seeks retribution after troggs slaughter her emissaries beneath Orgrimmar. Rahauro on Thunder Bluff’s Elder Rise sends warriors into Ragefire Chasm to cull the troggs infesting it. Magatha Grimtotem sent tauren emissaries into the fiery depths beneath Orgrimmar to make peace with the troggs. The creatures slaughtered the delegates as soon as they arrived. Magatha saw the massacre as an insult to the tauren and a growing danger to the Horde. She resolved to answer it with force. Rahauro carries out Magatha’s orders from Thunder Bluff. He directs warriors into Ragefire Chasm to find and kill trogg warriors and shamans. The Horde strikes deep into their underground home to thin their numbers before they can pour through their tunnels into Orgrimmar.

quest:5724.text: Returning the Lost Satchel. In Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar, the search for Maur Grimtotem ends with his satchel. You must carry it back to Rahauro on Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff. Maur Grimtotem was slain by troggs in the fiery depths of Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar. Even in death, his arms clung to his personal satchel. Freeing it from his grip is the only clue to why a member of the Grimtotem clan entered the volcanic caverns beneath Thrall's capital.

quest:5725.text: The Power to Destroy.... In the Undercity, Varimathras sends Horde adventurers into Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner wants two dark tomes held by the Searing Blade cult, hoping their power will aid her war against the Scourge and the Lich King. Thrall's orcs are hunting the Searing Blade cult beneath their capital, while the Forsaken covet the cult's occult stores. On Sylvanas Windrunner's orders, Varimathras sends operatives into Ragefire Chasm to seize two demonic grimoires: Spells of Shadow and Incantations from the Nether. The Dark Lady believes disciplined Forsaken will can put these demonic gifts to better use than the lesser cultists. Varimathras explains the tomes' purpose once they are secured. Their dark magic is meant to strengthen Sylvanas's campaign against the Scourge. By claiming every scrap of forbidden power, the Forsaken hope to break the Lich King's hold across Lordaeron and free the remaining undead from his mental enslavement.

quest:5727.text: Hidden Enemies. Thrall sends you into Orgrimmar to learn what the Burning Blade knows. After cult activity is found at Skull Rock, you carry a lieutenant's insignia to Neeru Fireblade and test his loyalties. Thrall turns to cunning instead of striking at the Cleft of Shadow. He knows Neeru Fireblade pretends to serve the Horde while aiding the cultists in secret. If Thrall strikes now, Neeru's masters will be warned and the trail into the conspiracy may end. So Thrall gives you an insignia taken from the cult in Durotar and asks you to pose as an initiate, to learn what Neeru knows.

quest:5728.text: Hidden Enemies. Thrall sends you against the Searing Blade beneath Orgrimmar. After tricking Neeru Fireblade into believing you are an ally, he sends you into Ragefire Chasm to assassinate the cult's top commanders. Orgrimmar was built as a haven for a free Orcish race, but its foundations conceal an old demonic threat. Beneath the markets, the Cleft of Shadow opens onto the tunnels of Ragefire Chasm. In those volcanic depths, remnants of the Shadow Council called the Searing Blade gather strength. They practice dark arts and scheme to seize the young Horde from within its own capital.

quest:5729.text: Hidden Enemies. Thrall's watch on Hidden Enemies reaches into the Cleft of Shadow. After Bazzalan and Jergosh the Invoker are killed beneath the city, Thrall sends you to win Neeru Fireblade's trust. Thrall sees a chance after Bazzalan and Jergosh the Invoker are killed in Ragefire Chasm. He chooses not to expose Neeru Fireblade. Neeru has lost his underground lieutenants, leaving the local cult without its leaders. Thrall sends you back to the Cleft of Shadow to offer yourself as an ally who can fill that gap.

quest:5730.text: Hidden Enemies. Neeru Fireblade has earned your trust, and Thrall awaits your report in Orgrimmar. The Warchief needs to know how far the Burning Blade's reach extends across Kalimdor.

quest:5761.text: Slaying the Beast. In Orgrimmar’s Cleft of Shadow, Neeru Fireblade sends Horde adventurers into Ragefire Chasm to hunt Taragaman the Hungerer. He claims Warchief Thrall ordered the hunt and demands the towering felguard’s heart as proof the demonic cult has fallen. Ragefire Chasm lies beneath Orgrimmar’s red earthen streets, a fiery fissure filled with troggs, beasts, and covert Searing Blade agents. In the Cleft of Shadow above, Neeru Fireblade presents himself as a loyal servant carrying out Thrall’s order to cleanse this demonic rot. He points to Taragaman the Hungerer, a massive felguard in the cavern’s heart, and names him as the mastermind behind the cult below the city.

quest:579.text: Stormwind Library. In Stormwind Keep, Donyal Tovald copies the kingdom’s histories for those with library scrips. Young King Anduin Wrynn has set aside royal funds for the work, opening these accounts of Azeroth to citizens and scholars. While Highlord Bolvar Fordragon and Lady Katrana Prestor guide Stormwind’s defenses and court in King Varian’s absence, young King Anduin turns royal support toward learning. He funds copies of ancient manuscripts and historical journals, so the kingdom’s past can be preserved and studied. Within Stormwind Keep, the Royal Library keeps these written accounts and copies them for those in royal service. Hand copying delicate parchment takes time, ink, and royal sanction. Librarian Donyal Tovald accepts official library scrips issued to adventurers and scholars across Alliance territories. In return, he provides copies of historical works, from the ancient histories of the Eastern Kingdoms to accounts of distant lands, offering knowledge of conflicts beyond the capital.

quest:59.text: Cloth and Leather Armor. In Goldshire, Cloth and Leather Armor sends a trusted traveler east for gear. Marshal Dughan issues an armor marker redeemable with Sara Timberlain at Eastvale Logging Camp. The trip carries recruits beyond Guard Thomas's bridge to obtain armor for the realm's defense. Guard Thomas watches Elwynn's eastern river crossing, where murlocs and gnolls threaten the border. After you carry his report to Goldshire, Marshal Dughan recognizes your service with an official Stormwind Armor Marker. Goldshire's garrison has meager stores, so Dughan gives you a marker instead of drawing equipment from them. The marker is a military voucher that records your service to the crown. East of Guard Thomas's bridge lies Eastvale Logging Camp, Elwynn's main timber operation. Sara Timberlain works there under an official commission from the Stormwind Army to make cloth and leather gear. The kingdom's central armories are strained, leaving local artisans like Sara to outfit troops and auxiliary scouts on the frontier.

quest:5921.text: Moonglade. In Darnassus, young night elf druids learn to reach Moonglade. Mathrengyl Bearwalker teaches novices a spell to carry themselves across the world into Moonglade, where they meet Dendrite Starblaze in Nighthaven. There begins their path toward mastering bear form. Moonglade is an ancient sanctuary apart from the rest of Azeroth, devoted to the teachings of Cenarius. Keeper Remulos watches over its groves, where druids find peace and communion with nature. Young druids learn a spell that lets them carry themselves across the world into Moonglade, reaching a heart of druidic wisdom beyond mortal distances. Moonglade welcomes all who follow the wild, though the Cenarion Circle knows its share of tension. In Darnassus, Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm and Keeper Remulos disagree over nature’s care and the creation of Teldrassil. Their differences do not close Nighthaven to young acolytes, who are welcomed to pursue their studies. In Nighthaven, Dendrite Starblaze guides young druids in the ways of the Claw. Before an initiate can take up the bear’s mantle, the trials teach the bear’s endurance, fury, and defense of the wild. Starblaze welcomes each student in reverence to Father Cenarius as the trials of the Great Bear Spirit begin.

quest:5931.text: Back to Darnassus. After meeting the Great Bear Spirit, a young night elf druid returns to Darnassus. The initiate has left Moonglade and now reports to Mathrengyl Bearwalker in the Cenarion Enclave for practical shapeshifting trials. Dendrite Starblaze sends the initiate from Nighthaven back to Darnassus after the meeting with the Great Bear Spirit in Moonglade. The journey joins two sanctuaries: Moonglade, where the young druid has communed with the spirit, and the unsettled world beyond. In Darnassus, local mentors watch over Teldrassil and guide the next stage of training. Mathrengyl Bearwalker waits in the Cenarion Enclave, where he guards nature even as its balance falters. The Great Bear Spirit's blessing is only the first step. Mathrengyl prepares the initiate for trials of body and heart, to give physical form to the spirit's fierce ancestral wisdom.

quest:6.text: Bounty on Garrick Padfoot. In Northshire, an Alliance bounty names Garrick Padfoot, a notorious local thief. Deputy Willem at Northshire Abbey calls for recruits to hunt him near the vineyards. Northshire Valley once offered a safe place to train recruits and tend its sacred vineyards. As order falters across Elwynn, thieves have reached the valley. Garrick Padfoot, a cutthroat, quickly rose to lead them. For weeks, he and his gang have plundered shipments, robbed merchants on the roads, and threatened local farmers. Stormwind's guards are stretched thin, protecting the capital and its outer borders. Local marshals and deputies rely on volunteers to keep Northshire peaceful. Deputy Willem places a public bounty on Garrick's head, hoping to rid the valley of his gang. Bringing Padfoot down at his rundown shack east of the river strikes at the lawlessness spreading through the human heartland.

quest:60.text: Kobold Candles. At the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, William Pestle seeks candles from kobolds that have overstocked Elwynn Forest's mines. Visiting from his shop in Stormwind, the alchemist needs their thick wax, and the errand introduces adventurers to the subterranean pests encroaching on the kingdom's valuable gold veins. William Pestle runs Pestle's Apothecary with his brother in Stormwind City's Trade District. Wax is always in short supply as he brews remedies, ointments, and concoctions. Instead of buying polished candles from city merchants, Pestle turns to the vermin in Elwynn. The kobolds carry hefty lumps of tallow and wax on their brows, ready for an adventurer willing to pry them loose. Kobolds have overrun Fargodeep Mine south of Goldshire and Jasperlode Mine to the northeast. These snuffling creatures prize their candles above almost all else. The flickering flames guide them through dark shafts as they dig for gold and shiny trinkets. Taking the candles replenishes Pestle's alchemy stocks and chips away at the vermin choking off the kingdom's precious mining claims.

quest:6001.text: Body and Heart. In Darnassus, a young night elf druid nears the end of initiation into the path of the claw. Mathrengyl Bearwalker sends the initiate into Darkshore to summon Lunaclaw and prove strength of body and heart before taking the form of the bear. Mathrengyl Bearwalker sends night elf druid initiates east of Auberdine, the coastal settlement in Darkshore. A natural cavern there shelters wild moonkin and an ancient Moonkin Stone. Anointing the sacred stone with Cenarion Moondust awakens Lunaclaw, its ancient defender. The guardian challenges any initiate who seeks the sacred strength of the claw.

quest:6062.text: Taming the Beast. In Razor Hill, Taming the Beast begins a young Horde hunter’s training with a taming rod. Thotar guides aspiring hunters as they face a vicious dire mottled boar. Orc and Darkspear troll hunters in Durotar must learn to command the wild as well as survive it. Thotar, the veteran hunter trainer, gives young hunters an enchanted taming rod and sends them to face a fierce wild boar. They must subdue the beast without killing it, then make it a loyal ally. Dire mottled boars roam the dry brush around Razor Hill. Their strength and temper make them a fitting first test for young hunters. The rod can subdue a charging boar, but using it takes patience and resolve, qualities every Horde tracker needs.

quest:6063.text: Taming the Beast. In Dolanaar, Taming the Beast begins a night elf hunter’s trials with a wild Webwood Lurker. Dazalar lends an enchanted taming rod, and the hunter must win the spider’s trust through a bond with nature. For the kaldorei, hunting means more than tracking prey or surviving in the wild. It binds a hunter to nature, which is greater than any mortal. Animals are independent creatures, not tools to bend to a hunter’s will. Dazalar teaches novice hunters to meet them with respect. Before gaining a lifelong beast companion, a hunter must master local wildlife through ancient techniques, never brute force. Giant arachnids infest Teldrassil’s boughs, and Dazalar gives the hunter a taming rod. The hunter seeks a Webwood Lurker in the shadowed thickets, facing the venomous spider and its attacks while trying to reach it through empathy. A brief mental bond proves the hunter can commune with the World Tree’s eerie, skittering predators.

quest:6068.text: The Hunter's Path. In Durotar, The Hunter's Path sends young orc and troll hunters to Razor Hill. There, Thotar teaches them to bind wild predators. In Durotar, young hunters learn to track prey with bow and cunning. Following trails through red clay canyons and harsh scrubland teaches patience. To master the hunter's way in the Horde, they must also learn to bond with the land's wild beasts. When class trainers judge a student ready, they direct them to Razor Hill. Thotar waits at Razor Hill, where he teaches young hunters how to subdue Durotar's fierce beasts without breaking their spirit. Learning from him begins the path to traveling the wilderness with a loyal companion.

quest:6081.text: Training the Beast. In Durotar, young orc and troll hunters are sent to learn from veteran master hunter Ormak Grimshot. After proving themselves with the plains beasts, they travel from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar. There they learn to care for, feed, and train a lifelong animal companion. In Durotar's arid canyon lands, skill with a bow and survival in the harsh wilds are only part of a hunter's duty. Young hunters first tame the plains beasts: fierce boars, crab scavengers, and armored scorpid stalkers. Once they prove their resilience, Thotar sends them from Razor Hill north through the red clay gulches to Orgrimmar's fortified gates, ready to take responsibility for a companion. Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor is an enclave where veteran stalkers and warriors hone their craft. There, aspiring hunters seek Ormak Grimshot, one of the Horde's revered master hunters. He looks beyond their youth to judge whether they have the patience to command a beast and sustain and nurture it through famine, battle, and loss. A beast won through force remains wild until hunter and companion come to understand one another. Ormak teaches the sacred traditions that keep their bond: which foods nourish each creature's spirit, how discipline teaches a beast lethal techniques, and the spiritual focus needed to revive one that falls in the line of duty.

quest:6082.text: Taming the Beast. In Durotar, Taming the Beast tests a young Horde hunter's skill with wild creatures. Thotar in Razor Hill guides the hunter through one last trial: taming a dangerous armored scorpid. Success brings the ability to tame, call, and dismiss a lasting companion. Before a hunter can travel Kalimdor with an animal companion, they must prove they can command Durotar's harsh wildlife. Thotar, the hunter trainer in Razor Hill, sends trainees to subdue three kinds of creature with an enchanted taming rod. After facing dire boars and swift surf crawlers, they must now tame an armored scorpid, a venomous predator protected by heavy plates and known for resilience and speed. Taming an armored scorpid tests a hunter's focus and control under attack, not their skill at killing. Thotar urges hunters to match the beast's quick, confident strikes. Once the hunter has charmed the scorpid, they return to Razor Hill and give the taming rod back to Thotar. That return completes the trial, and Thotar then teaches the wild's innate techniques, letting the hunter seek out and bind a permanent companion of their choosing.

quest:6083.text: Taming the Beast. In Durotar, Taming the Beast sends young hunters to the coast for their second trial. Thotar, the hunter trainer in Razor Hill, directs aspiring orc and troll hunters to pacify a surf crawler near the Echo Isles and extend their bond to coastal wildlife. After mastering a dire mottled boar, you turn your attention to the sea at Thotar's direction. Durotar's harsh shores are jagged, and shallow reefs teem with armored crustaceans. A surf crawler resists intrusion into its coastal domain, so taming one calls for patience and fortitude. Thotar teaches that a bound beast must become an extension of a hunter's strength. Subduing a surf crawler with the taming rod teaches you to command creatures of different temperaments in different surroundings. It proves you are ready for permanent companions.

quest:61.text: Shipment to Stormwind. William Pestle sends a parcel from Goldshire to his brother Morgan in Stormwind. Its candles carry wax supplies from Elwynn Forest to Pestle's Apothecary in the Trade District. William gathers herbs, reagents, and raw goods in Goldshire, while his brother Morgan runs Pestle's Apothecary in Stormwind's Trade District. William cannot easily leave his post at the Lion's Pride Inn, so he depends on travelers heading into the city to carry goods for him. William's parcel holds large candles gathered from kobolds in Elwynn's mines. He says he collects them for their wax. Delivering the shipment brings those supplies to Morgan at Pestle's Apothecary in the Trade District.

quest:6101.text: Taming the Beast. Dazalar guides a night elf hunter through a second trial in Dolanaar. With an enchanted taming rod, you subdue a nightsaber stalker and learn how wild beasts differ. Dazalar teaches you that the forest's creatures do not all behave alike. Each species has its own temperament, and a hunter must learn to meet it on its own terms. Beneath Teldrassil's canopy, the next test brings you against beasts more cunning and predatory than webspinners. Kaldorei revere nightsabers as sacred predators, fierce guardians, and companions of the Sentinels. With the taming rod, you face a nightsaber stalker and must keep a steady nerve and calm authority. Winning its trust shows you can handle a predator, not only the more docile creatures of the woods.

quest:6102.text: Taming the Beast. In Dolanaar, Taming the Beast brings a young night elf hunter to the final trial of basic training. Under Dazalar’s direction, hunters tame a predatory owl of the skies before gaining the power to choose a lifelong companion. Night elf hunters must make peace with creatures across Teldrassil before their basic beastcraft is complete. After proving their will against beasts of the underbrush, they face the spirit of the skies, the Strigid Screecher. These watchful birds of prey roost high in the boughs west of Dolanaar. Patience and a steady nerve are needed to pacify one with the enchanted Taming Rod. Taming the Strigid Screecher fulfills the ancient lessons of communion between kaldorei hunters and nature. When the apprentice returns the spent rod to Dazalar, the training exercises end. The apprentice earns the full art of calling, dismissing, and permanently taming beasts of their own choosing across Azeroth.

quest:6103.text: Training the Beast. In Teldrassil, Training the Beast sends night elf hunters from the wilds to Darnassus. After taming beasts among the boughs, they learn pet care and discipline from Jocaste. Dazalar sends you from the wilds near Dolanaar to Darnassus once you prove you can tame a beast. Before you travel Kalimdor with a loyal companion, you need to learn more than how to use a taming rod. Subduing a wild creature tests your strength and will, but an untrained beast can still be unpredictable. Jocaste teaches you the arts of caring for a companion in Darnassus's Cenarion Enclave. She shows you how to feed your pet, bring it back if tragedy strikes, and train it to fight. For night elves, this bond reflects reverence for nature, not simple control.

quest:6121.text: Lessons Anew. Mathrengyl Bearwalker sends Alliance druids from Darnassus to Moonglade for training. There, Dendrite Starblaze begins their instruction in cleansing venom and toxins. Druids learn from Cenarius, the demigod whose teachings and blessings bind them to the living world. His gifts include the power to cleanse venom with a simple incantation. Such power is not given lightly. Before young druids can wield it, they must learn the hard, ordinary work of fighting toxins without nature's magic. Mathrengyl Bearwalker trains druids in Darnassus's Cenarion Enclave. He sends his student past local practice and on to Moonglade. In Nighthaven, Dendrite Starblaze coordinates the Cenarion Circle's wider efforts and has practical work for the novice.

quest:6122.text: The Principal Source. At Cliffspring Falls, a sickness among Darkshore's deer draws the Cenarion Circle's attention to the water. Dendrite Starblaze sends young druids from Moonglade to collect a sample for Auberdine naturalist Alanndarian Nightsong. Cliffspring Falls feeds northern Darkshore with fresh water. When deer began to sicken with a lingering malady, the Cenarion Circle looked to the river for its cause. Dendrite Starblaze in Moonglade suspects the water source is tainted and sends novice druids to gather a sample at the cavern mouth beneath the falls. Vicious naga dwell inside Cliffspring River Cave, near the falls' headwaters. Their presence threatens anyone trying to investigate the blight. The Cenarion Circle needs a sample from the cave mouth to study what is making the wilderness sick.

quest:6124.text: Curing the Sick. Darkshore’s deer are sick, and Curing the Sick asks you to bring them relief. Alanndarian Nightsong gives you salve to treat the poisoned animals before you report to the Cenarion Circle in Moonglade. In Darkshore, deer fall sick from the Cliffspring River south to the border of Ashenvale. They wander the misty woods, weakened by toxins in the soil and streams. After you gather the needed reagents, Alanndarian Nightsong gives you freshly brewed animal salve to treat the afflicted deer.

quest:6125.text: Power over Poison. In Darnassus, a young druid returns to complete Power over Poison. The Cenarion Circle's trial began in Darkshore, where the initiate learned to brew a remedy by hand. In Darkshore, Alanndarian Nightsong asks young druids to gather Earthroot and Lunar Fungus by hand. They brew a salve to heal stricken wildlife. Before granting the magic to purge toxins, the Cenarion Circle wants initiates to know the hardship of treating poison without spiritual aid. The work teaches them what common folk face when venom strikes, and why a druid must meet their suffering with care. After the remedy proves effective in Auberdine, Starblaze sends the druid across the sea to Darnassus. Mathrengyl Bearwalker awaits in the Cenarion Enclave. Pleased with the initiate's grace under pressure, he teaches the art of cleansing toxins through nature's power. But virulent poisons in the wilds around Auberdine trouble him, for they point to an unnatural blight disturbing the land's balance.

quest:6127.text: The Principal Source. Dendrite Starblaze sends Horde druids to Dreadmist Peak for a water sample. From Moonglade, she asks them to bring it to Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads, where it can help explain the poison harming wildlife. Dreadmist Peak rises northwest of the Crossroads, with springs and pools high above the dry northern Barrens. Their waters shape local weather and moisture. The Burning Blade, a cult devoted to demons, has taken hold on the crags. Dendrite Starblaze fears their foul sorcery may taint the basin around this important mountain. Sick gazelles stumble across the northern savanna, north of the main east-west trail through the Crossroads. Tonga Runetotem seeks help for the local tauren and turns to the Cenarion Circle to learn what is poisoning the herd. Druids who reach the peak and bring back a sample of its tainted water give Tonga what he needs to study the sickness and brew an antidote.

quest:6128.text: Gathering the Cure. At the Crossroads, young tauren druids face a sacred passage under Tonga Runetotem's guidance. You gather earthroot and sturdy kodo horns to make a salve for the poisoned gazelles of the Barrens. Tonga Runetotem needs raw ingredients to brew an antidote from the water sample you secured at Dreadmist Peak. Natural water forms the salve's base, earthroot supplies its medicinal qualities, and ground kodo horn gives it the strength to drive venom from a creature's system. For a young druid, gathering them means relying on the gifts of the earth and hunting local beasts. Tonga Runetotem uses the salve's preparation to teach the limits of physical medicine. Herbal lore and alchemy can counter specific toxins, but each poison usually needs its own cure. Rather than carry endless herbs and horns, druids learn to attune to nature's healing energies. That lesson leads to the druidic art of Cure Poison.

quest:62.text: The Fargodeep Mine. Kobolds have overrun The Fargodeep Mine south of Goldshire, between the Stonefield and Maclure farms. The mine's fall points to a growing pest problem across Elwynn Forest. While Northshire Valley faces its own vermin, reports reach Goldshire that kobolds have claimed another vital site. Between the feuding Stonefield and Maclure homesteads south of town, the Fargodeep Mine once supplied stone and ore for the realm. Now shrill chattering and tallow candles fill its damp tunnels. Marshal Dughan sends you to scout the depths and learn how bad the trouble is. The report of kobolds in the mine adds to the Stormwind Guard's strain. Its troops are already stretched thin defending against Defias bandits and gnoll incursions, leaving too few to clear the tunnels. When Dughan hears the report, he worries about other mineral sites, including the Jasperlode Mine to the northeast.

quest:6261.text: Dungar Longdrink. At Stormwind's Trade District roost, Dungar Longdrink arranges swift gryphon transport for supplies bound to Westfall's embattled defenders. Defias outlaws and feral harvest golems have pushed Westfall close to breaking point. Quartermaster Lewis and the People's Militia are desperate for provisions. Lewis sent word to the capital, and armorer Osric Strang packed the requested equipment. Carrying military cargo on foot through bandit-ridden Elwynn and Westfall takes precious time. Stormwind's new aerial routes offer a vital link to the frontier. The gryphon roost sits in Stormwind's Trade District, where Dungar Longdrink coordinates courier and passenger flights. Wildhammer dwarves traditionally raise and handle these majestic beasts. They carry people and cargo across human lands when roosts at both ends know the route. Bringing Osric's heavy crate straight to Dungar teaches couriers how aerial logistics work. It connects the capital's stockpiles directly to frontier outposts such as Sentinel Hill.

quest:6281.text: Continue to Stormwind. You carry a requisition from Sentinel Hill to Stormwind by gryphon, where Osric Strang awaits in Old Town. Quartermaster Lewis prepares a requisition note in Sentinel Hill. The local gryphon master Thor offers you the fastest way out of the contested plains. For a modest fee, you ride one of the kingdom's trained gryphons above dusty farmlands and the river border of Elwynn Forest, then over Stormwind City's high white ramparts. After you land at the capital's trade roosts, you head into Old Town to find Osric Strang at his shop, Limited Immunity. Osric supplies the frontier, but his grim reception shows the growing rift between Westfall's beleaguered People's Militia and the distracted rulers in Stormwind Keep.

quest:6285.text: Return to Lewis. Dungar Longdrink sends armor from Stormwind to the People's Militia at Sentinel Hill. Osric's Crate crosses Elwynn and Westfall by gryphon, carrying supplies to defenders under pressure. Westfall is slipping from the kingdom's grasp. Defias bandits, ravenous gnolls, and mechanical harvest reapers threaten the land. Overland supply routes face harassment, and roads are dangerous for solitary wagons. The flight master network offers a crucial lifeline. Osric, an armorer in Stormwind's Old Town, prepared a heavy crate of armor for the battered volunteers of the People's Militia at Sentinel Hill. Gryphons are loyal, well-trained beasts, but travel across the lands depends on established familiarity. Dungar Longdrink explains that gryphons instinctively know how to return to their capital roost in Stormwind. To carry a rider to a remote outpost, though, they need the traveler to have met its flight master in person. You have already checked in with Thor at Sentinel Hill, opening the skies over the frontier to rapid travel. At Sentinel Hill, Quartermaster Lewis receives the crate. He is the officer tasked with outfitting Gryan Stoutmantle's volunteer force, and he sets to work distributing the armor among the frontier defenders. For Sentinel Hill, reliable aerial contact with the capital can mean the difference between holding the line and being overrun by the Defias Brotherhood.

quest:6341.text: The Bounty of Teldrassil. Nessa Shadowsong is sending fish samples from Rut'theran Village to Auberdine for comparison. She wants to learn whether Teldrassil's fish are larger and more plentiful than those along the mainland coast. Nessa Shadowsong asks you to carry fish bones and scales to Laird in Auberdine. Fishers in Rut'theran Village bring in large, plentiful catches, and she wants to know whether the mainland waters yield the same kind of fish. The samples will let Laird compare the island catch with fish from the coast of Darkshore. Nessa Shadowsong sends you to Vesprystus, the hippogryph master in Rut'theran Village, with the collection for Auberdine. Carrying the samples to him arranges your passage across the water to Darkshore.

quest:6342.text: Flight to Auberdine. You leave Teldrassil for Auberdine with a bundle of unusual fish specimens. Vesprystus sends you from Rut'theran Village by hippogryph to deliver them to Laird. Rut'theran Village is a sanctuary at the edge of the wider world for young adventurers leaving Teldrassil. A mundane ferry crosses the strait between the island and mainland Kalimdor, while night elves also travel by bonded hippogryph. Nessa Shadowsong entrusts you with a parcel of rare fish parts, and you take wing to reach the shores of Darkshore. Laird waits for Nessa's findings at the docks of Auberdine. He finds enormous scales as large as fists and a jawbone nearly twice the size of mainland specimens. The waters around the base of the World Tree seem to produce altered or abnormally large life, a curiosity tied to Teldrassil's potent, restless nature.

quest:6343.text: Return to Nessa. You carry Laird's findings from Auberdine back to Nessa Shadowsong in Rut'theran Village. The journey is an introductory errand that teaches young travelers how to cross between Kalimdor and Teldrassil. Laird sends you back across the water with his written observations. He has found stark differences between the fish caught off Darkshore and those near Teldrassil, and suspects the great World Tree changes the local marine life. You can return to Rut'theran Village by hiring a flight from Caylais Moonfeather, the hippogryph master, or by boarding the regular ferry at Auberdine's pier. Nessa Shadowsong receives Laird's reply at Rut'theran Village and is fascinated by the difference in marine life. Fish near the World Tree grow so large that they bring an immediate boon to local fishermen, though the Kaldorei still do not know why. Nessa plans to share the findings with her fellow villagers. For now, she is content to harvest the abundant sea life and watch for whatever forces may be responsible.

quest:6344.text: Nessa Shadowsong. In Darnassus, Mydrannul sends a courier to meet Nessa Shadowsong below the World Tree. The delivery runs from Rut'theran Village to Darkshore, linking the canopy city with the shore. Mydrannul watches over travelers seeking work and purpose in Darnassus. Fishing merchant Nessa Shadowsong needs a package carried across the sea to Darkshore, so Mydrannul directs able couriers toward the coast. Many young night elves begin their journeys among Teldrassil's boughs; this delivery takes them beyond the tree. From the Temple Gardens, the western portal in Darnassus leads down through the World Tree to Rut'theran Village. At the ocean-level roots, fishing docks and hippogryph perches connect Teldrassil with the rest of Kalimdor. Nessa Shadowsong tends her trade there and prepares shipments for Auberdine.

quest:6361.text: A Bundle of Hides. Jahan Hawkwing sends cured hides from the Crossroads to Thunder Bluff for leatherworking. The delivery takes you across central Kalimdor and introduces the Crossroads wind rider roost. Hunters bring game hides and meat to the Crossroads, where Jahan Hawkwing gathers pelts from across the Barrens. The outposts cannot process every raw hide, so he asks travelers to carry them west to Thunder Bluff. Master leatherworkers there can turn the pelts into gear for the Horde. The trail across the Barrens and into Mulgore is rough, and quilboar and predators threaten anyone carrying cargo on foot. Jahan sends you to Devrak, the Crossroads wind rider master. He can take the goods by air aboard a trained wyvern, linking the Horde’s scattered settlements.

quest:6365.text: Meats to Orgrimmar. At the Crossroads, Zargh sends a parcel of Barrens meat toward Orgrimmar. He asks young orc and troll adventurers to carry it to Devrak, the wind rider master, and learn the flight route to the Horde capital. Wildlife fills the Barrens, from zhevras and plainstriders to kodos and thunder lizards. Zargh has prepared choice cuts for a personal delivery to Gryshka, the innkeeper in Orgrimmar's Valley of Strength. Rather than risk the long, dusty trek across the Southfury River into Durotar, he sends runners from the Crossroads to the wind rider perch. Meeting Devrak gives a young Horde warrior a first look at the wind rider flight network. Wind rider masters connect remote outposts like the Crossroads to the Horde's fortified seat of power in Orgrimmar. Devrak prepares you and the cargo for a swift flight over the savannah.

quest:6384.text: Ride to Orgrimmar. A wind rider carries Horde travelers from the Crossroads to Orgrimmar. With Zargh’s fresh cuts of meat in hand, you fly to the capital’s Skytower and deliver them to Innkeeper Gryshka. Devrak sends trained wind riders between the Crossroads and Orgrimmar. The flight crosses the dry Barrens and reaches Durotar’s red cliffs, sparing travelers the hard journey on foot. From high above the dusty canyon trails, the wyverns carry messengers and travelers, along with dispatches and trade goods, straight to the capital. Zargh has prepared fresh cuts of meat for Innkeeper Gryshka in Orgrimmar’s Valley of Strength. From the central Skytower, her inn is a short walk away. Gryshka accepts the parcel and remarks with fondness that Zargh knows how to win a lady’s heart.

quest:6385.text: Doras the Wind Rider Master. Innkeeper Gryshka needs a courier to carry her thanks to Zargh at the Crossroads. She sends travelers to Doras the Wind Rider Master at Orgrimmar's skytower to arrange the flight back to the Barrens. Innkeeper Gryshka sends thanks to Zargh after a shipment of meat arrives safely from the Barrens hunting grounds. With no time to travel through Durotar herself, she trusts the established aerial courier network linking major Horde settlements to carry her letter back across the frontier. At the flight tower in the Valley of Strength, Doras oversees Orgrimmar's wind rider roost. The trained wyverns carry military messages and supplies between the capital and outposts such as the Crossroads, far faster than anyone traveling by foot or kodo cart.

quest:6386.text: Return to the Crossroads.. Gryshka's reply is on its way from Orgrimmar to Zargh at the Crossroads. A wind rider carries it across the distance between Durotar and the Barrens. You carry Gryshka's written reply to Zargh after bringing her a parcel of prime meat in Orgrimmar. Doras, the wind rider master atop Orgrimmar's high bluffs, provides a mount for the return to the Barrens. You have already met Devrak at the Crossroads, so the wyverns know the flight path. The ride crosses the desert sky and saves you the long march overland across the Southfury River. Zargh's courtship has won Gryshka's warm reply. Quality provisions have pleased her, and Zargh celebrates, even musing about an impending wedding. The delivery also brings you back to the Barrens' central hub for travel.

quest:64.text: The Forgotten Heirloom. In Westfall, the Furlbrows have fled their farm, leaving a cherished heirloom behind. Recovering the pocket watch offers them a chance to salvage something personal from the chaos spreading through the region. Farmer Furlbrow and his wife Verna were driven from their Westfall farm by violence. Shouts rose from the pumpkin patches in the night, waking them with little time to gather what they could carry. In the rush to flee, Furlbrow left behind the pocket watch Verna's father gave him on their wedding day. It remains in the wardrobe of their occupied farmhouse. Defias thugs and thieves, including Benny Blaanco, now pick through the abandoned Furlbrow farm. For ordinary folk, returning for a keepsake could mean death. By securing the pocket watch from the wardrobe, you restore a measure of dignity to a family that has lost nearly everything to Westfall's lawlessness.

quest:65.text: The Defias Brotherhood. In Westfall, the Defias Brotherhood's thieves threaten the farms and roads. Gryan Stoutmantle sends you from Sentinel Hill east into Redridge to seek a contact who may know where they hide. Westfall's harvests are gone, and bandits in red bandanas roam the land. Gryan Stoutmantle and the People's Militia hold Sentinel Hill under near-constant attack, but they do not know who directs their enemies. Stoutmantle knows that fighting stray looters will not save the region. He needs to find the cartel's inner circle and learn who commands it. Gryan Stoutmantle sets aside military channels and Stormwind's absent nobles, and calls on someone he knows. He sends trusted adventurers east, past Elwynn and into the Redridge Mountains. In Lakeshire, a quiet village by the lake, Wiley the Black waits on the upper floor of the local inn. The rogue knows the underworld better than any militia captain, and may offer the first lead to the Brotherhood's hideouts.

quest:6541.text: Report to Kadrak. At the Crossroads, Thork sends proven Horde fighters north to report to Kadrak. The orc holds a watch tower near the Ashenvale border and prepares recruits for the fighting ahead. The Crossroads faces quilboar, centaur, and local brigands, while the Horde looks north to Ashenvale's thick forests. Thork directs fighters who have proved themselves in the central Barrens to the northern border tower, where Kadrak is stationed. Kadrak oversees the southern approach to Ashenvale and organizes reinforcements for the Horde's foothold across the border. Splintertree Post and an outpost along the Zoram Strand help the Horde strengthen its presence in the timber-rich woodlands, where native night elves resist them fiercely.

quest:6543.text: The Warsong Reports. Kadrak sends couriers from the northern Barrens to gather reports across Ashenvale. The Warsong Reports carry orders and field observations from outriders near Azshara, Splintertree Post, and the Zoram Strand. Kadrak watches the mountain pass between the northern Barrens and Ashenvale from a fortified tower. The Horde needs the pass because the Barrens cannot supply the timber Orgrimmar requires. The Warsong clan has pushed into the ancient elven forest to reach those supplies. Couriers carry orders between scattered patrols and help keep them in step, while night elf ambushes threaten the wilderness trails. Warsong scouts watch three parts of Ashenvale. On the western coast, a runner at Zoram'gar Outpost watches naga activity and other coastal threats along the Zoram Strand. At Splintertree Post, a scout coordinates defense against Sentinel raids. Farther east, an outrider watches the road toward the shattered ruins of Azshara. Their reports give Kadrak a view of night elf movements and weaknesses along the frontier.

quest:6544.text: Torek's Assault. Torek's Assault is a direct Horde raid launched from the wilds of Ashenvale against the nearby night elf garrison at Silverwing Outpost. Led by the orc raider Torek under orders from Splintertree Post, the strike aims to crush local Sentinel resistance and slay their commander, Duriel Moonfire. It marks one of the most brazen, bloody skirmishes in the ongoing war for Ashenvale's borders. Ashenvale is locked in an escalating border war between the Horde lumber camps and the native night elves. Seeking to break the Alliance's defensive perimeter, Torek gathers a pack of Splintertree raiders just outside Silverwing Outpost. Rather than waiting for a counter-attack, Torek coordinates a head-on charge to shatter the outpost's defenses before the night elves can mount a reinforced campaign against Splintertree Post. Silverwing Outpost stands as a fortified woodland bastion garrisoned by vigilant Silverwing Sentinels and fierce elven warriors. Torek's primary target is their leader, Duriel Moonfire. Bringing down Duriel decapitates the local night elf military hierarchy in the area, allowing the raiders to report a bloody victory back to commander Ertog Ragetusk at Splintertree Post.

quest:6608.text: You Too Good.. Lumak sends you from Orgrimmar to find his friend Nat Pagle. Your skill has outgrown ordinary lessons, and Nat camps on a distant islet south of Theramore Isle. Lumak trains fishers in Orgrimmar's Valley of Honor. He sees that you have learned all he can teach about rod and reel, and admits you are too good for ordinary lessons. To learn the art of artisan fishing, you must seek knowledge beyond the city and the Horde. Lumak sends you to find his human friend, Nat Pagle. He warns you not to harm or eat Nat, despite the friction between the Horde and Alliance across Kalimdor. Nat camps on an islet south of Theramore Isle in Dustwallow Marsh. He keeps clear of politics and cares only whether the fish are biting.

quest:6611.text: To Gadgetzan You Go!. In Orgrimmar, Zamja sends Horde cooks south to learn from an eccentric goblin butcher. Zamja trains cooks in the Drag, where she feeds warriors and travelers passing through Durotar. When a cook has learned every recipe and technique she can teach, Zamja admits she has imparted all her culinary mojo. She sends her seasoned pupil to Tanaris, saying only a master of strange and exotic meats can help a talented cook advance further. In Tanaris, Gadgetzan is a steam-powered trading hub run by the Steamwheedle Cartel. Dirge Quikcleave works inside the town tavern. The eccentric goblin butcher has an unconventional palate and no squeamishness about food. Across Kalimdor, he is known for turning monstrous desert creatures, and sometimes scraps of leather, into hearty meals for hardened adventurers.

quest:6623.text: Horde Trauma. At Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands, Horde Trauma calls skilled medics into front-line surgery. Doctor Gregory Victor, chief physician of the Horde's trauma division, seeks hands able to save lives under extreme pressure. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits, the orc first aid trainer Arnok tells proficient healers that they have caught Doctor Gregory Victor's attention. Victor oversees Horde Trauma from Hammerfall, tucked away in the contested hills of the Arathi Highlands. Arnok regards the summons as the pinnacle of professional advancement for a battlefield surgeon. At Hammerfall, constant skirmishes with Stromgarde's forces and local hostile factions leave Victor inundated with wounded grunts, raiders, and scouts. The chief physician wastes no time welcoming recruits with pleasantries. Instead, he orders newcomers into their scrubs to prove their worth in brutal, fast-paced emergency triage.

quest:6641.text: Vorsha the Lasher. Vorsha the Lasher is a violent hydra terrorizing the Horde's foothold at Zoram'gar Outpost along the coast of Ashenvale. Revering the creature's ferocity, the local naga maintain an offering brazier on an offshore island to honor her. By extinguishing this sacred flame, Horde champions provoke Vorsha and draw her ashore to end her predatory assaults. Zoram'gar Outpost sits on a tenuous strip of coast in northwestern Ashenvale, constantly besieged by hostile wildlife, night elves, and serpentine invaders. Among the most destructive threats prowling the Zoram Strand is Vorsha the Lasher, a gargantuan hydra known for brutal, unprovoked strikes against the outpost. The beast emerges from the surf to crush fortifications and butcher warriors before vanishing back into the deep tides. The nearby naga do not merely tolerate the ravenous hydra; they actively venerate her predatory malice. On a rocky outcrop off the strand, the serpentine fiends keep an offering brazier burning continuously in tribute to Vorsha. Muglash, an orc determined to end the constant harassment of the outpost, realized that defiling this ritual flame would bring the beast surging to the surface in a fury, allowing the defenders to lure her into an ambush rather than waiting for another surprise slaughter.

quest:6962.text: Treats for Great-father Winter. At the Smokywood Pastures display in Orgrimmar, the Greatfather Winter performer is worn out from hearing holiday wishes. He asks you for gingerbread cookies and milk. The Greatfather Winter who greets visitors in the Valley of Strength works for Smokywood Pastures. Long hours listening to citizens speak of festive treats leave him hungry. He turns to passing travelers for warm baking and a cold drink. You can bake the cookies with Holiday Spices sold by Smokywood Pastures peddlers and Small Eggs gathered from wild birds. Bring them together with Ice Cold Milk from a local tavern, and the feast's organizers offer you festive cheer and a small token of gratitude.

quest:6984.text: A Smokywood Pastures' Thank You!. Great-father Winter waits in Orgrimmar to thank those who recovered Smokywood Pastures' stolen holiday treats. Kaymard Copperpinch sends you to receive a token of appreciation for bringing the supplies back. In Orgrimmar, Smokywood Pastures sells treats, recipes, and seasonal cheer for the Feast of Winter Veil. Their shipment was stolen in the snowy hills of the Alterac Mountains, and business stalled. With the treats recovered and the Abominable Greench dealt with, Kaymard Copperpinch sends you to receive the company's thanks. Great-father Winter waits beside the holiday tree in the Valley of Strength. The goblins have arranged for him to honor those who rescued the holiday supplies with a seasonal blessing and a Smokywood Pastures Special Gift.

quest:7.text: Kobold Camp Cleanup. At Northshire, Kobold Camp Cleanup puts new recruits to their first test defending Stormwind's borders. Marshal McBride sends volunteers after kobolds in the northern woods, where their growing numbers threaten the abbey grounds. Northshire Valley once offered quiet for prayer, farming, and novice training. In recent years, Stormwind's forces have grown thin. With the King missing and royal garrisons scattered, wild creatures and opportunists press at civilization's edge. Marshal McBride directs the valley's defense from Northshire Abbey. He depends on fresh volunteers to keep threats from disrupting the abbey or endangering the surrounding vineyards. Kobolds are timid cave-dwellers with a strong attachment to candles. They usually pick at underground seams, far from direct sunlight. Now an entire clan has reached Northshire's northern timberline. If left unchecked, their numbers can turn scavenging into open raids. McBride sends recruits to thin their vanguard and test their resolve to defend the realm.

quest:7025.text: Treats for Greatfather Winter. During the Feast of Winter Veil, the performer portraying Greatfather Winter in Ironforge grows tired and asks passersby for a seasonal treat. Bringing him freshly baked gingerbread cookies and ice cold milk earns a festive reward and his warm gratitude. While Winter Veil has its roots in ancient titan lore and dwarven myths of an immortal figure cloaked in winter's chill, modern festivities rely heavily on the commercial sponsorship of Smokywood Pastures. Stationed by the holiday tree in the Commons of Ironforge, an ordinary dwarf spends grueling hours suited up as Greatfather Winter, fielding holiday wishes from citizens and eager children alike. After listening to requests for gifts all day, the resident Greatfather Winter inevitably develops a hearty appetite of his own. Rather than asking for something extravagant, he requests a simple comfort: five freshly baked gingerbread cookies made with holiday spices and an ice cold milk to wash them down. The trade offers a moment of relief to an exhausted festival worker and spreads goodwill throughout the snowy capital.

quest:730.text: Trouble in Darkshore?. In Darnassus, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker seeks help for his missing crew. His introductory appeal sends travelers across the sea to Auberdine, where the dwarven expedition met Darkshore's wild, shadowy coast. Darnassus, the grand night elven capital, is home to dwarven researchers from Ironforge studying Kalimdor's ancient mysteries. Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker sent an excavation party across the water to Darkshore to unearth artifacts of antiquity. Weeks have passed without a message or progress report, and Greywhisker fears his field crew has met dangers they could not survive alone. Greywhisker laments that many in the Alliance dismiss dwarven archaeology as an eccentric hobby. Findings in Khaz Modan have convinced his colleagues that an ancient, terrifying force threatens Azeroth from Lordaeron to Kalimdor. The work in Darkshore's ruins is more than scholarship: it seeks to understand historic cataclysms and the deep-seated menaces buried beneath ancient soil.

quest:743.text: Dangers of the Windfury. Dangers of the Windfury is a rite of martial readiness offered by Ruul Eagletalon in Bloodhoof Village. Young tauren and Horde adventurers are tasked with battling the savage Windfury harpies nesting in the southeastern cliffs of Mulgore. Hunting these feral predators serves as an essential test of skill and survival before journeying beyond the tribal homeland. In Bloodhoof Village, the veteran warrior Ruul Eagletalon observes all travelers who pass through the heart of Mulgore. For those coming of age or seeking to prove themselves ready for wider adventures, Ruul demands tangible proof of their combat instincts. Survival beyond the sheltered valleys of Mulgore requires poise against aggressive, cunning foes, and Ruul uses the land's fiercest native predators to measure a youth's mettle. The Windfury harpies roost along the mountainous southeastern rim of Mulgore, safely off the beaten trails but constantly posing a threat to wandering wildlife and isolated travelers. Vicious and relentlessly hungry for fresh flesh, these avian terrors rely on swift swoops and razor-sharp claws. Defeating them and claiming their talons demonstrates not only the power to defeat an entrenched threat, but the speed required to counter aerial raiders.

quest:7493.text: The Journey Has Just Begun. After Onyxia's fall, skilled leatherworkers in Orgrimmar learn how her scales can guard against the black dragonflight. Overlord Runthak recognizes their craft and teaches a rare technique for making protective cloaks, needed against the flames of Blackrock Spire. Onyxia's fall is a triumph for the Horde, yet the black dragonflight remains a threat. The broodmother's scaled hide resists draconic flame. Horde leaders seek craftsmen who can turn the dragon's remains into defensive armor rather than let them go to waste.

quest:7497.text: The Journey Has Just Begun. In Stormwind, Major Mattingly recognizes the artisan who brought down Onyxia. He teaches the craft needed to make a cloak from her scales. Few who helped bring down Onyxia can also work her hide. When an artisan with master leatherworking reports to Major Mattingly in Stormwind, the officer recognizes how much those skills matter in the battles ahead.

quest:76.text: The Jasperlode Mine. Kobolds have overrun the Jasperlode Mine in eastern Elwynn. Marshal Dughan sends scouts to learn how far the infestation has spread. After kobolds swarmed the Fargodeep tunnels south of Goldshire, Marshal Dughan feared they had reached other mines. Jasperlode lies in the rocky foothills northeast of the Tower of Azora and supplies raw stone and metal to the kingdom. Dughan cannot spare Stormwind guards from their town patrols, so he sends independent adventurers east to see whether kobolds have taken this mine too. Scouts who reach Jasperlode's chambers find kobolds have driven out the human miners and fortified the dark passages. Marshal Dughan faces another blow as the crisis grows. King Varian Wrynn is missing, and royal troops are withheld from outlying territories. The local garrison has too few soldiers to clear the mines, leaving the kingdom's heart short of minerals and hemmed in by threats.

quest:768.text: Gathering Leather. Gathering Leather is a straightforward trade request offered by Veren Tallstrider on the rises of Thunder Bluff. To sustain the capital and test young hunters, Veren exchanges a bundle of cured light leather skins for crafted goods. It highlights the deeply ingrained tauren tradition of turning the fruits of the plains hunt into essential clothing and armor.
