In the newly settled capital atop the high mesas of Mulgore, craftsmanship and survival walk hand in hand. Veren Tallstrider works skins into clothing and protective armor needed by the growing population of Thunder Bluff. Rather than harvesting everything himself, he encourages young adventurers heading out into the plains to bring back their quarry, turning mundane hunting into honorable civic service. For the tauren, hunting beasts across the grasslands is not sport; it is an honorable endeavor that feeds, clothes, and shelters the tribe. Veren Tallstrider looks for hunters with a hunger to bring honor to their clan, asking specifically for light leather stripped from the local wildlife. In return for twelve well-kept hides, he repays the hunter with sturdy goods, reinforcing the mutual support that binds tauren society together.

quest:769.text: Kodo Hide Bag. Kodo Hide Bag is a trade quest offered by Veren Tallstrider, a skilled tauren leatherworker atop the high mesas of Thunder Bluff. In exchange for fundamental crafting supplies, he passes on the traditional plains technique for stitching durable travel packs from sturdy beast hide. It serves as an early rite of passage for apprentice leathercrafters in Mulgore. Perched on Thunder Bluff's crafting rises, Veren Tallstrider upholds the long-standing nomadic tradition of wasting nothing from the hunt. To earn his tutelage, an aspiring leatherworker must present him with cured light leather and sturdy thread. By demonstrating their competence with foundational materials, apprentices prove they are ready to craft goods worthy of carrying survival gear across Kalimdor's rugged expanses. To the tauren, the kodo beast is an emblem of endurance, strength, and steady resolve. Its thick hide shields against brambles, biting wind, and beast claws alike. Crafting bags and garments from kodo hide is not merely a utilitarian act, but an expression of reverence for the animal that has nourished and carried the Shu'halo through countless generations across the plains of Mulgore.

quest:770.text: The Demon Scarred Cloak. The Demon Scarred Cloak is a ragged pelt recovered from the legendary white wolf Ghost Howl, who roams the grassy plains of Mulgore. Marked by an enduring wound inflicted during past clashes with the Burning Legion, the pelt serves as proof of the beast's release from torment. Bringing it to the elders of Bloodhoof Village brings closure to the story of a tragic local legend. Ghost Howl is an elusive white wolf known across Mulgore for both his ferocity and his sorrowful howl. When slain, the beast leaves behind a pelt that is visibly scarred by foul demonic corruption. These lingering marks date back to the wolf's desperate battles against the invading demons of the Burning Legion, a confrontation that left Ghost Howl wounded in both flesh and spirit long after the Third War came to a close. The tauren of Mulgore maintain a deep respect for the wild beasts of their homeland, revering them as children of the Earth Mother. Presenting the scarred cloak to Skorn Whitecloud in Bloodhoof Village confirms the demise of the tormented predator. Skorn recognizes the immense skill required to track and defeat Ghost Howl, expressing the somber hope that in death, the wolf's tortured spirit has finally attained peace.

quest:7781.text: The Lord of Blackrock. Nefarian's severed head is bound for Stormwind Keep after his defeat in Blackwing Lair. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon receives the trophy, a sign that the master of Blackrock Mountain has fallen. The victory is among the Alliance's greatest military triumphs in recent history. Nefarian, brood-master of the Black Dragonflight and ruler of Upper Blackrock Spire, has long threatened the surrounding human kingdoms. His defeat ends his twisted experiments and schemes. Carrying his battle-scarred head back to Stormwind gives proof that the Lord of Blackrock has fallen to the Alliance's greatest heroes. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon governs the kingdom from the throne room of Stormwind Keep. The dragon's severed head shocks the royal court and commands reverence. With the kingdom strained by internal political strife and threats from beyond, the victory lifts morale and earns a place in Alliance history.

quest:7783.text: The Lord of Blackrock. Nefarian's severed head is carried from Blackrock Mountain to Orgrimmar as proof of victory. Presented to Warchief Thrall, it marks the fall of a great enemy of the Horde. Nefarian has fallen at last. He masterminded Blackwing Lair and led the black dragon brood in the Eastern Kingdoms. His colossal, battle-scarred head proves his death. For Horde warriors, carrying the prize from the burning heights of Blackrock Mountain across the Great Sea to Durotar brings great honor. The trophy is brought before Warchief Thrall. He knows the corruption of Blackrock Mountain well. He freed his people from the internment camps and led them away from the old Horde's demonic bloodlust. The son of Deathwing has fallen, and the Blackrock orcs are free of the dark dragon's cruel dominion.

quest:7784.text: The Lord of Blackrock. In Orgrimmar, Nefarian's severed head is brought before the Horde. After Thrall confirms the black dragon's death, he sends the victor to High Overlord Saurfang in the Valley of Strength to show the trophy to all. Nefarian's head reaches Orgrimmar after the black dragon is slain atop Blackwing Lair. Warchief Thrall confirms that Deathwing's son has fallen, then sends the victor to High Overlord Saurfang in the Valley of Strength. There, the remains are prepared for public display, a warning to enemies and a rallying cry for the true Horde.

quest:783.text: A Threat Within. Volunteers are answering Stormwind's call in Northshire Valley, where local defenses need help. At Northshire Abbey, Marshal McBride explains that the kingdom's forces are spread thin abroad, leaving garrisons short-handed against trouble at home. Northshire Valley once offered quiet for prayer, farming, and monastic study. Now it is Elwynn Forest's first line of defense against unrest at home. Stormwind's regular forces serve on distant fronts, leaving the heartlands short of soldiers. With few guards nearby, the Stormwind Guard must call on every willing volunteer who reaches the abbey. Marshal McBride directs Northshire Valley's defenses from Northshire Abbey as pressures grow. Distant dangers threaten the Alliance, while bandits, vermin, and pests from below ground take advantage of the shortage of soldiers close to home. You answer the call to serve in the valley, starting with the ground around the abbey as threats spread across Elwynn.

quest:784.text: Vanquish the Betrayers. At Tiragarde Keep, Kul Tiran forces hold a coastal foothold in Durotar. Gar'Thok has ordered a Horde strike against Lieutenant Benedict's garrison, whose presence breaks the fragile peace with Theramore. Thrall led the Horde across the Great Sea to Kalimdor, where he joined Lady Jaina Proudmoore against the Burning Legion at Mount Hyjal. Peace broke when Jaina's estranged father, Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore, brought Kul Tiras's navy to Durotar. He blamed all orcs for the Old Horde's atrocities and seized coastal footholds, including Tiragarde Keep. Daelin died at Theramore, but remnants of his fleet still refuse any pact or surrender their hatred. Tiragarde Keep fell briefly after the Grand Admiral's defeat, then Kul Tiras reserves under Lieutenant Benedict retook it. The fortress lies between Razor Hill and Sen'jin Village. From there, sailors and marines harass travelers and threaten Durotar's eastern sea approaches. Gar'Thok sees their position as an immediate danger to Durotar's security and calls on Horde warriors to strike at Benedict's command.

quest:786.text: Thwarting Kolkar Aggression. Lar Prowltusk has found invasion plans in Kolkar Crag, west of Sen'jin Village. The Kolkar centaurs plan to strike Durotar's settlements and Orgrimmar. Lar Prowltusk, a troll tracker scouting western Durotar, slipped into Kolkar Crag under cover of night. There he found the Kolkar centaurs planning more than scattered coastal raids. Three centaur leaders had divided the invasion plans among them, with attacks aimed at the Valley of Trials, Sen'jin Village, and the gates of Orgrimmar. You are sent into Kolkar Crag to destroy the three attack scrolls before the centaurs can strike. The dry canyons hold their camps, and each scroll belongs to a different leader. Lar Prowltusk believes the Horde would defeat a full invasion, but burning the plans can spare Durotar's defenders costly fighting while their young nation finds its footing.

quest:787.text: The New Horde. In the Valley of Trials, veteran warrior Eitrigg calls new recruits to the Den. He sends you to Gornek to begin training and shares why he returned to the Horde and what Thrall hopes it can become. Eitrigg stands in the Valley of Trials under Warchief Thrall's orders, ready to evaluate and mentor the Horde's newest hopefuls. After the Second War, he abandoned the Old Horde, disillusioned by its corruption by the Burning Legion. He lived in quiet exile until humans captured him. Thrall rescued Eitrigg, and the veteran chose to return after learning of the young Warchief's dream: an honorable Horde rooted in ancestral shamanism and entirely free of demonic masters. Before you venture beyond the harsh canyons of the Valley of Trials, Eitrigg sends you into the shaded cavern called the Den to speak with Gornek. Gornek rarely minces words about the crude state of new aspirants. His oversight ensures that only those who master discipline and survival enter the wider reaches of Durotar.

quest:791.text: Carry Your Weight. Atop the watchtower overlooking Razor Hill, Furl Scornbrow asks young Horde adventurers to gather canvas from human and centaur hostiles. Too old for the front lines, the scarred veteran will make supplies to aid their journey. Furl Scornbrow fought beside Warchief Thrall in Durotar and at Mount Hyjal. Age and old injuries have slowed the veteran, and he no longer wields his axe in battle. From the Razor Hill watchtower, Furl keeps a steady vigil and sounds the alarm against incursions. He supports the next generation of defenders from his post. As the Horde's grip on the region tightens, signal horn alerts grow less frequent, leaving Furl more hours to craft practical gear. Sturdy canvas is scarce in Durotar's arid canyons, but the Kul Tiran interlopers along the eastern shore and the nomadic Kolkar centaur roaming the plains carry it in abundance. Canvas scavenged from these hostile forces gives Furl cloth to stitch utility bags for active scouts.

quest:792.text: Vile Familiars. In the Valley of Trials, Vile Familiars are creeping out of a nearby cavern. Zureetha Fargaze found a hidden Burning Blade coven while watching over the valley's trials. Recruits are sent to hunt the familiars spreading across Durotar's red earth. The Valley of Trials tests young orcs and Darkspear trolls in strength, discipline, and loyalty to Thrall's Horde. Its trials were meant to pit recruits against scorpids and boars, not demonic corruption. Yet a cave to the northeast shelters agents of the Burning Blade, who have formed a secret coven beneath the valley overseers' watch. Zureetha Fargaze, an instructor guiding newcomers near the Den, spotted the taint before it could overrun the canyon. Vile Familiars now pour from the cave mouth, hurling fire at anyone who wanders too close. Before the Horde can root out the masters in hiding, young recruits are sent to cut down these lesser servants and keep the valley secure.

quest:794.text: Burning Blade Medallion. Zureetha Fargaze sends young Horde initiates into the Burning Blade Coven cave in the Valley of Trials. They face a hidden cultist and seek a dark relic, the Burning Blade Medallion. Its presence points to demonic corruption taking root near the Horde. Young orcs and trolls face trials of combat and survival in the Valley of Trials, while a menace gathers nearby. The warlock Zureetha Fargaze senses through divination that the vile familiars on the northern bluffs are only the vanguard of a darker presence. Deep in a nearby cavern, the Burning Blade cult has made a hidden coven, where its followers practice dark arts and keep dangerous relics of demonic power.

quest:804.text: Sarkoth. In the Valley of Trials, Hana'zua waits for help after Sarkoth's venom leaves him stranded. You have slain the scorpid that wounded him; now Gornek needs word at the Den so aid can reach the scout. Hana'zua, a Darkspear scout, lies stranded on the high bluffs of the Valley of Trials. Sarkoth's venom has left him too weak to descend the treacherous paths alone. You have avenged him by slaying the scorpid, but he still cannot cross the arid stones without help. A passing initiate must carry word down to the training encampment. Gornek waits at the Den for your report. Once he hears of Hana'zua's plight, he recognizes the danger from Sarkoth and organizes aid for the scout. Horde commanders honor those who set aside their own training to defend and rescue a fallen stranger. Such conduct proves an initiate's worth before they march into Durotar proper.

quest:805.text: Report to Sen'jin Village. Zureetha Fargaze sends word from the Valley of Trials to Sen'jin Village. Burning Blade cultists have been active in the valley, and she asks young initiates to warn the Darkspear trolls. Master Gadrin tells them dark magic threatens the nearby Echo Isles. Young initiates leave the Valley of Trials after proving their combat mettle and recovering dark medallions from the Burning Blade Coven. Zureetha Fargaze sees that the demons in the sacred proving grounds are no isolated nuisance; they point to a blight spreading across Durotar. She sends the proven fighters east past the ravine's mouth, then south toward the coast, to warn the Darkspear tribe.

quest:806.text: Dark Storms. In Durotar, Burning Blade cultists corrupt the land from Thunder Ridge. Orgnil Soulscar in Razor Hill has learned that the goblin warlock Fizzle Darkstorm leads them, and asks you to end his threat. Orgnil Soulscar has learned that dark magic has taken hold in Thunder Ridge, northwest of Razor Hill. Burning Blade cultists prowl the ravine while young Horde defenders patrol Durotar’s borders. Their presence brings ruin to the wildlife and land. Fizzle Darkstorm, a goblin warlock allied with the Burning Blade, directs the cultists in Thunder Ridge. He wields fel power for the cult rather than serving commerce or cartel interests. Slaying him and bringing back his twisted claw will show Orgnil that the cult’s leaders in the ravine have been struck down.

quest:808.text: Minshina's Skull. In Sen'jin Village, Master Gadrin hears the desperate cries of his dead brother, Minshina. Zalazane slew Minshina on the Echo Isles and bound his soul with dark magic to his own severed skull. To free him from torment, you must reclaim the skull from Zalazane's ritual grounds. Master Gadrin is one of the Darkspear tribe's spiritual anchors in Sen'jin Village, yet dark visions torment him. His brother Minshina fell when Zalazane betrayed the tribe and seized control of the Echo Isles. Minshina died in the conflict, but death has brought him no peace. In troll tradition and voodoo mysticism, the body can die while the spirit remains bound. Now Minshina's tormented voice reaches Gadrin in his dreams, pleading to be saved from a fate worse than death. Zalazane does more than kill his former brethren; he traps their souls to fuel his dark sorcery. He bound Minshina's spirit to his own skull, now set within a blasphemous circle of power on the largest of the Echo Isles. Hexed trolls guard the circle, where candles burn through the rites and the skull focuses Zalazane's twisted mojo. While it remains there, Minshina is captive to the witch doctor's will.

quest:809.text: Ak'Zeloth. Neeru Fireblade sends you from Orgrimmar into the Barrens after signs of demonic corruption emerge. His contact waits near the border. Neeru Fireblade says the Burning Blade still threatens the Horde with demonic corruption. After you bring him a Burning Blade insignia collar from Durotar, he sends you into the Barrens. A cult gathers around the Demon Seed, an artifact of vile power, and Neeru wants you to find his contact near the border.

quest:812.text: Need for a Cure. Rhinag lies poisoned on Durotar’s northwestern cliffs, far from the cure he needs. The Darkspear troll has little time before the venom kills him, so he sends a passing courier to Orgrimmar for Kor'ghan’s remedy. Rhinag was fighting venomtail scorpids near Durotar’s border when one stung him. Their venom can kill in less than an hour. The poison keeps him from walking to Orgrimmar, so his survival depends on a traveler reaching his remote camp in time. Rhinag sends travelers beneath Orgrimmar to the Cleft of Shadow, where Kor'ghan knows how to counter the poisons of Durotar’s wastes. Kor'ghan can brew a cure, though he rarely helps those who have not proved themselves.

quest:813.text: Finding the Antidote. Kor'ghan in Orgrimmar races to brew a cure for the poisoned hunter Rhinag. You gather venomtail poison sacs from scorpids outside the city walls before their venom proves fatal. Durotar's wildlife is unforgiving, and survival depends on wilderness preparation. Rhinag, a Darkspear troll, was hunting in Durotar when he faced venomtail scorpids without an antidote. Their potent venom struck quickly, leaving him in need of immediate aid. Kor'ghan, an experienced hunter in Orgrimmar, must mix a draught before the poison kills him. Mature venomtail scorpids outside Orgrimmar's gates carry the sacs Kor'ghan needs to make an antidote. He says there will be time to chastise Rhinag for going unprepared, but every moment matters now. Bring the sacs back into the city, and Kor'ghan can brew the draught for the dying hunter.

quest:816.text: Lost But Not Forgotten. Misha Tor'kren waits at her homestead for news of her son, Kron. He went west to hunt crocolisks along the Southfury River, and she fears the worst. Misha Tor'kren lives at a farmstead northwest of Razor Hill in Durotar. Days ago, her son Kron set out west toward the Southfury River, along the Barrens border, to hunt its fierce crocolisks. Misha warned him how deadly the beasts were, but pride drove him to leave and prove his strength. No one has seen him since.

quest:817.text: Practical Prey. Vel'rin Fang needs hunters to bring tiger hides from the Echo Isles to Sen'jin Village. The Darkspear need the supplies as their numbers grow and their stores run low. The Darkspear in Sen'jin Village have to make every resource last along Durotar's harsh coast. Tiger pelts can be made into tents, blankets and armor. As refugees arrive and scouts return, the village's stores have thinned, and leatherworker Vel'rin Fang has sent hunters out for more hides. The Darkspear leave the tigers of Durotar largely undisturbed, hunting them only when the tribe needs more supplies. Hunters cross the water to the Echo Isles to track the predators. For the trolls, the hunt also tests patience, discipline and skill in the wild.

quest:818.text: A Solvent Spirit. Master Vornal tests would-be pupils in Sen'jin Village as his eyesight fades. He asks them to gather makrura eyes and crawler mucus along Durotar's coast. Though he scoffs at taking an apprentice, the work tests patience and resolve. Master Vornal lives in Sen'jin Village, where age has dimmed his sight. Primal magic once came readily to his fingertips, but now he relies on alchemy to sharpen his perceptions and weave his arts. Though his body weakens, the stubborn troll refuses an apprentice. He says neither the Darkspear nor Durotar's orcs have produced anyone worthy of his teaching. Vornal asks for raw materials from the harsh coast: intact makrura eyes and vials of crawler mucus. Taking undamaged eyes from armored, snapping makrura calls for careful strikes. Gathering enough mucus tests whether a would-be pupil can endure tedious work. For Vornal, hunting these coastal beasts is less about the reagents than finding out who can keep their focus. For Master Vornal, time and patience measure strength. He expects brash youths to grow frustrated or abandon the work. Bringing pristine ingredients back to Sen'jin Village shows survival skills along the dangerous reefs of the Echo Isles channel, and the discipline needed to master alchemy's subtle arts.

quest:819.text: Chen's Empty Keg. A keg bearing Chen Stormstout’s mark lies abandoned in the Barrens. Its discovery points toward the wandering brewmaster’s old ties to Durotar. Travelers sometimes find an abandoned wooden barrel across the dry Barrens. Razormane quilboar and Kolkar centaur leave ordinary casks behind, but this barrel is carefully made and bears a plaque: “Chen Stormstout - May your spirit be raised and always raise your spirits.” It is an odd relic beneath Kalimdor’s sun. To learn how it came to the Barrens, you seek someone who knows brewing. Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet recognizes the keg’s craftsmanship and names Chen Stormstout as its owner. Chen, a wandering Pandaren, traveled with Rexxar during the battles that secured Durotar for Thrall’s Horde. Years have passed since Chen walked Kalimdor’s red earth, yet seasoned brewers still remember his recipes and wandering spirit.

quest:821.text: Chen's Empty Keg. In Ratchet, Brewmaster Drohn hopes to revive Chen Stormstout's potent brew with wild ingredients from the Barrens. A marked keg brings Chen Stormstout to mind for Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet. Chen passed the secrets of his namesake brew to Drohn's mentor, who entrusted them to Drohn. The recipe calls for raw, potent elements taken straight from the Barrens' fierce wildlife, an unusual choice to those outside the brewing trade.

quest:823.text: Report to Orgnil. Master Gadrin sends word from Sen'jin Village to Razor Hill about the Burning Blade. This early Horde dispatch carries a warning of demonic corruption spreading through Durotar. Sen'jin Village faces its own troubles, especially Zalazane's treachery on the Echo Isles. Yet reports of the Burning Blade point to a danger far wider than the village's local woes. Demonic corruption was uncovered in the Valley of Trials, and Master Gadrin knows the threat cannot be met in isolation. He sends you north along the road to Razor Hill, where orc authorities watch over Durotar. Orgnil Soulscar is stationed at Razor Hill's military encampment, charged with rooting out evils within Durotar and guarding its central lands. When you bring Gadrin's warning, Orgnil combines reports from Sen'jin Village and the Valley of Trials. The Burning Blade's reach is dangerously close, so he quickly mobilizes forces to break up the cultists before their rituals can unseat the young nation.

quest:825.text: From The Wreckage..... Gar'Thok sends Horde scouts to the wrecks off the Scuttle Coast for Gnomish Tools. The Horde hopes to study Alliance engineering and turn its advantage to their own use. Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore brought Kul Tiras's fleet to Kalimdor, where its ships crowded the shore near Tiragarde Keep. After his defeat, broken hulls sank along the Scuttle Coast. Kul Tiran soldiers who survived fortify the keep, while the fleet's wreckage lies scattered on the shoals beneath the tide. The Horde knows Alliance ingenuity can give its enemies an edge over orcish strength, iron, and blood. Gnomish technicians sailed with the expeditionary fleet and equipped its ships with complex machinery and precise tools. Gar'Thok wants those tools recovered from the wrecks so the Horde can learn how they work. Gar'Thok sends the salvaged tools by caravan from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar. Horde craftspeople and tacticians hope to study the gnomish instruments and better counter Alliance devices in future conflicts, while strengthening their own industries.

quest:826.text: Zalazane. On the Echo Isles, Zalazane's treachery has driven the Darkspear from their home. Master Gadrin of Sen'jin Village sends Horde champions to end the witch doctor's rule. Dark magic drove Zalazane mad, and he enslaved his fellow tribesmen, seizing the Darkspear trolls' rightful home and forcing them into exile on Durotar's coast. The Darkspear made a home on the Echo Isles after fleeing their sunken island and following Thrall across the Great Sea. The isles lie just off Durotar's southeast coast. Zalazane, once a respected and powerful witch doctor of the tribe, hungered for power. He used hexes to enslave the minds of his kin and began a violent uprising. Vol'jin led the Darkspear who remained free, but they were driven from their ancestral camps across the water. They had to build a temporary refuge at Sen'jin Village. Zalazane still sends raiding parties from his hilltop stronghold on the largest Echo Isle. They cross the channel to seize more Darkspear and drag them under his control. The captured trolls become mindless voodoo and hexed thralls, lost to their tribe. Master Gadrin sees more than an occupation of Darkspear land: Zalazane threatens the tribe's survival. Until his severed head is brought before the elders, no Darkspear can be safe.

quest:827.text: Skull Rock. Margoz sends you into Skull Rock, east of Orgrimmar. Burning Blade cultists have overrun the cave and use painful demonic devices to bind themselves to dark magic. Margoz needs the cursed artifacts to study the cult's presence near the capital. In northeastern Durotar, cultists gather close to Orgrimmar's gates. The cave lies among the hills, far from the open roads, yet near the Warchief's seat. The Burning Blade, a demonic cult that has long plagued orcish society, has made its home in the tunnels. Its followers perform rituals there while the Warchief's scouts watch nearby. Burning Blade cultists wear Searing Collars around their necks, metal bands that scorch and brand their flesh. Margoz believes the pain and fel sorcery in the collars attune their wearers to demonic power. He asks you to recover the collars so he can study the spells and bindings that empower the cultists.

quest:828.text: Margoz. In northern Durotar, Margoz watches for the Burning Blade's growing threat. After the clash with fel corruption at Thunder Ridge, Orgnil Soulscar sends champions to seek the isolated orc shaman before they strike a nearby cultist stronghold. Margoz's counsel reveals Skull Rock, the Burning Blade's concealed cavern base. After Thunder Ridge revealed the depth of fel taint, Orgnil Soulscar sees that strength alone cannot cleanse Durotar. He sends champions to Margoz, an experienced orc shaman keeping a lonely camp in the crags northeast of Razor Hill. Between Drygulch Ravine and the eastern sea, Margoz watches the northern reaches for dark omens that Orgrimmar's busy warriors often miss. Margoz knows the Burning Blade's power base in northern Durotar: Skull Rock, a concealed cavern system carved into the mountain cliffs outside Orgrimmar's southern gates. The cultists are closer to Thrall's capital than the Warchief's guards realize, and Skull Rock's hidden passages can conceal a demonic ambush. Margoz gives those sent against the coven counsel so they do not enter blindly.

quest:829.text: Neeru Fireblade. In Orgrimmar, Neeru Fireblade studies dark arts he says can protect the Horde. Margoz sends you from Durotar with a Searing Collar taken from the Burning Blade cult, hoping the warlock can explain its demonic power. Margoz has found the limit of shamanic arts. The collars taken from Burning Blade cultists at Skull Rock carry demonic sorcery, beyond what he can unravel. Shamans draw on the elements and ancestral spirits, so Margoz sends you to a warlock in the capital to learn what the collars do. Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow lies beneath its red cliffs. Warlocks and other practitioners of forbidden magic work there under Thrall's wary eye. Neeru Fireblade lives in the cavern and says he studies fel power to thwart demonic threats. When you bring him the collar, his curiosity turns Durotar's investigation toward the warlock enclave.

quest:83.text: Red Linen Goods. At Eastvale Logging Camp, Sara Timberlain needs cloth for her tailoring. She asks passing adventurers to hunt Defias bandits and take their linen bandanas, then uses the cloth to make goods for travelers. Defias bandits across Elwynn wear red linen bandanas. Their less organized kin in Northshire Valley make do with cheap burlap masks. For local craftsmen short on materials, the bandanas offer cloth they can use. Sara Timberlain works as a seamstress at Eastvale Logging Camp, near Elwynn's eastern border. She needs workable textiles for her trade, so she asks adventurers to thin the Defias camps scattered through the woods. The cloth keeps her tailoring supplied while the bandits' encroachment on the area is checked.

quest:8311.text: Hallow's End Treats for Jesper!. Jesper lies sick in Stormwind during Hallow's End, longing for the treats and fun beyond the orphanage. Too ill to go out, he asks Alliance adventurers to gather sweets for him. Jesper stays in the orphanage in Stormwind's Cathedral Square, sick during Hallow's End. He cannot enjoy the childhood pleasure of gathering sweets across Azeroth, so he hopes passing adventurers will share the holiday spirit and collect treats for him. To bring Jesper the sweets he hopes for, you travel beyond Elwynn Forest. You visit the innkeepers of Stormwind, Ironforge, and Darnassus, along with the gnome exile Talvash del Kissel. Each asks you to perform before giving you a treat. You cluck like a chicken, dance, flex, or chug like a train, earning regional sweets such as Stormwind Nougat and Gnomeregan Gumdrops.

quest:834.text: Winds in the Desert. A stolen supply caravan leaves Rezlak waiting in Durotar. Dustwind harpies ambushed it in Razorwind Canyon, scattering the construction materials among the cliffs. Rezlak came directly from Ratchet, sent by Chief Engineer Gazlowe to help the Horde build across Durotar. The harsh, barren land already makes fortification work hard. Now shipments keep vanishing before they reach the building sites, and without the cargo, work stops. The irritable goblin supervisor has nothing to build with. Dustwind harpies ambushed the latest supply run in Razorwind Canyon. They roost along the high ravines beside the road from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar, then swoop on passing wagons. These scavengers do not eat or destroy the freight. They hoard the crates and sacks near their nests, where the supplies remain for anyone willing to fight through their territory.

quest:835.text: Securing the Lines. Near Razorwind Canyon, Rezlak needs the goblin supply routes through Durotar protected. Harpies in Drygulch Ravine keep intercepting and plundering caravans, so he hires help to drive them out. Dustwind harpies make travel through Durotar’s dry valleys dangerous. Rezlak watches over regional supply operations for his boss, Gazlowe. The harpies roosting in Drygulch Ravine raid caravans in Razorwind Canyon and seize shipments before they reach their destinations. Rezlak believes the right price can get anything done. Rather than enter the canyon himself, he hires adventurers to break the roost by eliminating Dustwind Savages and Dustwind Storm Witches. Clearing the harpies keeps trade corridors open, secures shipments of engineering gadgets, and points helpful travelers toward greater opportunities in Ratchet.

quest:8354.text: Chicken Clucking for a Mint. During the festive season of Hallow's End, Innkeeper Norman of the Undercity offers a piece of candy to travelers helping an ailing child. To earn the Undercity Mint, adventurers must cast aside their dignity and flap about like a chicken. The Undercity is rarely known for laughter or warmth, built as it is beneath the ruins of Lordaeron by the liberated Forsaken. Yet when Hallow's End arrives, even the grim denizens of the Trade Quarter join in seasonal revelry. Innkeeper Norman holds onto a stash of Undercity Mints, designated for those collecting treats on behalf of young Spoops, a sick orphan in need of holiday cheer. Rather than surrendering the treat outright to seasoned adventurers, Norman demands a bit of humiliating spectacle. Believing that grown warriors and spellcasters ought to earn their confections, he refuses to part with the mint until the petitioner mimics a barnyard chicken right before his counter.

quest:8356.text: Flexing for Nougat. During autumn's Hallow's End, you gather festive sweets for an orphan in Stormwind. Innkeeper Allison at the Gilded Rose asks you to flex before she gives you Stormwind Nougat. Hallow's End brings a lighter mood to Stormwind's streets. The holiday marks the turning of the seasons and wards off dark spirits. Common folk celebrate with disguises, revelry, and trick-or-treating. Alliance innkeepers join in, offering traditional sweets to those who perform a harmless trick. At the Gilded Rose in the Trade District, Innkeeper Allison asks for a show before handing out holiday candy, even when you're gathering sweets for Jesper, an orphaned boy. She comments playfully on your physique and asks you to flex your muscles. When you do, she gives you a piece of chewy Stormwind Nougat.

quest:8357.text: Dancing for Marzipan. During Hallow's End, travelers in Darnassus gather sweets for Jesper, a sick orphan in Stormwind. Innkeeper Saelienne keeps the trick-or-treat custom: a dance comes before her Darnassus Marzipan. Hallow's End brings a lighter spirit to Darnassus, the sacred forest city of the long-lived night elves. You come seeking sweets for Jesper, a sick child recovering in Stormwind. Innkeeper Saelienne keeps the season's custom, even when the treat is meant for a child in need. First, she asks for a trick. Saelienne asks you to dance on the inn floor before she gives you Darnassus Marzipan. The performance earns the sweet needed for the holiday care package bound for Jesper.

quest:8359.text: Flexing for Nougat. In Orgrimmar, Innkeeper Gryshka offers nougat to those who play along. During Hallow's End, she asks you to flex for a piece meant to cheer Spoops, a bedridden child. Hallow's End brings pranks and sweet-gathering to Azeroth's capitals. In Orgrimmar's inn, Innkeeper Gryshka keeps holiday sweets for those who take part in the season's custom. You face dragons and dark sorcery in your travels, but here the bargain is simple: perform a trick or leave without a treat. Innkeeper Gryshka wants a display of Orcish strength before she gives you Orgrimmar Nougat for young Spoops. Whatever disguise or armor you wear, she asks you to strike a muscular pose. Even the Horde's feared combatants can be made to entertain the common folk for candy.

quest:84.text: Back to Billy. You carry Bernice Stonefield's freshly baked pie across the road to Billy Maclure, who has information about her missing necklace. The delivery continues the feud between the Stonefield and Maclure families in central Elwynn Forest. The old feud between the Stonefields and Maclures leaves little room for kindness. Auntie Bernice Stonefield baked a pork belly pie because Billy Maclure would not share what he knew about her family heirloom without it. She hands you the pie with plain irritation and hopes Billy chokes on every bite.

quest:840.text: Conscript of the Horde. Along Durotar’s western road, Conscript of the Horde sends recruits toward the Barrens. Takrin Pathseeker watches beyond Razor Hill and gives them a letter for Kargal Battlescar, whose outpost guards the crossing. After proving your strength around Razor Hill, you are called west to serve the wider Horde. Takrin Pathseeker watches the road out of Durotar for his friend, veteran Kargal Battlescar. He gives capable travelers a recruitment letter to carry across the Southfury River. For a recruit, the letter marks a first formal assignment beyond the orcs’ new homeland. Kargal Battlescar holds the outpost beyond the bridge, between Durotar’s red canyons and the dry Barrens. He gathers recruits to guard the frontier, where centaur, quilboar, and Alliance expeditions test the border. The Horde needs more than guards there: raw manpower is being sent to the settlement of the Crossroads.

quest:842.text: Crossroads Conscription. Recruits leave the Far Watch Post for duty at Crossroads Conscription. Carrying Kargal Battlescar’s signed letter, you report to Sergra Darkthorn at the Barrens’ central hub. Kargal Battlescar sends you west from the Far Watch Post after you prove your worth. He gives you a signed recruitment letter to carry along the packed dirt road through the Barrens’ arid brush. The road reaches a central junction, where the Crossroads links northern Kalimdor with the southern wilderness. Sergra Darkthorn receives new arrivals at the Crossroads. Warchief Thrall chose the sharp-tongued orc shaman to oversee its operations. Kargal Battlescar grumbles that she is difficult and talks too much, but Thrall holds her in high esteem. Sergra is fierce and unyielding. She reminds recruits, especially arrogant men, that female warriors and leaders stand as equals in Thrall’s Horde, and she will tolerate no insolence.

quest:844.text: Plainstrider Menace. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn sends new Horde adventurers after plainstriders east of the outpost. The birds threaten its food supplies, and the hunt gives newcomers a first measure of the Barrens. The Crossroads coordinates supplies across Kalimdor, but plainstriders east of the outpost have begun picking at its food crates. Sergra Darkthorn, an orc shaman, sends newly arrived Horde adventurers to hunt the birds before they damage the stores. Their attacks threaten provisions the settlement depends on. Sergra Darkthorn uses the hunt to measure newcomers as well as protect supplies. She sees the plainstriders as simple prey, fit to teach young hunters to endure the elements and track quarry across the sun-baked plains. Bringing back their sharp beaks shows a hunter has patience and the basic martial skill needed to face fiercer beasts of the Barrens.

quest:845.text: The Zhevra. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn sends young Horde warriors after the zhevra. Their hunt tests the skills needed to face the Barrens' more dangerous beasts. After the plainstriders, Sergra Darkthorn sends you after tougher prey. Zhevras run in herds across the northern and southern Barrens. They are not the savanna's fiercest beasts, but they are swift and stubborn, and their kicks can break bone. Sergra uses the hunt to test your growing skill. She asks for four intact hooves as proof of the kill and warns that a zhevra's rear kick can knock a grown tauren onto their haunches. Passing this trial brings you closer to facing the plains' predatory prowlers.

quest:848.text: Fungal Spores. At the Barrens oases, Horde adventurers gather Fungal Spores for Apothecary Helbrim of the Royal Apothecary Society. Strange, mutative energies flow through the springs and alter the local plants into potent reagents. Helbrim seeks the specimens to brew concoctions for his colleague in Thunder Bluff. The Barrens is a dry savanna, but the Forgotten Pools, Lushwater Oasis, and Stagnant Oasis brim with unnatural vitality. A curious surge of life energy flows from their waters, warping and invigorating plants and beasts that drink there. Laden mushrooms grow along the muddy banks, absorbing those currents. Their spores hold rare properties that draw the curiosity of passing alchemists. Apothecary Helbrim works at the Crossroads, far from the Undercity, yet remains devoted to the Royal Apothecary Society's research. He gathers the altered spores because Kalimdor's native reagents have strange potency, and he uses them to craft powerful mixtures. The specimens are destined for Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff, part of the Forsaken's scientific work across allied lands.

quest:85.text: Lost Necklace. In southern Elwynn, Bernice Stonefield searches for her missing necklace. She suspects Billy Maclure, the young son of the neighboring family, and asks you to find him across the road. The Stonefield and Maclure families live on adjoining land in southern Elwynn Forest, but they share little goodwill. When "Auntie" Bernice Stonefield discovers her cherished necklace is gone, she blames the youngest Maclure. Certain that Billy Maclure slipped onto her farm and took it, the bitter widow asks you to cross the road to the vineyards, find the boy, and demand its return.

quest:851.text: Verog the Dervish. Across the southern Barrens, Verog the Dervish keeps moving, and Regthar Deathgate seeks to draw him out. The orc directs Horde champions to attack the Kolkar command tent at the Stagnant Oasis, hoping to force the nomadic leader into the open. After Barak Kodobane fell, Regthar Deathgate turned to the remaining Kolkar warlords. Barak had stayed near the northern waters of the Forgotten Pools, but Verog the Dervish roams the sun-baked plains and rarely lingers in one camp. Horde scouts cannot easily track him across that wide territory. Their chance is to make the commander come to them. Verog operates from the Kolkar command post at the Stagnant Oasis, southeast of the Crossroads. Regthar sends you against the camp, where you strike the Kolkar warriors near their command tent. Their alarm calls Verog back to defend the outpost, bringing him within reach of the Horde blades.

quest:852.text: Hezrul Bloodmark. At Lushwater Oasis, Hezrul Bloodmark directs the Kolkar incursions across the Barrens. Regthar Deathgate sends you to end his command and break the centaur's hold on the region. After Barak Kodobane and Verog the Dervish fall, Hezrul Bloodmark remains the Barrens Kolkar's paramount chieftain. Regthar Deathgate calls him brutal and cunning, the spearhead behind the centaur incursions across the savanna. The Horde hopes his death will sow chaos and fracture the Kolkar ranks beyond recovery, before they can overwhelm Horde settlements. Hezrul commands his warbands from Lushwater Oasis, south of the Crossroads. The few watering holes in the Barrens are vital to survival, making this oasis a strategic hub and a staging ground for Kolkar raiders. On Hezrul's own ground, you deny the centaur their most vital stronghold and sever their hold on the southern trails.

quest:854.text: Journey to the Crossroads. At Camp Taurajo, Kirge Sternhorn sends travelers north to aid Thork at the Crossroads. The journey carries them from Mulgore into the Barrens and the wider struggles of the Horde. Camp Taurajo is where many tauren first face the Barrens beyond Mulgore. Just past the mountain pass, mystic Kirge Sternhorn watches travelers descend into the dry grasslands. When Sternhorn sees that a traveler is ready to go farther, Kirge points north along the dusty trade route toward the Crossroads. The tauren of Thunder Bluff and Thrall's new Horde now share their fortunes. Kirge says the two peoples' fates are bound together, and orcs at the Crossroads need reinforcements as they struggle to establish an outpost. At the settlement, Thork welcomes travelers from even the high bluffs, ready to test their strength against the dangers of the savanna.

quest:855.text: Centaur Bracers. West of the Crossroads, Regthar Deathgate calls for Centaur Bracers. Kolkar centaurs contest the central Barrens, threatening Horde control of the plains. The young Horde is fighting to secure territory across Kalimdor. The Barrens lie between Durotar and Mulgore, but Kolkar centaurs contest its watering holes and open plains. They attack supply trains and scouting parties. Regthar Deathgate, an orc warrior, directs the defense from his bunker west of the Crossroads. Regthar asks for proof that Kolkar warriors have fallen. Soldiers who enter Kolkar territory bring back bracers taken from slain centaurs. The trophies verify claims for Horde bounties and are meant to frighten surviving Kolkar raiders.

quest:8569.text: Past Efforts in Warsong Gulch. In Warsong Gulch, soldiers fight for Ashenvale while commanders honor their sacrifices. Capital officers accept the Ribbon of Sacrifice as a sign of steadfast service, even when battles bring no clear victory. The Silverwing Sentinels and Warsong Outriders fight brutal skirmishes along Ashenvale’s southern border. Many battles end without a clear victory. Stormwind, Orgrimmar, and other capitals honor those who hold their ground despite the odds. The Ribbon of Sacrifice marks fighters who gave themselves to the struggle. Far from the front, Alliance Brigadier Generals and Horde Warbringers oversee their forces. Recruiters send new fighters to Warsong Gulch, while quartermasters and tacticians account for veterans returning from hard campaigns. By honoring courage in stalemate or defeat, their leaders help keep soldiers committed to holding Ashenvale.

quest:858.text: Ignition. At a Venture Company camp in the northern Barrens, a trapped pilot needs an ignition key before their cover fails. The operative hijacked a shredder without its key and needs someone to fetch it from the site supervisor. A spy sent by Sputtervalve has slipped into a Venture Company shredder at the northern Barrens drilling grounds. The operative means to seize the machine and study how it works. But the steering and movement column stays locked without its ignition key. A goblin worker has noticed the shredder sitting idle, so the hijacker bluffs that its engine has failed. Trapped beneath the glass canopy with workers nearby, the operative points you toward the central derrick. The supervisor keeps spare ignition keys in the upper control office, the only way out before the bluff fails.

quest:86.text: Pie for Billy. Auntie Bernice Stonefield's missing necklace has left Billy Maclure bargaining for a pork belly pie. The Stonefield and Maclure families have feuded for generations, and Billy will say who has the necklace only after he gets his pie. Billy Maclure gives no apology when asked about Auntie Bernice Stonefield's missing necklace. He will not return it or say who has it until he gets a freshly baked pork belly pie. He knows Bernice is the finest cook in the valley, and he means to enjoy the bargain. The Maclures and Stonefields have traded insults, brawls, and accusations across their pumpkin patches for generations. Bernice is furious at the thought of feeding the boy she believes stole her family's jewelry, yet she agrees to bake. You gather tender meat from the wild boars roaming the nearby pastures, and she sets aside her pride to get her prized necklace back.

quest:863.text: The Escape. You help Wizzlecrank flee the Venture Company drill site at the Sludge Fen in the northern Barrens. Trapped in a stolen prototype shredder, the goblin pilot needs protection from company mercenaries as he climbs from the industrial pit. Afterward, you report to his contact, Sputtervalve, in Ratchet. Wizzlecrank struggles to control the stolen shredder at the Sludge Fen. He has lit the prototype deep inside the Venture Company drill site, but knows little of its levers and switches. The heavy machine lurches across the muddy quarry floor, and its erratic driving and roaring joints alert nearby laborers and armed guards. A stealthy escape becomes a running battle up the excavation pit’s western ramp. The Venture Company sends mercenaries to stop the stolen prototype. As the machine claws up the slope toward open ground, squads move to intercept and disable it. The shredder lashes out, but cannot withstand their sabotage without your protection. It clears the rim and staggers from the main drilling depression, though the machine soon suffers a critical failure.

quest:8642.text: Silvervein the Elder. Silvervein the Elder is an honored ancestral spirit who appears during the Lunar Festival atop the hills overlooking Thelsamar in Loch Modan. Travelers pay their respects to him to honor the ancient ties among Azeroth's elder peoples. In return for acknowledging his presence and heritage, he bestows his ancestral blessing. Perched on the rolling ridges above Thelsamar, Elder Silvervein stands as a quiet guardian and reminder of antiquity. As a figure honored during the Lunar Festival, he represents the enduring memories of bygone eras. Even as the surrounding lands of Loch Modan grapple with trogg invasions and local disputes, Silvervein watches peacefully from his overlook. The presence of spirits like Silvervein serves to bridge the divide between modern folk and ancient lineages. When adventurers seek him out, he expresses gratitude that travelers still pay homage to the olden races of Azeroth. His greeting carries the warmth of ancestral appreciation, offering a commemorative token to those who honor him.

quest:8646.text: Hammershout the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Hammershout the Elder appears in Stormwind's Park. Travelers honor the old races and receive a ceremonial token from him. During the Lunar Festival, revered ancestor spirits appear across Azeroth with wisdom and blessings for travelers who pay their respects. Hammershout the Elder appears in Stormwind's Park district. His presence near the heart of human civilization recalls the ancient races who walked the land before today's kingdoms rose. Hammershout the Elder asks for no trial or oath, only acknowledgment of the past. He is relieved and grateful when people still honor the old races. In return, he gives travelers a ceremonial token, a sign of the bond between the living and the spirits who came before.

quest:8648.text: Darkcore the Elder. Darkcore the Elder is a seasonal quest encountered during the Lunar Festival within the Undercity. By seeking out Elder Darkcore, travelers pay homage to the ancient spirits honored across Azeroth and receive a Coin of Ancestry in return. During the Lunar Festival, spirits of ancient night elven and earthen ancestors appear throughout the continents to share their wisdom and blessings. Elder Darkcore resides in the shadowed halls of the Undercity, bearing witness to the modern realm while offering remembrance to those who seek out the roots of the world. Approaching Elder Darkcore satisfies an ancient custom of showing respect to the venerable dead and the timeless wardens of Azeroth. In recognition of this pilgrimage, the spirit gifts travelers a Coin of Ancestry as a token of goodwill and enduring memory.

quest:8649.text: Stormbrow the Elder. Near Goldshire, Stormbrow the Elder waits beside the water during the Lunar Festival. Travelers honor ancient traditions and the olden races of Azeroth, and receive a token of remembrance in return. A quiet pond lies just behind the smithy in Goldshire, where Stormbrow the Elder appears. Guards, tradesfolk, and weary travelers pass through town on their way into the forest. Beneath Elwynn Forest's canopy, the honored spirit welcomes anyone who comes to honor the realm's long history. During the Lunar Festival, spirits of great ancestors return to walk among the living. Stormbrow the Elder commends travelers who remember those who came before. For honoring the wisdom and legacy of the elder peoples, he grants a blessing and a commemorative coin for the season.

quest:865.text: Raptor Horns. In Ratchet, Mebok Mizzyrix wants intact raptor horns for a scheme of his own. The goblin believes the cunning of Barrens raptors lies in their horns and hires travelers to hunt Sunscale Scytheclaws. Mebok Mizzyrix looks for fortune in Ratchet, where goblins chase one scheme after another. He has watched the Barrens raptors act with unusual craft and coordination compared with beasts elsewhere. Mebok decided their intelligence must be held in their horns. He has no formal inquiry in mind; he wants to put this idea to profit. Mebok wants undamaged horns from Sunscale Scytheclaws, among the Barrens' deadliest predators. They prowl the southern stretches of the Barrens and the northern borders near Ashenvale. The raptors hunt in packs and defend their territory fiercely, so bringing down one and taking its horns intact calls for considerable skill in battle.

quest:8652.text: Graveborn the Elder. Graveborn the Elder is a Lunar Festival encounter situated near the town of Brill in Tirisfal Glades. During the celebration, travelers seek out Elder Graveborn among the blighted groves to honor the ancient forebears of Azeroth. Paying respects to this spirit earns his blessing and a token of the holiday. While the Forsaken dwell among ruined manors and grave sites in Tirisfal Glades, the Lunar Festival brings an unexpected communion with ancient times. Elder Graveborn appears as a spectral elder stationed just outside Brill. Even in a realm shattered by the Scourge and reclaimed by the undead, he welcomes pilgrims who pause to honor the ancient ways. The Lunar Festival marks a time when the great spirits of long-past eras return to offer wisdom and gratitude. When travelers approach Elder Graveborn, he remarks on how heartening it is that the inhabitants of Tirisfal still offer homage to the ancestors despite the land's current decay, bestowing a Coin of Ancestry upon those who greet him.

quest:8653.text: Goldwell the Elder. Goldwell the Elder is a Lunar Festival quest offered by Elder Goldwell in Kharanos, Dun Morogh. Honoring him reflects the enduring tradition of seeking out ancestral spirits across the snowbound dwarven lands. In exchange for your respects, he bestows a token of ancestral blessing. Standing in the bitter cold beside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Elder Goldwell watches over the bustling trade path leading to the gates of Ironforge. During the Lunar Festival, this venerable figure welcomes weary travelers, adventurers, and locals alike, embodying the long memory of ancient days when early mortals walked beneath the stars of Azeroth. Approaching Goldwell offers a moment of reflection amidst the harsh winter winds of Dun Morogh. He expresses relief and joy that mortals still remember the ancient races and their deeds, thanking all who pause their journeys to show respect. In turn, he awards a sacred Coin of Ancestry as an emblem of his blessing.

quest:867.text: Harpy Raiders. Witchwing harpies strike supply caravans on the northwestern trails of the Barrens. Darsok Swiftdagger at the Crossroads sends you to hunt their raiders and roguefeathers, taking their talons as proof. Witchwing harpies strike caravans crossing the Barrens. From rocky crags in the northwest, they swoop on merchant trains and supply wagons. They kill pack animals and seize goods bound for orcish outposts, making each journey through the region dangerous. Darsok Swiftdagger, an orc rogue, has spent days watching the flock's habits and ranks. He believes an unfocused assault on their mountain roosts would scatter them. His plan is to break the Witchwing from the lowest rank upward, starting with the raiders before turning to their commanders.

quest:8670.text: Runetotem the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, travelers in Durotar can honor Runetotem the Elder, an ancestral spirit. She waits in Razor Hill beneath a beam of heavenly light, offering blessings and festival tokens to those who remember the past. During the Lunar Festival, spirits of ancient elders appear across Azeroth to commune with the living. Elder Runetotem waits inside Razor Hill, just past the southern entrance. A beam of starlight falls on her as she watches over the orcish settlement. Travelers can pause there to honor the wisdom of those who came before. When you pay Elder Runetotem homage, she gives you a festival token of fortune and tells you where other spirits can be found. Her directions point toward Elder Darkhorn and Elder High Mountain elsewhere across the continent.

quest:8673.text: Bloodhoof the Elder. Bloodhoof the Elder is an encounter with one of the venerated ancestral spirits who manifests during the Lunar Festival. Located just outside Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore, this honored spirit acknowledges the respect paid by wandering travelers and grants an ancestral token in return. During the celebration of the Lunar Festival, the spirits of great heroes and elders from ages past return to Azeroth. Shrouded in celestial radiance, Elder Bloodhoof appears just north of Bloodhoof Village near the bridge. Approaching these venerated ancestors is an act of honoring past sacrifices, and in exchange, Elder Bloodhoof offers words of encouragement and a sacred Coin of Ancestry. Standing on the ancestral lands of Mulgore, Elder Bloodhoof serves as a bridge between the living tauren tribes and the memory of their forebears. For the tauren, honoring the dead is a pillar of spiritual life, reinforcing the harmony between the Earth Mother, the ancestors, and those currently walking the plains.

quest:8675.text: Skychaser the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Skychaser the Elder appears atop Sentinel Tower in Westfall. Travelers climb to honor her and receive her blessing in return. Sentinel Hill holds against Defias raiders and roving scavengers in Westfall's troubled scrublands. During the Lunar Festival, an ancestral spirit named Elder Skychaser appears on the open platform atop Sentinel Tower. From above the dust and wind, she watches over the weary soldiers and beleaguered settlers below. Anyone may climb the tower and pay her respect. Across Azeroth, the Lunar Festival honors wisdom, heritage, and the deeds of ancient spirits who walked the earth before today's struggles. When you approach, Elder Skychaser recognizes the living spark within you. She accepts your homage and gives you a token of her favor, a bond between the living and the honored dead.

quest:8677.text: Darkhorn the Elder. At the Lunar Festival, Darkhorn the Elder receives travelers in Orgrimmar. Honored among the ancestors, she embodies age, survival, and ancestral pride. During the Lunar Festival, revered ancestors appear across Azeroth to share wisdom with the living. Elder Darkhorn rests within Orgrimmar’s fortified ramparts, watching the young warrior city. You can approach her to honor those who walked the earth generations ago, whether you fight for the Horde or brave the gates as an Alliance traveler. Travelers greet Elder Darkhorn and pay her reverence, and she recognizes the spark of life in them. For honoring the old ways, you receive a Coin of Ancestry and her blessing. The tokens celebrate victory over ancient perils and remind the living to cherish the strength handed down through unbroken bloodlines.

quest:8678.text: Proudhorn the Elder. Proudhorn the Elder is an ancestral tauren spirit honored during the Lunar Festival atop the heights of Thunder Bluff. Visiting him is an act of deep reverence, acknowledging the wisdom of the ancestors who watch over Mulgore and the Horde. Perched high on the windblown mesas of Thunder Bluff, Proudhorn the Elder manifests as an ancestral presence during the Lunar Festival. Tauren culture holds the voices of their ancestors in the highest regard, believing that the spirits of ancient leaders and sages linger to offer guidance and strength to the living. Travelers who climb the heights to pay their respects to Elder Proudhorn are greeted not as strangers, but as vital flames of life. In exchange for the traveler's homage, the elder bestows a Coin of Ancestry, symbolizing communion between the enduring past and the living champions fighting for the world's future.

quest:8680.text: Windtotem the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Windtotem the Elder receives travelers on a bluff above Ratchet. She welcomes those who honor the wisdom of ages past and offers an ancestral blessing and guidance to other elders across Kalimdor. On a grassy hill just northwest of Ratchet’s flight master, Windtotem the Elder watches over the goblin docks and open sea. Iron, gunpowder, and coin pass through the harbor below, while quiet Barrens winds and a shaft of celestial light reach the elder. During the Lunar Festival, Windtotem the Elder guides wandering mortals, as do the other ancestral spirits. Those who seek her receive her blessing and a token of her favor, along with whispers pointing to nearby elders across the continent, including Elder Runetotem and Elder Bloodhoof.

quest:869.text: Raptor Thieves. A raptor has stolen the guards' payroll from the Crossroads tower, leaving the defenders baffled. Gazrog calls for a cull to keep the beasts from striking again. The Crossroads depends on mercenary and grunt guards to keep trade routes open across the Barrens. Their pay matters to morale and discipline. When silver vanished from the guard tower, leaders expected Centaur raiders or Quilboar scavengers. Instead, a raptor was caught stealing in the dead of night, leaving the settlement stunned and short of coin. Gazrog does not know why wild beasts would hoard shiny coins, and he has no interest in studying their behavior. The guards are restless without their pay, so he calls for blood and deterrence. He sends hunters to take a dozen raptor heads from across the savannah, hoping to curb the predators' boldness before a full search for the silver begins.

quest:87.text: Goldtooth. Near Fargodeep Mine, Auntie Bernice Stonefield's necklace is missing, and the Stonefield and Maclure families blame each other. Billy Maclure admits he lost it while playing nearby, and you follow the trail to the kobold Goldtooth. Auntie Bernice Stonefield's missing necklace has stirred up trouble between the Stonefield and Maclure families. Bernice suspects her rivals, but Billy Maclure lost the trinket while playing near Fargodeep Mine. He tries to hide his guilt, saying he only found the necklace before a creature snatched it away. Billy says a large kobold with gleaming fangs took the shiny necklace and ran to a den above Fargodeep Mine. Goldtooth actually lurks on the mine's lower level. Slaying the kobold brings Bernice's necklace back, settles the families' dispute, and earns you an old campaign keepsake left by Bernice's late husband.

quest:870.text: The Forgotten Pools. At the Forgotten Pools, life surges through the dry Barrens for reasons the Cenarion Circle cannot explain. Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads sends Horde adventurers to inspect the oasis northwest of the settlement, where druids sense unseen forces beneath the earth. The Barrens once flourished as fertile land before ages of war and the Sundering shattered the continent. The region became sun-baked scrubland, but lush oases have recently begun taking root in its dry basin. Druids of the Cenarion Circle find this sudden growth unnatural. They sense powers beneath the earth pressing upward, stirring vegetation and wildlife into life in scattered pockets across the wastes.

quest:871.text: Disrupt the Attacks. Thork needs the Crossroads defended as Razormane quilboar cut its supply roads. Their ambushes have halted caravans from Durotar, and the outpost is running short on food and gear. You strike at the quilboar while scouts search for the one directing their warband. The Crossroads guards a key junction for Horde traffic through central Kalimdor. Freight wagons and caravans bring food, iron, and equipment west from Durotar, and the outpost depends on those supplies. Razormane ambushes along the northeast trails have stopped the deliveries. Stores are running low, and Thork cannot wait for peaceful talks. Thork sends you against the quilboar bramble dens northeast of the settlement before they can assault the town walls. Striking their Water Seekers, Thornweavers, and Hunters weakens the Razormane scouting perimeter and deprives raiding parties of magical and logistical support. These skirmishes buy time while Horde trackers search the brush for the one organizing the raids.

quest:8717.text: Moonwarden the Elder. At the Crossroads, Moonwarden the Elder receives travelers beneath a beam of light. During the Lunar Festival, people honor ancestral spirits and seek his wisdom and directions to elders across Kalimdor. At the Crossroads, a column of light falls around Elder Moonwarden. He is one of the ancient spirits honored during the Lunar Festival, when mortals set aside their conflicts to seek the wisdom of generations past. Elder Moonwarden looks to the stars for answers to earthly mysteries. He offers ancestral blessings and directs seekers to other elders across Kalimdor, including Elder Bloodhoof, Elder High Mountain, Elder Morningdew, and Elder Runetotem.

quest:8718.text: Bladeswift the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Bladeswift the Elder's ancient spirit is honored in Darnassus. In the Cenarion Enclave, travelers seek his wisdom beneath the stars and a blessing tied to night elven tradition. During the Lunar Festival, revered ancestral spirits appear across Azeroth to share wisdom and bless travelers. In Darnassus, Bladeswift the Elder appears among the boughs of the Cenarion Enclave. This ancient spirit turns his gaze to the night sky and its mysteries, while the living face the trials of the present. Night elves have long looked to the heavens as reflections of Elune and signs of deeper truths. Bladeswift urges the wise and fortunate to seek answers among the stars. Those who honor him receive a Coin of Ancestry and join a ceremony that links the living with spirits of the past.

quest:872.text: The Disruption Ends. Thork orders a strike against the Razormane raids on the Horde road. Kreenig Snarlsnout leads the attacks from the northern Barrens, and his death is meant to break the warband's hold on the route between Durotar and the Crossroads. The road between Durotar and the Crossroads carries provisions and reinforcements through the northern Barrens. Razormane quilboar ambushes have kept it under threat. Scout reports name their leader as Kreenig Snarlsnout, whose raiding party organizes the attacks. Thork orders a strike against Kreenig, hoping to break the warband's unity and secure the road. Kreenig's war party is entrenched in craggy hills northeast of the Crossroads. Hardy Razormane Defenders and geomancers who manipulate the arid earth shield his position. Thork's order is to break through that guard and strike Kreenig in his redoubt, sending a warning across the plains. His tusk will prove the leader's death and show that the Horde will not accept attacks on its lifelines.

quest:8721.text: Starweave the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Elder Starweave receives visitors in Auberdine. Travelers come to honor Kalimdor's ancestral spirits and seek her wisdom and blessing. During the Lunar Festival, ancestral spirits appear across Azeroth beneath pillars of celestial light. Elder Starweave joins the night elves in Auberdine, a harbor on Darkshore's coast. Travelers come to honor her and seek guidance from ages past. Elder Starweave looks to the heavens above Kalimdor. She tells visitors that the stars hold answers to mortal doubts and worldly riddles. Those who seek her counsel are urged to look skyward for truth and receive ancestral favor, along with tidings of other wandering spirits across the wild frontier.

quest:8725.text: Riversong the Elder. Elder Riversong is an ancestral night elf spirit honored during the Lunar Festival, found resting beneath a quiet shrine in Astranaar. Bathed in a beam of moonlight, she offers quiet wisdom to travelers and directs pilgrims toward other revered ancestors across the lands of Kalimdor. Amid the ancient boughs and wooden walkways of Astranaar, Elder Riversong appears under an open night elf shrine. Marked by a distinct column of celestial light piercing the Ashenvale canopy, her ethereal presence serves as a focal point for participants in the Lunar Festival seeking communion with past generations. Elder Riversong reminds pilgrims of the ancient night elven tradition of reading truth and mystery in the starry sky. Her words direct travelers to seek wisdom through patience and contemplation, guiding those honoring the season on toward fellow spirits, including Elder Starweave.

quest:875.text: Harpy Lieutenants. At the Crossroads, Darsok Swiftdagger sends Horde champions against the Witchwing coven in the northern Barrens. In the Dry Hills, the aim is to kill the flock’s front-line officers and break its chain of command. After the first clashes with Witchwing raiders, Darsok Swiftdagger turns the offensive toward the harpies roosting in the Dry Hills. Horde scouts are sent after the Witchwing Slayers who lead the flock. These officers keep the lesser harpies in line and coordinate raids against Horde supply paths. Their deaths are critical to securing the northern approaches of the Barrens. Witchwing Slayers lead through strength and dominance, and only the most vicious among them carry ornate rings that mark their authority within the matriarchy. Taking the rings proves the lieutenants are dead, disrupts the roost’s coordination, and sends the coven a clear message: attacks on Horde territory will meet decisive retribution.

quest:877.text: The Stagnant Oasis. Tonga Runetotem sends you southeast from the Crossroads to search the Stagnant Oasis. He wants to know if the hidden fissure beneath the Forgotten Pools has a match in its murky waters. Tonga Runetotem sends you to the Stagnant Oasis after a strange fissure is found beneath the Forgotten Pools. He suspects the sudden patches of lush growth across the Barrens have a cause beneath the earth. You search the oasis's murky shallows for another opening, among predators that haunt the water.

quest:88.text: Princess Must Die!. At Stonefield Farm, Ma Stonefield wants Princess Must Die! before Princess ruins the harvest. The enormous prize-winning sow from Brackwell Pumpkin Patch keeps raiding the Stonefields’ vegetables, and Ma wants the family to gather their crops in peace. Princess has put the Stonefield harvest at risk. The prize-winning sow belongs to the Brackwells, but she has grown enormous by crossing onto the Stonefield plots and devouring their vegetables. Ma Stonefield has had enough of the sow eating the crops she worked to grow. She wants Princess put down before the pig ruins the season’s yield. Princess does not roam alone. At Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, east beyond the Maclure homestead, protective boars surround her. To prove the sow will trouble the Stonefield fields no more, you need to get past her guards and bring back the distinctive brass collar from her neck.

quest:880.text: Altered Beings. At the Crossroads, Tonga Runetotem studies strange changes in the Barrens' oasis waters. Fissures beneath the pools may be changing the creatures that live there, and he asks you to bring him shells from altered snapjaws. Tonga Runetotem is searching for the cause of strange changes in the Barrens' oases. Though the savanna is dry, a handful of pools support fertile ground. Tonga found peculiar fissures beneath those waters, sending out potent energies. He does not know whether the force came from outside or rose from deep within the earth. Now he studies the creatures that drink from and live in the pools, hoping to learn what the fissures are doing to them. You are sent to the Lushwater Oasis and the Stagnant Oasis to gather altered snapjaw shells. Snapjaws live in the shallows, where they take in the strange essence through food and exposure. Their carapaces have changed, offering Tonga a sign of how the fissures affect local wildlife. He hopes the shells will help him understand the disturbance before it spreads farther across Kalimdor.

quest:881.text: Echeyakee. At the Crossroads, hunters prepare to face Whitemist in the northern Barrens. Sergra Darkthorn sends young Horde hunters to summon the legendary white lion and test their strength. Across the central plains, a white-maned lion rules the savannah cats. Taur-ahe speakers call him Echeyakee, or Whitemist. Legend says he moves so silently that he seems like morning mist gliding over the red earth. His strikes come swiftly, leaving prey no time for fear or suffering. Local hunters revere him as a sign of mercy and swift death. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn trains fledgling warriors. The experienced orc shaman sends her pupils to challenge the king of beasts after they have proven themselves against lesser savannah prowlers. With a special horn, you travel northeast past the mountain ridges to a graveyard of massive kodo bones. Sound the horn to challenge Echeyakee and draw the elusive predator from hiding for a test of strength and cunning.

quest:882.text: Ishamuhale. At Camp Taurajo, Jorn Skyseer sends you to face Ishamuhale, the fiercest sunscale raptor in the Barrens. The hunt tests your skill and respect for nature's deadliest predators. Sunscale raptors hunt the Barrens in cunning, vicious packs, but none inspires more dread than Speartooth. Jorn Skyseer says Ishamuhale kills by instinct and passion, not for food or territory. He hunts because killing is his nature. To face him is to test whether you can withstand a predator's unbridled ferocity. Ishamuhale will not be found resting in a nest. To draw him out, you follow the plains' natural rhythm. Jorn tells you to kill a fresh zhevra and carry its carcass to a lone, withered dead tree on the plains northwest of Ratchet. The scent of blood on the arid wind brings Ishamuhale swiftly to claim his prey. When you bring Ishamuhale's fang back to Camp Taurajo, Jorn Skyseer sees it as a profound spiritual milestone, not merely a sign of victory. Tauren belief holds that overcoming so fierce a predator lets you absorb some of its raw strength. The test then turns inward: you must carry that might with temperance, honor, and restraint, rather than surrender to blind bloodlust.

quest:8828.text: Winter's Presents. In Orgrimmar, Winter's Presents await beneath the festive tree during the Feast of Winter Veil. Holiday organizers and goblin apparatus tenders direct Horde heroes to Great-father Winter, where gifts have been prepared for them. The Feast of Winter Veil brings a pause for celebration to Orgrimmar as the chill winds of late year sweep across Durotar. Promoters from Smokywood Pastures and holiday enthusiasts spread word through the capital that gifts wait beneath the decorated tree. Warriors, hunters, and wanderers resting in the city are all invited to share in the season’s generosity. Great-father Winter sits among holiday ribbons and packaged cartons near the Smokywood Pastures market. The ancient figure marks the season’s renewal, while goblin merchants nearby offer seasonal wares and festive treats to visitors.

quest:8851.text: Five Signets for War Supplies. Orgrimmar's stores gather supplies for the Horde's campaign across Kalimdor. Workers earn commendation signets for their contributions, and Warlord Gorchuk exchanges them for supplies to equip the fighters. Across Kalimdor, the Horde gathers raw goods, weapons, and provisions for a vast campaign. Gatherers and tradesfolk bring bandages, metals, and herbs into the cities, where military overseers award commendation signets for their work. The tokens mark each contribution to the stockpile growing along Orgrimmar's central avenues. Warlord Gorchuk knows the wider war effort needs supplies, but each warrior also needs gear and provisions to survive the march into battle. Fighters can trade their commendation signets back into the Horde's stores for field supplies and surplus materiel, giving up personal recognition for what they need on the front.

quest:8866.text: Bronzebeard the Elder. Bronzebeard the Elder is a Lunar Festival encounter with Elder Bronzebeard within the dwarven mountain city of Ironforge. Honoring him during this ancestral celebration rewards travelers with wisdom and a token of his esteem. It reflects the deep reverence the folk of Khaz Modan hold for their forebears and long-lived heritage. During the Lunar Festival, spirits and venerable elders manifest across Azeroth to share their wisdom with travelers honoring the past. In Ironforge, Elder Bronzebeard stands as an embodiment of the stalwart resilience of the Bronzebeard clan. When approached by adventurers seeking to pay their respects, he expresses quiet satisfaction that the people of this land still acknowledge and honor the lineage of the olden races. The encounter requires no great trial or perilous expedition, asking only that travelers pause, acknowledge the elder's presence, and offer greeting. In turn, Elder Bronzebeard extends his well wishes and bestows a Coin of Ancestry. These sacred festival tokens serve as physical reminders of the living connection between modern heroes and the generations who forged Khaz Modan from stone and fire.

quest:887.text: Southsea Freebooters. Along the Merchant Coast south of Ratchet, Southsea Freebooters strike goblin trading vessels. Gazlowe hires adventurers to attack their camp and curb the raids. Ratchet's trade suffers from pirates on the Merchant Coast. The port sits in central Kalimdor, where merchant vessels travel between Kalimdor and the eastern continents. South of town, Southsea Freebooters hold a fortified beach camp. From there, they attack goblin cargo ships arriving and departing, cutting into profits and disrupting local shipping lanes. Gazlowe blames the pirates and the Steamwheedle Cartel's naval leaders. The Trade Princes have spent immense sums on defensive fleets, yet Vice Admiral Grezzlik has failed to patrol the waters effectively. Frustrated by Undermine's slow response, Gazlowe hires independent mercenaries to thin the pirate brigands and cannoneers.

quest:888.text: Stolen Booty. Pirate cargo off Ratchet’s coast has left Gazlowe choosing what matters most. Stolen Booty brings him two vital goods: boots for local laborers and a delicate telescopic lens needed to complete his observatory. The Southsea Freebooters have troubled merchant lanes across the Great Sea for years. Their fortified camp just south of Ratchet brought them into direct conflict with Gazlowe. Pirates intercepted merchant vessels bound for the port and took valuable supplies from the Steamwheedle Cartel. Some goods could be written off as a cost of shipping. Specialized cargo mattered enough for Gazlowe to hire mercenaries to break into the pirate stronghold. Gazlowe has two practical priorities. Drizzlik sent a needed shipment of boots from Booty Bay for local laborers. The other item is specialized: a ground telescopic lens made for the observatory tower overlooking Ratchet. Its twin arrived safely by caravan through Durotar, but pirates seized this lens at sea. Until it is recovered, the observatory remains an empty frame.

quest:890.text: The Missing Shipment. In Ratchet, Gazlowe waits for goods sent from Booty Bay across the Great Sea. He sends couriers to Wharfmaster Dizzywig to check the dock records, while the Southsea Freebooters remain a possible cause of the delay. Ratchet is the Steamwheedle Cartel's trading port on Kalimdor. Ships cross the Great Sea from Booty Bay with manufactured goods, exotic supplies, and heavy freight for the town's building and trade. When cargo goes missing, business suffers. Chief Engineer Gazlowe keeps close track of every crate brought into port. The Southsea Freebooters haunt the coast south of Ratchet and often intercept merchant ships. Gazlowe checks his records before accusing the pirates or sending anyone into a fight. He sends his inventory ledger to Wharfmaster Dizzywig at the docks. Dizzywig oversees the unloading and storage of ship cargo, and can check whether goods were lost at sea or misplaced in a warehouse.

quest:892.text: The Missing Shipment. At Ratchet’s docks, Dizzywig’s ledger points away from harbor graft and toward the Southsea Freebooters.
