Gazlowe receives the records and prepares to reclaim his lost cargo. Ratchet’s trade and its port bring constant logistical headaches. When a shipment fails to arrive, Gazlowe suspects bad harbor accounts or foul play on the piers. Wharfmaster Dizzywig examines the manifest and insists his books are clean. The intake records account for everything, so the missing merchandise never made it onto the dock.

quest:894.text: Samophlange. At a Venture Company outpost in the northern Barrens, Sputtervalve wants a device called a samophlange. He sends you southwest of the Sludge Fen to find it. In the northern Barrens, Sputtervalve cannot explain what the Venture Company is building. The goblin engineer and tinker works in Ratchet, while the rival company experiments southwest of the Sludge Fen. Its people call one device a samophlange. Sputtervalve does not know its purpose or value, but wants to study its design before his competitors can profit from it. The Venture Company guards its research site with armed overseers, deforesters, and machinery. Sputtervalve gives you an intercepted operating manual to help shut down the rig safely. At the central control station, you find a locked console with levers, lights, and gauges. Three control valves keep the rig's pressure in order.

quest:895.text: WANTED: Baron Longshore. On Ratchet's docks, Chief Engineer Gazlowe posts a bounty for Baron Longshore. The pirate captain hails from Gilneas and commands vessels of the Southsea Freebooters. His presence along the Merchant Coast threatens goblin merchant shipping across the region. South of Ratchet, the Southsea Freebooters hold fortified camps along the Merchant Coast. Their pirates harass merchant vessels and disrupt the sea lanes the Steamwheedle Cartel relies on between Ratchet, Booty Bay, and points beyond. Under captains such as Baron Longshore, the raids drain the local goblin administration and threaten trade along the coast. Baron Longshore comes from Gilneas, the isolated human kingdom across the sea. On Kalimdor, he commands the pirate vessel Heedless and leads crews ashore just north of Northwatch Hold. Chief Engineer Gazlowe answers with a bounty, calling for Longshore's identifiable head.

quest:896.text: Miner's Fortune. Wharfmaster Dizzywig has heard of a fist-sized emerald at the Venture Company's Boulder Lode Mine. He hires you to take the Cats Eye Emerald from the mine's supervisors and share the profits. Wharfmaster Dizzywig hears the merchants who pass through Ratchet's harbor on the routes between Ratchet and Booty Bay. Word reaches him of a huge gem found deep in the Boulder Lode Mine. The Venture Company strips the northern Barrens for its own gain, so few are likely to ask questions if its finest recent find disappears. Northeast of the Sludge Fen, laborers fill the Boulder Lode Mine's rocky shaft. The Venture Co. Overseers and Enforcers have taken the Cats Eye Emerald, and an ordinary digger cannot claim a prize so rare. You need to face the armed managers, secure the stone, and bring it to Dizzywig. He can judge its value against the market in Undermine.

quest:900.text: Samophlange. At the Sludge Fen, Samophlange machinery keeps the Venture Company's digging rig running. Three valves must be sealed before the central apparatus can be shut down safely. At the Sludge Fen, the Venture Company's machinery is complex and dangerous. The central console makes clear that the core cannot be stopped with a single switch. Its feed lines must be handled by hand first, or the apparatus could fail or explode. Three valves control the flow into the rig: the Main Control Valve, the Fuel Control Valve, and the Regulator Valve. Each must be sealed by hand against high pressure. As they close, the console's green indicators fade to yellow, making it safe to engage the central shutoff.

quest:901.text: Samophlange. At the Sludge Fen, the Venture Company’s machinery waits with its valves shut and its pressure relieved. Tinkerer Sniggles holds the key to open the control unit and free the samophlange within. You have relieved the pressure by turning the auxiliary valves, and the dials and gauges have settled. The housing remains locked against tampering. Its key rests with the goblin engineer overseeing the drilling site. Tinkerer Sniggles oversees the Venture Company’s equipment at the Sludge Fen. He keeps the console key in a hut just northeast of the main rig. You need that key to open the housing and reach the samophlange.

quest:902.text: Samophlange. At the Venture Company console, you uncover the elusive samophlange and carry it to Ratchet. You have shut down the controls and their defenses; now the delicate device is ready for Sputtervalve to examine. Behind the Venture Company console's faceplate, wiring and purposeless tubing crowd around strange engineering. Deep inside lies the samophlange, a core component that has baffled engineers across the region. With a firm tug, you free the device from its housing and carry it back to the goblin who began the recovery effort.

quest:903.text: Prowlers of the Barrens. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn sends you after the savannah prowlers. Their claws will show whether you can face the Barrens' greatest beasts. Sergra Darkthorn tests hunters who have already faced the plainstriders and zhevras. Southwest of the Crossroads, savannah prowlers vanish into the central Barrens' gold and ochre scrub. These great cats hunt instead of grazing with the herds. They wait in tall grass, then ambush their prey, and unwary travelers can fall to them. Sergra warns you that prowlers know how to hunt. Read the grasses and strike before a cat leaps if you mean to claim its paws and claws. Bring back seven prowler claws to show you have the cunning and quick reflexes to survive against Kalimdor's deadliest wildlife.

quest:905.text: The Angry Scytheclaws. South of the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn sends hunters to face the savage scytheclaws stalking the Barrens. Bring sunscale raptor feathers to their breeding nests, and prove your courage in a land that gives little quarter. Sergra Darkthorn tests hunters against the beasts of the Barrens. After lesser trials, she sends you south of the Crossroads to hunt vicious sunscale raptors and take their feathers. Then you carry those feathers southwest of the Stagnant Oasis, into the heart of raptor territory. Placing them in the nests is the true test: it shows you can face the scytheclaws without fear. Three raptor nests lie southwest of the Stagnant Oasis, near the Gold Road. Red, blue, and yellow eggs mark the separate clutches. Scytheclaws defend their nests fiercely against anything that comes near. Place the feathers of fallen raptors among the eggs, and you make your challenge clear to the beasts. Return to the Crossroads after entering the nests, and Sergra can see you have faced the danger and lived. Walking out of a raptor den takes raw courage. The Barrens test every hunter; each fight may harden you, or leave your bones among the kodo ribs scattered across the dirt.

quest:907.text: Enraged Thunder Lizards. In the southern Barrens, thunder lizards roam the plains around Camp Taurajo. Jorn Skyseer calls hunters to face the great beasts and bring back their blood as part of a wider rite of passage. After defeating the raptor Ishamuhale, you return to Camp Taurajo. The tauren elder Jorn Skyseer now tests your strength against the largest grazers of the land. Stormsnouts and Thunderheads roam the southern Barrens, their heavy strides able to crush an unwary hunter beneath them. Tauren and orc hunters prize poise, position, and strength when facing a thunder lizard. Jorn asks you to bring back samples of their potent blood, proof that you stood in the path of the rumbling beasts and survived with your bones unbroken. The trophy opens the way to Jorn's final quarry in the skies.

quest:916.text: Webwood Venom. In Shadowglen, Gilshalan Windwalker studies the giant webwood spiders of Shadowthread Cave. He asks young night elves to gather venom sacs so he can learn how Teldrassil's growth has affected the forest's wildlife. Gilshalan Windwalker has come to Shadowglen to study the webwood spiders in Shadowthread Cave. They are far larger and more aggressive than their cousins elsewhere. He suspects Teldrassil's immense magical energies are changing the local wildlife. He asks for venom sacs to compare with those of ordinary spiders and learn what has changed. Webwood spiders live in and around Shadowthread Cave, where they threaten young night elves in the glen. Gathering their venom can help thin their numbers and give Darnassian researchers evidence of Teldrassil's effect on the wild.

quest:917.text: Webwood Egg. In Shadowglen, Gilshalan Windwalker seeks an unhatched Webwood Egg for his study of Teldrassil’s wildlife. After gathering venom samples, he needs a living specimen to examine the unnatural aggression afflicting the forest’s creatures. An egg can be studied safely without subduing a full-grown spider. Gilshalan Windwalker needs live subjects to understand the unnatural corruption affecting the Webwood spiders around Shadowglen. You have secured raw venom from the aggressive spiders, but carrying a thrashing giant out of the depths would be deadly for a novice. Gilshalan asks you to bring back an unhatched egg from the brooding clutches inside Shadowthread Cave. Webwood spiders brood in Shadowthread Cave, where the forest’s increasingly hostile arachnids make their nests. An intact egg gives scholars a controlled subject that can hatch under containment. Gilshalan plans to bundle it with his venom samples and send both to Darnassus for examination. With his local study complete, he directs recruits toward higher duties in the boughs of Aldrassil.

quest:918.text: Timberling Seeds. At Lake Al'Ameth, botanist Denalan studies the growing hostility of Teldrassil's nature elementals. He seeks to harvest Timberling Seeds and test whether enriched soil can help them grow calmer. His work is one quiet effort by night elf herbalists to understand the subtle afflictions troubling the World Tree. Timberlings are nature elementals native to Teldrassil's boughs, closely bound to the health and vitality of the surrounding flora. They are usually peaceful reflections of the forest's balance, but their recent hostility has alarmed the local night elves, and no cause is known. Botanist Denalan hopes to learn what has stirred them rather than simply cull them. Denalan suspects the blemish lies deep in the ground. He hopes to sprout fresh timberlings, a gentler generation of elementals, in enriched and carefully treated loam. By harvesting seeds from wandering timberlings near Lake Al'Ameth, he aims to learn whether the land's corruption can be countered from the roots up.

quest:919.text: Timberling Sprouts. Around Lake Al'Ameth, Timberling Sprouts are spreading across Teldrassil. Denalan asks you to uproot them before they grow into hostile timberlings. Corrupted sprouts are spreading along Lake Al'Ameth's banks. Denalan lives beside the lake and knows these young plants cannot be healed. Left alone, they quickly grow into aggressive, bark-covered timberlings that threaten wildlife and travelers. Uprooting the sprouts helps protect the grove. Denalan is troubled by how quickly new sprouts appear across Teldrassil. Their spread points to a sickness in the World Tree's roots and soil, and Denalan and the druids of Darnassus seek its cause.

quest:920.text: Tenaron's Summons. In Shadowglen, Tenaron's Summons calls you to Aldrassil. After helping Gilshalan Windwalker with woodland dangers, you are asked to meet Tenaron Stormgrip high in the great tree. The call draws you from local troubles toward the spiritual afflictions touching Teldrassil. Your work against the venomous spiders and corrupted wildlife in the glen has reached Tenaron Stormgrip. Gilshalan Windwalker tells you the elder has asked for your presence. Even night elves, with their long lives, know better than to keep an elder waiting atop Aldrassil. Tenaron waits in Aldrassil's highest chamber, looking across Shadowglen's boughs. Meeting him brings you into wider concerns of stewardship, including the cleansing of Teldrassil's moonwells and the corruption spreading through the young World Tree's ecosystem.

quest:921.text: Crown of the Earth. At Aldrassil, Tenaron Stormgrip asks young night elves to draw sacred water before they leave Shadowglen. The rite recalls Mount Hyjal and the immortality their people gave up there. Before young night elves leave Shadowglen, their elders teach them what their people lost. At the Battle of Mount Hyjal, the kaldorei sacrificed the World Tree Nordrassil to defeat Archimonde and banish the Burning Legion. The blast cost them their ageless immortality and sacred shield. Tenaron Stormgrip teaches this history as he gives novices a rite, preparing them with humility and purpose for a changing world. To complete the rite, you draw water from the moonwell north of Aldrassil with a crystal phial. Moonwell waters carry remnants of the ancient Well of Eternity. Druids channel their restorative power into the wild, while Sentinels honor the wells as tranquil shrines to Elune. The kaldorei remain wary: arcane sorcery is forbidden, and the wellspring that sustains their land recalls the reckless magic that nearly broke the world.

quest:92124.text: Book Inventory. At Northshire Abbey, Brother Paxton is frustrated by misplaced and missing tomes. He asks young adventurers to find Daniel, his daydreaming assistant, and take stock of the library archives, but Daniel's thoughts keep wandering to local tradeskills, making a straight answer hard to get. Northshire Abbey preserves old scholarly works, spiritual writings, and historical records that survived the First War in the Kingdom of Stormwind. Brother Paxton, a meticulous monk, takes great pride in the collection. Lately, books have gone missing from the shelves, and Paxton needs a clear inventory to learn how widespread the loss is. He has little patience to chase after his daydreaming helper. Daniel works as Brother Paxton's assistant in the abbey library, but his thoughts rarely stay with parchment and catalog numbers. He is fascinated by the practical trades of Elwynn Forest: smithing, leatherworking, tailoring, and herbal craft. Paxton grows exasperated as inventory work leads Daniel to ramble about local crafters instead of locating lost scriptures.

quest:922.text: Rellian Greenspyre. At Denalan's lakeside retreat in Teldrassil, you carry a timberling seed to Rellian Greenspyre in Darnassus. The handoff brings news of trouble spreading through the World Tree's boughs. Denalan has studied the plants and elemental life around Lake Al'Ameth. After gathering seeds from the local timberlings, he sends you to Darnassus with a sample for his colleague, Rellian Greenspyre. Rellian is a druid who walks the Cenarion Enclave's terraces. He had shown interest in Denalan's research and hopes to grow a timberling of his own.

quest:923.text: Tumors. In Darnassus, the Cenarion Circle seeks to contain the sickness spreading through Teldrassil. You are sent to Wellspring Lake to gather mossy tumors from afflicted timberlings, so druids can study the poison and burn the growths safely. Teldrassil’s native plants and animals are being twisted by a strange affliction. Its timberlings, usually placid nature spirits with bark for skin, have grown hostile and erratic. Grotesque mossy tumors spread across their living wood, pulsing with unnatural poison. Cenarion scholars Denalan and Rellian Greenspyre search for the cause, while timberlings already lost to the sickness must be culled to protect the rest of the boughs. Wellspring Lake in northern Teldrassil has become a focal point of the outbreak, and its timberlings are among the most tainted on the World Tree. Rellian Greenspyre asks you to kill these corrupted guardians and cut away their tumors. Bring the growths to the druids in Darnassus, where they can be burned safely. The night elves hope this will slow the contagion while they search for the disease’s source.

quest:924.text: The Demon Seed. Neeru Fireblade's orders reach Ak'Zeloth, who sends Horde travelers to destroy the Demon Seed atop Dreadmist Peak. An unstable Flawed Power Stone can break the Burning Legion's conduit before its influence spreads farther through the Barrens. High in a cave on Dreadmist Peak, the Demon Seed hangs above an altar of fire. The artifact anchors demonic power in the heart of the Barrens for the Burning Legion. The orc Ak'Zeloth prepares specialized power stones to break its link to the Nether. One must reach the peak before the stone's unstable energy runs out.

quest:926.text: Flawed Power Stone. Across the Barrens, Flawed Power Stone rests on arcane tables, charged with arcane energy. Its makers left it fatally flawed, so it consumes its own power soon after it is moved. In the Barrens, flawed power stones hold arcane essence within compromised structures. Their makers deliberately left them unstable, so they decay into inert matter moments after someone handles them. A stone begins consuming its power as soon as it leaves the ritual table where it rests. Its energy burns away too quickly for anyone to carry it far.

quest:9260.text: Investigate the Scourge of Stormwind. Scourge forces press against Stormwind, with necropolises looming beyond its walls. Lieutenant Orrin calls defenders to strike their camps, gather Necrotic Stones, and study the runes there. Scourge forces have reached the outskirts of Stormwind City. Necropolises float overhead as undead and cultists take hold near the kingdom’s greatest bastion. Lieutenant Orrin gathers defenders outside the city to drive them back before they threaten the capital. Glowing runes mark the dirt around Scourge camps, and their purpose remains unclear. The circles crackle with magic like that of the necropolises and carry eerie whispers. Lieutenant Orrin can only guess who, if anyone, hears those unnatural voices.

quest:9262.text: Investigate the Scourge of Darnassus. Lieutenant Beitha calls for help as the Scourge encampments press close to Darnassus. The Argent Dawn needs defenders to strike the undead and learn what the runes outside the gates are for. The Scourge has reached Teldrassil, and floating necropolises loom above the invasion camps near Darnassus. Ghouls, skeletons, and other undead horrors spill from them. Lieutenant Beitha of the Argent Dawn coordinates the city's defense, calling on volunteers to slow the attack and gather information before the undead overwhelm the night elven homeland.

quest:9263.text: Investigate the Scourge of Orgrimmar. Outside Orgrimmar, the Scourge has raised a camp beneath a floating necropolis. Lieutenant Dagel calls on defenders to repel the undead, recover necrotic stones, and examine runic circles charged with necromantic energy. The attack brings the Lich King's reach to Durotar. The Scourge now threatens lands far from Lordaeron and the northern ice. Floating necropolises cast their shadows across Azeroth, even over Durotar. Undead forces have gathered at Orgrimmar's threshold, raising camps that threaten the Horde capital. Lieutenant Dagel and the Argent Dawn coordinate the defense, calling on local champions to drive the invaders back before they can secure a siege.

quest:927.text: The Moss-twined Heart. Near Lake Al'Ameth, Denalan studies a strange heart taken from Blackmoss the Fetid. Dark, oily moss covers the core, yet it keeps beating after being cut from the timberling. Blackmoss the Fetid's heart still pulses after being cut from the timberling. Dark, oily moss hides nearly all of the timberling's core, but a slow rhythm continues within it. That pulse points to a corruption reaching beyond ordinary rot in Teldrassil's wild plants. Denalan, a researcher of local flora near Lake Al'Ameth, takes a keen interest in the heart and recognizes its troubling corruption. Timberlings should be gentle beings tied to the boughs of the World Tree, yet this core bears a virulent blight. Troubled by what he sees and eager to understand it, Denalan plans to plant and study the organ, hoping to learn how foul moss takes root in the island's soil.

quest:92742.text: Testing the Wells. Alba Fairmoon sends you across Westfall to test the farm wells. The samples may reveal what is poisoning the soil and groundwater. Alba Fairmoon asks you to test Westfall's groundwater. Neglect and banditry have already hurt the open plains, and poison beneath the earth threatens the farmland that remains. You collect samples from farm wells so Alba can learn what is tainting the soil and water. You take samples from the wells at Jansen Stead and Molsen Farm. These homesteads lie among scattered farms exposed to Defias outlaws and feral wildlife. Their well water can show whether the blight is rising from the ground, caused by magic, or deliberately put into the water that feeds the region.

quest:92744.text: Murloc Gills. Alba Fairmoon sends Alliance help to Westfall's Longshore to gather murloc gills. She fears the crop blight may reach the Great Sea, and the gills could reveal whether the coastal waters are tainted. Westfall is already near ruin, with crops failing, farmers displaced, and bandits roaming the roads. Alba Fairmoon fears the blight may be draining from inland fields into the Great Sea. If the coast is tainted, the fish that feed Westfall's poor and grace Stormwind City's tables could vanish. That loss could tip an already strained kingdom into outright famine. Murlocs are stubborn and violent, but their amphibious bodies make them natural signs of water quality. Their breathing constantly filters seawater, leaving their gills exceptionally receptive to poisons, blight, and unnatural pollutants. Alba Fairmoon hopes to gauge the contamination by studying fresh gills from the murlocs prowling the Longshore.

quest:92745.text: The State of the Mines. Alba Fairmoon finds toxic metals in Westfall's wells and fears for its farmland. She suspects the mines seized by the Defias and warns the soil could fail for decades. You head to Jangolode Mine and Gold Coast Quarry to disrupt the mining. Alba Fairmoon finds dangerous levels of toxic metals in Westfall's wells. Once Stormwind's main breadbasket, the region now faces a threat to its crops. Alba suspects the mines seized by the Defias Brotherhood are poisoning the water. If the contamination continues, the surrounding earth could lie barren for decades. The Defias put local creatures to work alongside their highwaymen, stripping Westfall of its resources. Riverpaw gnolls dig for stone and minerals at Gold Coast Quarry, while kobold diggers tunnel through Jangolode Mine. Disrupting their labor weakens the Defias' ability to process and distribute contaminated minerals.

quest:92747.text: Moonbrook Espionage. Alba Fairmoon sends you to scout Moonbrook, where signs of industry trouble the Alliance. The poison found across Westfall does not seem to come from the lesser mines, so attention turns to the Deadmines beneath the town. The mines already examined across Westfall offer no answer to the poison spreading through the region. No known surface excavation appears to be its source. One major site remains unexplored: the vast shafts of the Deadmines, directly beneath Moonbrook’s ruined streets.

quest:92748.text: Explosive Consultation. In Westfall, toxic industry beneath the Deadmines is poisoning the farmland. You travel to Stormwind's Dwarven District to seek an engineer who can supply heavy explosives. Westfall faces displaced vagrants and banditry under the Defias Brotherhood. Evidence from across the region points to a coordinated, mechanised threat underground. Industrial refuse and caustic toxins foul the soil, and their trail leads into the Deadmines, where an organized operation works below the earth. Fortified tunnels and machinery in the Deadmines call for more than ordinary weapons. To stop the poison reaching Westfall's fields, you seek help in Stormwind City's Dwarven District. Roaring forges, tinkerers, and merchants selling blasting powder fill the district. There you look for Sprite Jumpsprocket, an engineer who can devise explosives for the work.

quest:92749.text: A Dynamite Plan. Sprite Jumpsprocket is eager to put dynamite to work in Stormwind. The inventive tinkerer in the Dwarven District has heard talk of industrial sabotage and wants a supply of coarse dynamite to begin her plan. Sprite Jumpsprocket, a gnome engineer in Stormwind's Dwarven District, welcomes talk of industrial sabotage. Rather than urge caution, she asks passing mercenaries to bring her a bundle of coarse dynamite. You can make coarse dynamite at an engineering workbench or trade with the city's craftsmen. Sprite asks for ten sticks, enough to disrupt the industrial schemes unfolding in the surrounding territories. Her plan shows the practical, perilous methods gnomes favor when facing mechanical and political disruptions.

quest:92750.text: Detonation at a Distance. Sprite Jumpsprocket needs a safer way to set off explosives, and Stormwind holds the answer. She sends you to Stormwind Intelligence for a remote detonator. Sprite Jumpsprocket wants to set off explosives from a safe distance. Goblins and gnomes are known for handling volatile chemicals recklessly, but some blasts demand care. A standard fuse can put the person lighting it in danger. Sprite knows a controlled explosion needs a special trigger, the kind common tinkerers do not keep on hand. Sprite sends you to Stormwind Intelligence in Old Town instead of to local dwarven blasters or ordinary engineering suppliers. The network is known as SI:7, and its covert agents handle sabotage, stealth, and targeted demolitions. Jasper Fel works among them in the capital and can provide discreet, dangerous equipment.

quest:92751.text: Detonation at a Distance. In Moonbrook, explosions beneath Westfall draw SI:7's attention. Jasper Fel, a Stormwind operative, sends a remote detonator kit to help handle the work from a safe distance. Jasper Fel and SI:7 watch events across Stormwind's lands, including Westfall's troubled border. When word reaches him of explosive work in Moonbrook, Fel already knows what is happening in the abandoned mining tunnels beneath the countryside.

quest:92752.text: Explosive Consultation. In Westfall, Sprite Jumpsprocket sends a volatile charge to Alba Fairmoon. The primed explosives must reach her safely, with the detonator undisturbed. Sprite Jumpsprocket has finished a bundle of Extra-Destructive Explosives for Alba Fairmoon. Carrying a live charge through wartime Westfall adds danger to a road already threatened by Defias bandits and feral beasts. Sprite Jumpsprocket warns you to mind the detonator. The cargo is meant to destroy the hidden industrial operation in the Deadmines, which is poisoning Westfall's farmland. Alba Fairmoon needs the explosives intact before she can use them.

quest:92753.text: Destruction in Deadmines. Deep beneath Moonbrook, Defias industry is poisoning the land. Alba Fairmoon suspects their metallurgical forge is the source of the blight and sends you to destroy it with explosives. Beneath Moonbrook, the Deadmines shelter a fortified complex that powers the Defias Brotherhood. Its heavy forge smelts metal and builds machinery. Alba Fairmoon believes this forge is the likely origin of the contamination blighting the area. Destroying it is her aim.

quest:928.text: Crown of the Earth. In Shadowglen, you set out with moonwell water for Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar. The journey carries you from secluded training into the wider work of protecting Teldrassil. After tasting the enchanted water of Shadowglen's moonwell, you meet Tenaron Stormgrip at the crown of Aldrassil. He seals the gathered water in a larger vessel and sends you beyond the sheltered glade. The road runs south toward Dolanaar, through woods where danger has grown harder to predict. Dolanaar is the first major village beyond Shadowglen, along the cobblestone paths through central Teldrassil. Its own moonwell lies at the heart of the village. Corithras Moonrage, an elder who oversees preservation across the boughs, waits there. The vessel you bring places you in the wider effort to protect the World Tree.

quest:92819.text: Destruction in Deadmines. In Westfall, Alba Fairmoon sends an operative to destroy the Defias forge in the Deadmines. The explosives are already planted, and Alba waits in the hills behind Moonbrook for the detonator. The Deadmines hold the Defias Brotherhood's strength beneath Westfall. Alba Fairmoon directs you to sabotage the forge hidden in the mines. The explosives are already planted beside it, and you return to Alba in the hills behind Moonbrook to set them off from a safe distance. She hopes destroying the forge will let Westfall's poisoned land begin to heal. The charge sits beside the forge deep in the Deadmines. A remote detonator lets you set it off from outside the caves, after you rejoin Alba Fairmoon in the hills behind Moonbrook. She hopes that with the forge destroyed, Westfall's poisoned land can begin to heal.

quest:929.text: Crown of the Earth. Near Starbreeze Village, you draw sacred water for Darnassus. Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar asks young night elves to replenish the city's moonwell, and the work teaches the history behind their care for Teldrassil's great boughs. You carry a jade phial made by druids to Starbreeze Village, where a lesser moonwell holds sanctified water. Its refined craft lets you draw and carry the luminous water without disturbing its purity. Darnassus's central moonwell depends on these scattered fonts, and the elders send initiates on foot so the city's fountains stay full of Elune's grace. The journey also teaches the young what it takes to nourish Teldrassil. Corithras Moonrage tells you of the sorrow that followed the Battle of Mount Hyjal. The sacrifice of Nordrassil, the ancestral World Tree, cost the night elves their immortality. Illidan Stormrage was unleashed amid the ruin, while Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage disappeared. Grief and isolation marked the days that followed, as the kaldorei turned to Teldrassil.

quest:931.text: The Shimmering Frond. Across Teldrassil, a curious plant shimmers among the roots and canopy. Travelers bring a cutting to Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth, hoping the botanist can explain its origin. In Teldrassil's boughs, a strange plant catches the light. Its fronds twist with a pulsing shimmer unlike the island's usual foliage. The glow draws the eye amid Teldrassil's young forest life.

quest:932.text: Twisted Hatred. Tallonkai Swiftroot sends trusted champions into Fel Rock to stop Lord Melenas. The satyr has rallied the cave’s grell into an organized force, threatening night elf settlements near Teldrassil. Satyrs recall an ancient betrayal that still stains kaldorei history. They were Highborne who gave themselves to the Burning Legion during the War of the Ancients. Now one has made a foothold on Teldrassil, the young World Tree meant to be a sanctuary. For defenders like Tallonkai Swiftroot, that presence is a bitter disgrace. Fel Rock lies north of the nearby paths, its corrupted caverns crawling with feral grell. Lord Melenas has gathered the chaotic creatures into a hostile force under his will. Tallonkai fears what the satyr may unleash on the World Tree’s boughs, and demands a swift, quiet end. He wants Melenas eliminated and his severed head brought back.

quest:933.text: Crown of the Earth. Corithras Moonrage sends you to the Pools of Arlithrien for water as Gnarlpine furbolgs turn violent. His account of Teldrassil begins with Malfurion Stormrage's disappearance after the Third War. Corithras Moonrage sends you with a tourmaline phial to a moonwell southeast of Darnassus's entrance, along the Pools of Arlithrien. The Gnarlpine furbolgs, once peaceful, now lash out with sudden violence. They ambush travelers and harry Sentinel patrols across the region. What seemed like isolated skirmishes has become a threat to the night elves' new home. When you return with the filled phial, Corithras tells you how Teldrassil came to be. After the Third War, Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage vanished, leaving the Cenarion druids without a leader and divided. Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm took the mantle of leadership in his absence. He urged the Circle of Ancients in Darkshore to set aside their mourning. The night elves, he argued, had to regain their lost immortality and heal their civilization by planting a vast new World Tree.

quest:934.text: Crown of the Earth. At the Oracle Glade, Corithras Moonrage sends you to gather water from Teldrassil’s sacred moonwell. The journey reveals the truth behind the World Tree’s creation. Corithras Moonrage sends you northwest across Teldrassil to the Oracle Glade. Beneath the Oracle Tree’s great boughs lies the first and most powerful moonwell raised on the island. You draw water into an Amethyst Phial from its sacred pool. The moonwell is the sanctuary where druids and the tree itself watch over the health of their new homeland.

quest:935.text: Crown of the Earth. In Teldrassil, moonwell waters are gathered to tend the World Tree’s sickness. The rites lead to Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus, where concern grows over a tree raised without blessings. Teldrassil rose after the Third War to give the night elves a new home and restore their lost immortality. The Great Aspects Alexstrasza and Nozdormu withheld their blessings and refused to sanction its creation. Without their divine protection, sickness spreads through the tree. Strange creatures emerge from its boughs, and once-peaceful furbolg tribes fall into madness.

quest:937.text: The Enchanted Glade. Bloodfeather harpies threaten the Oracle Glade on northwestern Teldrassil, where Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak guards the ancient Oracle Tree. After harpies kill a runner bound for Darnassus, Arynia calls for their nests to be thinned and their belts brought back as proof. Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak watches over the Oracle Glade with an escort of warriors. The sacred retreat centers on the colossal Oracle Tree, an ancient rooted among Teldrassil's boughs. Bloodfeather harpies have spread through the surrounding canopy, nesting in the hollows and threatening anyone who comes near. A runner carrying an urgent report from the Oracle Tree never reaches Darnassus. Bloodfeather harpies ambush and kill the messenger before the runner can leave the glade. Arynia calls on you to thin their flock and bring back Bloodfeather belts as proof that their nests have been weakened.

quest:938.text: Mist. In Teldrassil's shaded boughs, Mist lies wounded and separated from her companion. She needs a safe path back to Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak at a nearby moon well. A gray sabercat named Mist lies wounded among Teldrassil's undergrowth. Deep slashes mark her back and belly. Her blue eyes are bright, and she stays calm rather than acting like a feral beast. She looks to friendly travelers for guidance and protection.

quest:940.text: Teldrassil. After the harpies are driven back, Arynia Cloudsbreak sends you with a report to Darnassus. The inscribed bark tells Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm about the boughs and the corruption still troubling the World Tree. Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak entrusts you with a piece of inscribed bark after you clear the harpies from their nests in the Oracle Glade. The Oracle Tree watches over the forest, and with the harpies gone, Arynia can send word to the kaldorei leadership. You carry her report through the wilderness to Darnassus, the great forest of stone, and deliver it to Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm. Fandral Staghelm receives the report with mixed feelings. He is grateful to hear that the harpies have been pushed back, but the report shows how one threat gives way to another across Teldrassil. Staghelm championed the planting of the new World Tree to reclaim the night elves' lost immortality. The afflictions in its boughs remind him that his work remains far from finished.

quest:941.text: Planting the Heart. At Lake Al'Ameth, you help Denalan tend a wooden heart taken from a corrupted timberling. After clearing away its moss, he asks you to place it in his planter and see whether it can be healed. Denalan has scraped the foul moss from the wooden heart taken from Blackmoss the Fetid, a corrupted timberling. Yet an unnatural taint still pulses within the wood. Trusting his years of botany and soil tending, the herbalist asks you to bury the heart directly in his personal planter. He hopes the rich nutrients he blended can draw its remaining natural vitality back toward health.

quest:944.text: The Master's Glaive. In southern Darkshore, Onu sends Alliance scouts to investigate the Master's Glaive. He fears the Twilight's Hammer cult may have reached the fallen ancient horror. Along Darkshore, Onu sees corruption linger and wildlife driven from its homes. The naga on the coast trouble him, but signs of the Twilight's Hammer are worse. Its followers worship primal lords who ruled the world before they were overthrown in ages past. South of Onu, the Master's Glaive is a grim excavation around a colossal creature pierced by a great stone weapon. Onu gives you a Phial of Scrying and asks you to enter the pit and learn whether the cultists have gathered there. The behemoth has been dead for eons, yet corruptive power still clings to its bones. The Twilight's Hammer may seek to claim it.

quest:947.text: Cave Mushrooms. Barithras Moonshade sends you behind Cliffspring Falls for rare fungi. In Auberdine, the night elf prepares a specialized potion and asks you to investigate troubling warnings from the Grove of the Ancients. Barithras Moonshade needs scaber stalks and a death cap for a potent mixture. Both grow in a damp cavern hidden behind Cliffspring Falls in northeastern Darkshore. Gathering these fungi is more dangerous than picking ordinary woodland herbs.

quest:948.text: Onu. Barithras Moonshade sends you south from Auberdine to speak with Onu. Your findings in Cliffspring Falls have drawn the attention of one of Darkshore's oldest guardians. Barithras Moonshade sees more than strange fungi in the samples you brought back to Auberdine. The caves beneath Cliffspring Falls are tainted, and word of them reaches Onu, an Ancient of Lore in the Grove of the Ancients south of town. The corruption in Darkshore's waterways may reach beyond anything a naturalist can explain. Onu wants counsel, and even an Ancient's patient nature cannot hide the weight of that summons. The road south from Auberdine turns inland, away from the coastal ruins and toward the mountain slopes. The Grove of the Ancients shelters an old refuge of nature, set apart from the decay along the shore. Onu waits among stone barrows and kindred spirits, ready to guide allies toward the blights stirring at the edge of the wilderness.

quest:949.text: The Twilight Camp. Cultists gather around the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore, and Alliance scouts seek to learn why. A scrying bowl has shown their ritual site; now you enter the excavation to discover what the Twilight's Hammer seeks beneath the earth. The Twilight's Hammer has made the Master's Glaive an active threat. After a scrying bowl reveals the cultists' fortifications, you enter their camp to learn their designs before the Alliance can prepare its defenses.

quest:950.text: Return to Onu. You carry a page from the Twilight Tome back to Onu in Darkshore. The scribbles are all you could bear to take from the cultists’ book. The Twilight Tome overwhelms anyone who tries to read it. Its words swim across the page, and its ornate scrollwork twists into grotesque figures. You tear out a single page of scribbles before the strain brings on vertigo.

quest:95065.text: Fishin' Time. At Stormwind harbor, Gilbert Gray's bait runs low as the fish begin to bite. He asks passersby to fetch supplies from a shop along the city's canals. Gilbert Gray spends quiet days fishing at the edge of Stormwind harbor. He watches his bobber on the water, but a good run of biting fish can empty his bait tin. With his supplies gone and the fish still biting, the elderly angler asks passersby to bring him more. Catherine Leland runs a tackle shop along the stone canals, just west of the Trade District. She supplies fishermen across Stormwind with lures and bait, including regulars like Gilbert Gray.

quest:952.text: Grove of the Ancients. A dispatch carries you from Darnassus to Darkshore, where Onu waits in the Grove of the Ancients. Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm sends you across the sea with correspondence for the Ancient of Lore, who lives south of Auberdine. After you help with matters at the Oracle Glade atop Teldrassil, Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm summons you for another duty. He sends you across the sea to Darkshore with an urgent dispatch for Onu. From Darnassus, you can book a flight aboard a hippogryph. South of Auberdine, you reach the Grove of the Ancients and deliver the missive to Onu. The towering Ancient of Lore accepts it quietly and remarks on Staghelm's impatience. Onu and the forest's ancient keepers believe all things unfold in their proper time. Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage embodied that patient wisdom, while Staghelm lacks it.

quest:953.text: The Fall of Ameth'Aran. Sentinel Tysha Moonblade sends you to explore Ameth'Aran's ruins in Darkshore and read its ancient stone tablets. Their inscriptions tell of the Highborne city's ruin during the Sundering, preserving history largely lost in the War of the Ancients for the Circle of Ancients in Auberdine. Ameth'Aran was a flourishing settlement of Queen Azshara's elite sorcerers, who practiced powerful arcane magic. After the Well of Eternity was destroyed ten thousand years ago, the city lay in broken marble and cracked pillars. Restless, anguished spirits of the Highborne who died there still haunt the ruins. Few written accounts survived the Great Sundering intact, as the War of the Ancients drove night elves into a struggle for survival. Sentinel Tysha Moonblade surveyed the ruins and found two large engraved tablets, the Lay of Ameth'Aran and the Fall of Ameth'Aran. Ghostly Highborne specters forced her to retreat. The readings can carry the ancient disaster's history to the scholars of the Circle of Ancients in Auberdine.

quest:954.text: Bashal'Aran. Demonic satyrs and grells shun one shrine in Bashal'Aran, where an unearthly blue aura burns. Thundris Windweaver, Auberdine's elder, sends you to find its source. Bashal'Aran once flourished under the ancient Kaldorei Empire. Now demonic taint fills its broken marble halls and overgrown arches. Twisted satyrs and corrupt grells feed on the ruins' lingering magic, growing more malicious by the day. Yet Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine has noticed a mystery: atop a western bluff, a blue aura shines above a shrine that no demon will approach.

quest:955.text: Bashal'Aran. At Bashal'Aran, Asterion seeks release from the magic binding his ghostly form. He suspects the grells have touched the seal that holds him, and asks travelers to gather their earrings so he can trace its lingering magic. Asterion waits among Bashal'Aran's shattered marble, bound there for centuries. The ancient night elf spirit is trapped between life and true death beneath Darkshore's canopy. Arcane craft ties him to the ruined settlement, and he cannot break free alone. Solitude and despair have worn down his mind through all those years. Asterion believes an ancient seal hidden in the ruins may hold the key to his release. Though he cannot search the brush and fallen stones himself, the feral grells of Bashal'Aran forage there and steal small baubles. He asks travelers to gather their earrings, hoping the trinkets' lingering magic will lead him to the seal that torments his soul.

quest:956.text: Bashal'Aran. Asterion seeks release from his prison among the ruined pillars of Bashal'Aran. He has traced the binding magic to the satyrs who command the grells and asks travelers to recover the Ancient Moonstone Seal. For more than a thousand years, Asterion has remained bound to the ruins of Bashal'Aran. The marble pillars around him mark the limits of his prison, beyond the reach of his fading strength and ancient magic. A cursed relic holds him here. Through the centuries, he has watched Darkshore's canopy and wondered whether the wearing stone could ever set him free. Nearby grells carried traces of the magic that binds Asterion, and he deduced that the Ancient Moonstone Seal was the source of the enchantment. The satyrs who command the grells now hold the seal. These demonic night elves wander the ancient groves, keeping watch over the relic. Asterion needs the seal recovered before its binding power can be broken.

quest:960.text: Onu is meditating. At the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore, Onu enters a deep trance over a growing threat. The ancient of lore weighs the alliance and motives of the Twilight's Hammer cult and the naga. If you lose your scrying phial, you can speak to him for another. In the Grove of the Ancients, Onu is an Ancient of Lore and a living repository of Kalimdor's history. Ominous reports of dark excavations at the Master's Glaive draw his immense consciousness inward. He ponders what brings the fanatical Twilight's Hammer cultists and the naga to the petrified remains of an ancient behemoth. For adventurers carrying out his reconnaissance, Onu remains within reach and can replace a scrying phial misplaced in the wild. Onu uses nature-attuned divination to watch the ruins without risking his physical presence. He entrusts adventurers with a phial of scrying, which conjures a scrying bowl at the excavation site so he can commune from afar. The journey south through Darkshore is perilous, with hostile wildlife and cultist patrols, so mishaps can happen. Onu's trance is an attentive vigil, not unbroken slumber. He readily offers another vial of sacred waters so the investigation of the Master's Glaive can continue.

quest:963.text: For Love Eternal. In Auberdine, Cerellean Whiteclaw asks you to free Anaya Dawnrunner's spirit from torment in Ameth'Aran. His grief has endured since the city's fall. Ten thousand years ago, the War of the Ancients tore ancient Kalimdor apart around the Well of Eternity. The catastrophe destroyed Ameth'Aran and took Anaya Dawnrunner from Cerellean Whiteclaw. Stricken with grief, Cerellean followed Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage into the druids' long hibernation. He hoped that walking the Emerald Dream through the ages would quiet his aching heart, but sorrow remained with him. After awakening, Cerellean wandered Darkshore in a stupor until he reached Ameth'Aran's melancholy ruins. Among the ancient stones, he saw Anaya's tortured ghost. He cannot raise a weapon against the woman he loved, so he asks passing travelers to destroy her tormented form, retrieve her pendant, and grant her troubled soul peace.

quest:965.text: The Tower of Althalaxx. North of Auberdine, Sentinel Elissa Starbreeze fears trouble at an ancient ruin. She sent Balthule Shadowstrike to watch the Tower of Althalaxx, but he has missed his report. Sentinel Elissa Starbreeze watches for danger around Auberdine. Suspicious activity near the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore drew her notice, so she sent Balthule Shadowstrike to watch the ancient ruin. Days have passed without word from him. Elissa asks you to travel north, find Balthule, and make sure he has not met an untimely end.

quest:966.text: The Tower of Althalaxx. Warlocks gather at the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore, drawing the scout Balthule Shadowstrike’s attention. He asks travelers to recover parchment scraps from the fanatics camped outside the ruins, hoping to learn who they are and what they seek. Balthule Shadowstrike watches the misty shore of northern Darkshore, keeping sight of the ancient Tower of Althalaxx. Auberdine sent him to monitor the ruin and warn Delgren the Purifier if danger grew. But leaving his post to report might mean missing the dark spellcasters moving among the stones. So Balthule asks passing travelers to scout the camps around the tower.

quest:96607.text: The Great Outdoors. You learn how rest and preparation help you survive beyond city walls. Travelers across Azeroth teach new wanderers to rest by a campfire and prepare for the wilds. Even a sharp blade or potent magic cannot protect you from the wilds if you neglect the basics of survival. Seasoned wanderers near roadside clearings share this lesson with travelers leaving their home valleys. Resting by a campfire eases sore boots, settles the mind, and readies you for the road ahead. Regular rest and preparation give you a better chance of surviving long enough to find fortune and glory. Once you understand the value of a fire and proper rest, your instructors point you toward town tradesfolk. A field camp needs more than an ember and a bedroll; survival also calls for practical crafts. You can forge replacement rivets, cook trail rations, or stitch torn gear under the stars. Each profession offers camp fixtures that can help turn a bare hillside into a self-sufficient outpost.

quest:96627.text: The Adventurer. In Northshire Valley, Marshal McBride sends The Adventurer toward Goldshire to find Sam Sarsaparilla. You have shown your skill defending the abbey, and McBride wants you to look into the newcomer. As threats from the local Defias and vermin ease, Marshal McBride turns his attention to the road beyond Northshire Valley. Stormwind's regular forces are stretched thin across the kingdom, so the local garrison relies on promising fighters to watch travelers and wanderers in the surrounding woods. Marshal McBride asks you to check on Sam Sarsaparilla, a newcomer spotted near Goldshire. It is an unusual request, not a military order or a bounty hunt, and it leads you from Northshire's secluded valley into the wider wilds of Elwynn Forest.

quest:96630.text: The Adventurer. In Teldrassil, a lost journal waits to be carried to Lyreena Duskblade near Dolanaar. Its pages record an unknown traveler's simple journeys and camping outings. You find a journal among Teldrassil's boughs and roots. Its nameless writer records modest wanderings and the simple pleasure of making camp beneath the twilight canopy. The journal can be carried toward Dolanaar instead of left in the wilderness. Lyreena Duskblade waits near the night elf settlement to receive the lost pages.

quest:96652.text: The Adventurer. In Durotar, The Adventurer finds a lost journal among the red wastes. Its pages tell of quiet travels and nights beneath the stars, and it is meant for Brakk near Razor Hill. A lost journal lies in Durotar's red dirt, far from the bloody battles and grand campaigns that mark the land. Its unknown writer fills the pages with day-to-day travels and the simple pleasure of making camp beneath the open sky. The book offers a quiet glimpse of life on the road through a harsh country. The journal is meant for Brakk, an adventurer camped near Razor Hill. Its pages connect an unknown traveler to someone watching the dusty roads, and carrying it to Brakk may help keep the writer's travels remembered.

quest:96658.text: Camping 101: Cooking. At nearby settlements, new adventurers learn to cook and kindle a Basic Campfire for life in the wild. The lesson is offered across Alliance and Horde lands. Every traveler needs to know how to build a fire beyond the safety of fortified walls. A campfire can boil water and roast meat, and it anchors a campsite in unfamiliar country. Apprentice cooks can kindle only modest fires with few surroundings. Greater skill in cooking lets them light larger fires that support more elaborate campsites. Other practical trades also teach ways to make useful furnishings for a camp.

quest:967.text: The Tower of Althalaxx. At the Tower of Althalaxx, Dark Strand cultists are gathering, and Balthule Shadowstrike needs help. He sends an Alliance courier to Maestra's Post in Ashenvale with a warning for his mentor, Delgren the Purifier. Balthule Shadowstrike sees that the Dark Strand threat is too great for one scout to face alone. After clashing with cultists near the Tower of Althalaxx, he writes a report and entrusts it to an Alliance messenger bound for his master, Delgren the Purifier. The cult's summoners are growing bolder, and Balthule needs seasoned leaders to direct a response. Balthule's dispatch takes you south along Darkshore's coastal road, then across the wooded border into Ashenvale. Delgren the Purifier is stationed at Maestra's Post, beside the western road. The human paladin works to cleanse demons and undead from the woodland. Though night elven customs were once unfamiliar to him, he has earned the Sentinels' deep respect as an indispensable ally.

quest:968.text: Tools of the Highborne. Thundris Windweaver sends help from Auberdine to the ruins of Ameth'Aran. Restless Highborne spirits still carry enchanted relics through the shattered settlement, and he wants them taken away. South of Auberdine and east of the coastal highway, Ameth'Aran's stone foundations lie overgrown. Ten thousand years ago, the settlement was a stronghold of the Highborne, the privileged aristocracy of the ancient night elven empire. Their unchecked use of arcane magic helped bring about the Sundering, which shattered Ameth'Aran. The inhabitants never truly left. Sentinels patrolling Darkshore report that the Highborne ghosts still haunt the sunken plazas, clutching the enchanted tools and trinkets they held in life. For the kaldorei, arcane magic carries the memory of a danger that nearly destroyed life on Azeroth. Thundris Windweaver fears that leaving the Highborne implements in ghostly hands could invite corruption. He sends adventurers to wrest the relics from the restless spirits, intending to have them destroyed so their tainted magic cannot fuel another disaster.

quest:97279.text: Wayward Weapons. At the Valley of Trials, Gornek sends new recruits to recover weapons for the encampment. With young warriors arriving to serve the Horde, supplies run thin, and the weaponsmith needs old arms returned to use. New recruits face harsh trials in Durotar's red wastes. Many arrive ready to pledge their blades to the warchief, straining the encampment's weapon stocks. Weaponsmith Kzan Thornslash struggles to meet demand, especially when early lessons prove fatal or humiliating for the unready. Overseer Gornek makes the shortage a practical trial. He sends fresh arrivals to recover abandoned blades and blunt training weapons left by recruits who fell or fled. Bring the recovered arms to Kzan, and he can repair and temper them for the next wave. New recruits learn that survival in the Horde calls for scavenging as well as swinging steel.

quest:97894.text: Business in Auberdine. Borgus Steelhand seeks news of his brother Gorbold in Auberdine. The dwarven merchant asks travelers sailing west to check on Gorbold, who recently began trading in the night elven port. Their route links Stormwind Harbor with the shores of northern Kalimdor. Borgus Steelhand trusts his family's name among traders. His brother, Gorbold Steelhand, crossed the Great Sea recently to work a merchant stall in Auberdine. Gorbold hoped to profit by supplying ships that call at Darkshore. Weeks have passed without a word, and Borgus worries about how his brother fares so far from Ironforge and Stormwind. Travel from the Eastern Kingdoms to Kalimdor once meant a winding passage through Menethil Harbor or neutral goblin ports such as Booty Bay. Borgus directs travelers to a vessel at the southern-most dock of Stormwind Harbor. It sails directly to Auberdine's long wooden piers.

quest:97914.text: Expanding Horizons. Thundris Windweaver sends word from Auberdine across the Great Sea to Stormwind. The letter asks City Architect Baros Alexston to recognize Auberdine's work and its home. Auberdine now links Darkshore to Stormwind by sea. Night elves once kept to Kalimdor's forests, apart from the Eastern Kingdoms, but after the Third War they joined the Grand Alliance. The new passage gives the northern port a direct tie to the human kingdom. Local leaders want the shipping route secured and Auberdine connected to the wider Alliance. Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran, ruined cities nearby, have long drawn more notice than the living coastal settlement. The letter crossing the Great Sea is addressed to Baros Alexston, Stormwind's City Architect. He oversees construction and infrastructure in the human capital, including public works and logistics. Thundris Windweaver wants Auberdine's work recognized and its home made known.

quest:97919.text: Camping 101: First Aid. At the Lion's Pride Inn, Michelle Belle shows travelers how to prepare for camp. In Goldshire, you can learn to make a First Aid Kit for the road ahead. Travel across Elwynn Forest can leave you wounded, far from a town healer or inn. First Aid lets you tend your own injuries and care for yourself without relying on others. Bandages offer help with bleeding and trauma, without arcane rituals or holy supplication. A campsite offers a place to rest amid the dangers of the wild. At the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, Michelle Belle teaches skilled practitioners to assemble First Aid Kits. Keep medical supplies at camp so a weary party can treat injuries and regain strength before facing the perils ahead.

quest:97920.text: Camping 101: Fishing. In Elwynn Forest, novice anglers seek ways to make camp life more comfortable. Near Goldshire, fishing expert Lee Brown teaches travelers how angling can add simple comforts to a campsite. Fishing gives you food, but camp life asks for more than food and shelter. A fish bowl can bring comfort and lift the spirits of weary travelers between excursions. Sound minds and high spirits help make formidable fighters. Lee Brown waits beside the waters outside Goldshire to help novice fishermen broaden their craft. Travelers who show skill with rod and line can learn how simple catches and basic materials become useful additions to a campsite.

quest:982.text: Deep Ocean, Vast Sea. North of Auberdine, the Silver Dawning and Mist Veil lie beneath the waves. Murlocs ambushed both night elf vessels as they sailed into port, and their surviving crews seek a way to mourn their lost captains. Murlocs overwhelmed the Silver Dawning and Mist Veil as the ships approached Auberdine. Both vessels sank in the shallows north of the settlement. Their surviving crews reached shore, but the loss of the ships and their captains weighs on the port. Gorbold Steelhand, a dwarf in Auberdine, seeks to honor the fallen night elf captains. Murlocs now occupy the underwater wrecks, but the captains' lockboxes remain in the flooded holds. Their logs and personal effects could help the surviving sailors mourn their commanders and lay their spirits to rest.

quest:98247.text: Shipping Label. The Shipping Label is a recovered freight marker attached to a supply crate owned by the Azeroth Commerce Authority. Directing couriers to their trade hub at the Three Corners crossroads in Redridge Mountains, it introduces travelers to the organization's network of independent haulers. Found pasted to a stocked supply crate, this damaged shipping label marks cargo belonging to the Azeroth Commerce Authority. Although the intended destination and recipient have been torn away, clear instructions direct anyone who discovers the freight to return it or report to the authority's trade outpost in the Redridge Mountains. Beside the formal text, a rudimentary map sketches out the roads leading toward the Three Corners intersection. At the crossroads of Three Corners, representatives of the Azeroth Commerce Authority actively enlist travelers as independent couriers. Rather than binding haulers to strict merchant contracts, the authority operates an informal network where adventurers are compensated with Merchant's Favor in return for recovering missing cargo and fulfilling abandoned deliveries along the highway.

quest:983.text: Buzzbox 827. Along Darkshore's coast, Buzzbox 827 waits silent for repairs. Wizbang Cranktoggle built it as the first of a chain of voice relays, each made to use parts from local wildlife. Restoring it lets Wizbang test his network from Auberdine. In Auberdine, gnomish engineer Wizbang Cranktoggle is trying to bridge Darkshore's wild coast with a chain of voice relays called Buzzboxes. Their levers and gears carry speech across great distances, a sharp contrast with the ancient ruins and somber forests around them. The machines break down often, and each needs constant care to keep working. Buzzbox 827 lies on the misty shore just south of Auberdine. Wizbang built each relay to use parts from nearby wildlife, so repairs do not depend on carrying refined iron gears and copper pins through the wilderness. This unit takes the sturdy, jointed legs of local tide and reef crawlers. Put the legs in its receiver hopper, and the machine assembles itself and carries Wizbang's voice through its speakers.

quest:984.text: How Big a Threat?. Terenthis asks scouts in Auberdine to learn whether furbolg corruption has reached Darkshore. After madness takes hold among furbolgs in Teldrassil, the night elf druid sends them to inspect mainland settlements across the sea. Night elves across northern Kalimdor have long lived peacefully with the furbolg tribes. Since the Third War, strange corruption has unhinged furbolg minds in Teldrassil. They have kidnapped and attacked their former allies. Terenthis, a druid stationed in Auberdine, fears the affliction has spread beyond the World Tree to the mainland tribes along Darkshore’s coast.

quest:985.text: How Big a Threat?. Terenthis in Auberdine sends you against the Blackwood furbolgs south of town. Their corrupted camp threatens the settlement, and the Sentinels want its pathfinders and windtalkers culled. The Sentinels see the Blackwood furbolgs as an immediate danger to Darkshore’s refugees and defenders. After you scout south of Auberdine, Terenthis sends you to strike their camp. Killing Blackwood Pathfinders and Windtalkers may break their attack before it reaches the settlement. Night elves have long regarded furbolgs as spiritual kin and allies of the wilderness. Fel moss and demonic taint have spread across northern Kalimdor, driving the Blackwood tribe mad. No known remedy can restore their minds, so Auberdine’s defenders see a grim choice: stop them before innocent people die.

quest:98576.text: Glyphic Parchment. In the Valley of Trials, Glyphic Parchment points young mages toward their first lessons. Gornek delivers the runed notice, which sends them to Mai'ah near the Den to begin learning the arcane. New recruits test their strength against Durotar's local pests, but those drawn to magic need more than brute force. Gornek passes along a notice marked with runes. It directs novice spellcasters to Mai'ah, who guides the Horde's newest recruits through their first lessons in magic. Mai'ah waits just outside the Den, where she teaches young spellweavers to temper ambition with patience and thought. She urges them to choose their moment instead of hurling raw sorcery without care. In her lessons, novices learn to weave delicate strands of the cosmos rather than unleash an unruly tempest.

quest:997.text: Denalan's Earth. In Dolanaar, Syral Bladeleaf sends a late shipment of rare earth south to Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth. The night elf researcher studies Teldrassil's young plants. Syral Bladeleaf stops travelers in Dolanaar with a special shipment of rare earth for Denalan. The soil came from Darnassus to support his botanical studies, but delays kept it from reaching Dolanaar until now. Syral seeks a courier to carry the parcel south along the forest trail to Denalan's campsite by Lake Al'Ameth. Denalan works alone at a station on Lake Al'Ameth's eastern shore, watching Teldrassil's young ecosystem take root. The tree grew quickly after the Battle of Mount Hyjal, and its plants behave in unexpected ways. Denalan tests the vitality and behavior of timberlings and native plants with unique soil mixtures and specimens. The rare earth shipment will support those experiments.

quest:cutting-teeth.text: Cutting Teeth. In the Valley of Trials, fresh recruits face a first test against mottled boars. Overseer Gornek sends aspiring warriors and spellcasters to thin the boars around the cactus dirt farms, where they can prove their fighting skill and readiness to serve the Horde. The Valley of Trials leaves little room for grand dreams. Young recruits may imagine hunting great beasts in the Barrens or winning glory on a battlefield, but overseer Gornek begins with the farms. Thinning the mottled boars is a grounded test of a recruit’s first skills with a weapon or spell. It shows whether they can face a wild attacker and have the sense to survive their first skirmish. Feral swine roam the red desert settlement’s dirt farms north and northeast of camp. They root through cactus patches and threaten the few supplies grown in Durotar’s harsh soil. Sending aspirants to clear them keeps local pests in check while shaping young orcs and trolls into defenders of the new nation.

quest:galgar-s-cactus-apple-surprise.text: Galgar's Cactus Apple Surprise. In the Valley of Trials, Galgar sends fresh recruits to gather cactus apples for his cooling treat. The work teaches them to forage and survive in Durotar's arid land. Young orcs and Darkspear trolls take their first steps as defenders of the Horde in the Valley of Trials. Combat drills and fierce trials against native beasts quickly bring exhaustion and thirst. Learning to live off the land matters as much as learning to swing an axe. Cacti across the valley bear ripe, water-rich apples that offer relief from the desert sun. Galgar tends his cooking in the training grounds, where he has made an art of foraging. His Cactus Apple Surprise is known among the valley's people for cooling a person faster than a plunge into river water. He sends eager recruits to gather prickly fruit from nearby cacti, keeping his kitchen stocked and ensuring new wanderers do not set out into Durotar hungry.

quest:lazy-peons.text: Lazy Peons. Foreman Thazz'ril sends new Horde recruits across the Valley of Trials to wake sleeping peons. Their work keeps lumber moving to Durotar's settlements. Durotar's new homes need timber, stone, and hard labor. Peons, orcs with little skill in battle, carry much of that burden and keep the Horde supplied with workers. In the Valley of Trials, the heat and grueling work leave Foreman Thazz'ril's crews seeking shade beneath trees for unauthorized naps. Foreman Thazz'ril gives new Horde recruits his blackjack and sends them across the valley to wake the sleeping workers. The startled peons return to chopping wood, keeping lumber flowing for Durotar's survival.

quest:sarkoth.text: Sarkoth. On a southern plateau in the Valley of Trials, Sarkoth has left a young Darkspear hunter near death. Wounded beneath a tree, Hana'zua asks a passing warrior to kill the scorpid and bring back its mangled claw, so his last strike will count for something. In the Valley of Trials, the Horde tests aspiring warriors against Durotar's harsh desert. While hunting the valley's venomous creatures, young troll scout Hana'zua met a scorpid far larger and deadlier than the rest. He struck hard enough to mangle one pincer, but Sarkoth drove its tail into his chest. Now Hana'zua bleeds in the red dirt, fearing his life is near its end. He wants the beast dead before it can outlive him. Sarkoth roams a high mesa above the southern Valley of Trials. Hana'zua's blow left one claw shattered, but the scorpid still rules the ridge and attacks anyone who climbs the rocky path. Bring the scarred claw back to the wounded scout, and he will have proof that his last strike weakened the monster enough for someone to bring it down.

quest:your-place-in-the-world.text: Your Place In The World. In the Valley of Trials, untested recruits take their first steps toward honor and survival in Durotar. Kaltunk sends them straight to Gornek for basic combat training, beginning their service to the Horde. In Durotar's arid Valley of Trials, young orcs and Darkspear trolls prove their worth before entering the wider world. Under Warchief Thrall, life demands strength, vigilance, and discipline. Kaltunk evaluates every eager recruit, tempering dreams of wrestling demons and dragons with the practical duties ahead. Training begins in the canyon, where recruits learn humility before claiming glory. Gornek waits beside the camp fire, only steps away from Kaltunk. The gruff veteran regards fresh arrivals with a skeptical eye and often grumbles about the meager stock reaching camp. His duty is to harden these young fighters through trials, starting with the vermin that threaten the encampment's supplies.
